The artist will have full access to the common areas such as kitchen, central patio, laundry room etc. There are two bathrooms, residents can use: one full bathroom and another partial (no shower or bathtub). The arts residency is on the border between two old and very popular neighborhoods of Guadalajara, Colonia Moderna and Colonia Americana. Colonia Americana was named the coolest neighborhood in the world by a famous international magazine, in 2023.

name: Rondo Residency
description: Rondo Residency is proud to be an integral part of a larger strategic alliance alongside Plomo Gallery, Galeria Union, Clavo Art Fair, and El Paint Lab. Together, they form a dynamic network committed to fostering artistic growth, promoting cultural exchange, and shaping the future of the contemporary art scene of Mexico. Through collaborative efforts and shared vision, they aim to provide emerging and established artists with opportunities for professional development. RONDO is an international artist residency organization established in 2024 in Mexico City. The residency program is centered around production and connection to the local contemporary scene through their strategic partners. In the heart of Mexico City's bustling art scene lies RONDO Residency Program. The program is uniquely structured around four essential axes—Production, Theoretical, Art Market, and Public Relations—each offering a distinct lens through which artists can deepen their practice and engage with the vibrant cultural landscape of the city. At RONDO, they offer two distinct residency options tailored to the diverse needs of artists. The Live-Work modality provides artists with the opportunity to fully immerse themselves in the creative environment by residing on-site while actively engaging in their projects. Alternatively, the Only-Work option affords artists the same enriching programming while allowing them to arrange accommodation independently.
studioInfo: 6 Studios private studios of 9 m2, one shared communal working space of 120 m2.
accommodationInfo: Private room with single bed, shared bathroom, and shared amenities. They host 6 artists at the same time in the program but only 4 artists reside on site while the other 2 reside elsewhere in the city.

name: COBERTIZO A.C.
description: Cobertizo Art Residency is a non-profit association aimed at international artists willing to develop their creative processes in a professional environment and build a community of exchange and reflection around their art practices. The program, designed to provide a space for immersion and exchange focused on art production, is four weeks long in which the residents will be provided with all services needed (specialized studios, hosting, transport and meals) in order to fully engage with their projects. On the first weekend a trip to Mexico City is programmed for residents to approach diverse independent art spaces and galleries and get to know some of the initiatives that are shaping Mexico city’s art scene. In the second and fourth weeks, two professional artists will visit Cobertizo in order to guide critical mentorships with the residents and open a common dialogue along the residency.
studioInfo: A semi-individual studio fully equipped with a big working table, a support table with racks and wheels, a bookshelf, a mobile work chair and wooden walls where things can be hanged. The studios share two bathrooms.
accommodationInfo: Eight individual rooms with full bathrooms each. Individual working space with wifi and 24/7 access. Maximum eight residents at a time. The artists may work collaboratively at the residency but the facilities and payments are individual. Partners or families cannot be hosted the whole time of the residency.
technicalInfo: a library with a small but growing archive of art books big common living room kitchen and dinning room basic material for visual artists to make their own canvases general artifacts like drill, stapler, hammer, tacks, etc...

name: Casa Snowapple Mx
description: Casa Snowapple Mx opened its doors in 2021 to offer national and international artists the necessary time and space away from their usual obligations to research, develop, produce and share new creative and cultural work. Casa Snowapple Mx is created and run by women. They are an inclusive house where everybody is equal and where they offer the opportunity to expand the national and international community of artists, creatives, musicians and the public through intimate gatherings such as concerts, conferences, artistic residencies, well being activities, dance and more. All women dedicated to art, academia, activism, cultural and technological development are called to apply in a residency with them. They are keen to receive both emerging and experienced artists, but it is substantial that all applicants show a deep commitment to the artistic work and innovative research topics.
studioInfo: Casa Snowapple has: 1 new music/recording studio 1 studio tailored for workshops (multidisciplinary)
accommodationInfo: Casa Snowapple has: 5 individual rooms and 1 shared room 1 music studio 1 studio tailored for workshops (multidisciplinary) 1 multipurpose room 1 kitchen 1 big garden 1 backyard with a terrace 1 beautiful dinning room 1 small parking space (for 5 cars approx) 1 laundry space They are located at the end of an alley in one of the streets of Coyoacán. The space seems to be an oasis in the middle of the crowded Mexico City.
technicalInfo: They offer logistical support. Free internet. Bicycles. Printer and stationery items. Kitchen utensils. A laundry room. Cleaning service once a week.

name: Casa Lü
description: "In Tibetan, the word for body is 'lü', which means 'something you leave behind,' like baggage. Each time we say 'lü', it reminds us that we are only travelers, taking temporary refuge in this life and this body." Sogyal Rinpoche ​Casa Lü is also a place where you can take temporary refuge to concentrate on your artistic practice. The aim of the program is for residents to focus on the production of their work while creating a network and dialogue within emerging artists from all over the world. The participants live and work in Casa Lü. While working on their personal projects they are encouraged to visit Mexico City's dynamic art scene. The organisers provide a calendar with openings and other artistic events, as well as a list of recommendations for museums, galleries and other local attractions.
studioInfo: 2 studios, a private one and a shared one for 4 residents.
accommodationInfo: They have 5 bedrooms, each one with an ensuite bathroom.

name: Moniker Art Foundation
description: Established in 2020 The Moniker Foundation was created to celebrate the world of Urban and New Contemporary art. The foundation works to build the reputation of Urban and New Contemporary art with the public and to support artists. It does this through public displays of art, the commission of original artworks, sculpture and installations and the creation of educational programmes and links. The foundation further acts to document and preserve the origins and history of Urban and New Contemporary art to build understanding and appreciation.​ Build a collection that documents Urban and New Contemporary art Create a public showcase for the breadth of Urban and New Contemporary art Help to support and develop the artists, careers and creative practices Develop educational resources for artists, curators and art collectors Establish dialogue with our network of leading figures within Urban and New Contemporary art Document the growth and development of Urban, Street, Graffiti and New Contemporary art Create a platform for the Moniker Collection to be loved, admired and engaged with Over the coming years, the Moniker Foundation will continue to build on a 10 year legacy of Moniker Art Fair to support and encourage the growth of the contemporary art market, being a leading supporter to the artists, galleries and curators that have helped develop the subculture. The Moniker Foundation is proud to announce its inaugural International Artist Residency Program to be held at prestigious locations in Tulum, Mexico, in partnership with Tulum Art Club and in support of LADLE, a Non-profit dedicated to empowering Native Mayan and Mexican children.​​ This residency offers a unique opportunity for 4 artists, 2 international artists and 2 local Mexican artists to immerse themselves in the rich cultural landscape of the Yucatán Peninsula while developing their artistic practice.
studioInfo: Artists will have space to reflect, draw, and collaborate in the beautiful jungle and within a studio space located on the beach in Tulum.
accommodationInfo: Artists will be hosted at their hotel partner on the beach in Tulum, Mexico where there is space to paint, draw and work on site.

name: La Manchoza
description: Ana Paula Luna is a Mexican sculptor with an established professional practice spanning sculpture, ceramics, and material-based experimentation. Her work has been exhibited internationally and is rooted in a deep engagement with craftsmanship, landscape, and the transformative potential of materials. Alongside her artistic practice, she has developed studios, workshops, and creative spaces that support artistic production and research. Juan Lanzagorta is a programmer, designer, and builder with a background in technology, entrepreneurship, and project development. He has led the design and construction of much of La Manchoza's infrastructure, combining technical expertise with a strong interest in sustainable living, architecture, and creative problem-solving. Together, they founded La Manchoza as an artist-run residency where art, nature, architecture, and self-directed creative practice converge in the mountains of Jalisco, Mexico. La Manchoza is an independent, artist-run organization dedicated to supporting self-directed artistic practice through residency programs, creative infrastructure, and engagement with place. Located in the mountains near Tapalpa, Jalisco, Mexico, the project brings together art, architecture, sustainable living, and material experimentation within a rural environment. Founded by sculptor Ana Paula Luna and programmer and builder Juan Lanzagorta, La Manchoza operates as a small-scale, hands-on initiative where artists are encouraged to develop their work with autonomy, focus, and access to adaptable creative spaces. The organization supports a range of disciplines, including sculpture, ceramics, painting, writing, and interdisciplinary practices. Rooted in principles of curiosity, craftsmanship, sustainability, and creative freedom, La Manchoza seeks to foster meaningful artistic development while remaining closely connected to the landscape, local knowledge, and the evolving process of making.
studioInfo: The residency provides a range of adaptable studio and workshop spaces 1. A covered outdoor woodworking area is available for sculpture, woodwork, and experimental construction processes. The space is suitable for tools and material-intensive work, including chainsaw sculpture and large-scale fabrication. 2. The residency includes a dedicated ceramic workspace and a high-temperature gas kiln, allows for firing of ceramic works on-site. Raw materials are available for glaze development. 3. Painting can be carried out in multiple locations. Easels and diverse lighting are available. 4.The residency includes interior and exterior areas suitable for writing and research. 5. Bronze casting is not conducted on-site but is available through collaboration with a professional foundry and local artisans in Tapalpa.
accommodationInfo: Residents are provided with a fully private, self-contained two-story house located on the property, approximately 30 meters from the founders’ residence, ensuring both privacy and proximity to support when needed. The house measures 4 x 11 meters per floor, with a total interior area of 88 m² (947 ft²), and includes a private garden area adjacent to the building. The accommodation is fully equipped for long-term stays and includes a kitchen, private bathroom, living and dining areas, bedroom, terrace, and flexible studio spaces that can be adapted for different creative practices. Furniture is movable to accommodate individual working needs. Amenities include Starlink internet, electricity, gas, water, and weekly cleaning service. The house is designed as an off-grid smart home incorporating rainwater harvesting, reclaimed materials, and bioconstruction elements. The accommodation is intended to function both as a living space and an integrated working environment for artists during their residency.
technicalInfo: La Manchoza is a self-directed, off-grid residency designed to support long-term artistic production in a rural environment while maintaining essential modern infrastructure. The property operates with on-site utilities including electricity and a rainwater harvesting system. Water is managed sustainably as part of the off-grid infrastructure. High-speed Starlink internet is available throughout the residency house and selected work areas, supporting research, communication, and digital production. The residency incorporates off-grid and low-impact living systems, including rainwater collection and the use of reclaimed construction materials. The infrastructure is designed to balance comfort with environmental responsibility. Technical facilities include a ceramic kiln, woodworking and sculpture tools, a covered outdoor workshop, and flexible studio spaces. A shipping container is available for storage and additional workspace. Bronze casting is available off-site through collaboration with local artisans and a professional foundry in Tapalpa. The residency is self-directed. Technical assistance is available informally depending on project needs, particularly for material sourcing and coordination with local workshops. Located in the mountains near Tapalpa, Jalisco, the residency is situated in a rural environment approximately 20 km from town, with access to basic services, markets, and transport within a 25–30 minute drive.

name: La Coyotera Taller Estudio
description: La Coyotera Taller are focused on Land Art, Ceramics, Stone Sculptures, Paintings and Drawings. Located in a rural small village high in the mountains at 2250 m with a small lake in front of the studio. They expect nothing else then have a great time creating works of art in a beautiful quiet location here in Mexico.
studioInfo: 4 spaces: inside they have a drawing room and painting studio,outside we have a space for Land Art and stone sculpture and we have a separate ceramic studio with 2 kilns.
accommodationInfo: A cabin that accommodates up to 6 people with a private bathroom and kitchen.
technicalInfo: All the materials needed for ceramics,stone sculpture, land art, painting and for drawing are available or could be provided.

name: Caracollabs
description: Qualia provides dynamic spaces for creating art and academic residency that foster collaboration, wellbeing, and a integrated environment for innovation, sustainability, trust, research, technology, and play.
studioInfo: The art studio & library are specially designed for artists and creatives seeking a space to work and find inspiration. The art studio is situated in the tree canopy, featuring ample natural light, spacious work areas, and art supplies to nurture artistic endeavours. The studios are equipped with comfortable seating, easels, and art materials, creating an ideal setting for artistic exploration. Our kiln for pottery is underway… They hold a library, A large terrace (a multidisciplinary space I.E performance art, projection) and instruments acquired from around the world. The garden it’s self is a living laboratory.
accommodationInfo: A palapa built on the principles of permaculture, with a double bed, en suit bathroom, a large living-dining room including a kitchenette equipped with fridge, stove and sink and a large patio that overlooks the jungle. They can host 4 residents at once. Groups as well as family and kids are welcome.

name: Nomadic Red Corner – International Artist Residency
description: Nomadic Red Corner is a collaborative project between the Mongolian Contemporary Art Support Association and Art Space 976+, dedicated to the development of ger districts of Ulaanbaatar city through the implementation of creative community development and artist residency programs. Today Ger districts are home to nearly 800,000 people, the majority of them are rural-urban migrants and low-income families. Ger districts have very limited access to utilities and infrastructure. Low-quality life in these areas affects community health, caused by pollution and an unpleasant environment, with no street lighting, pedestrian roads, green park and public spaces. Migrants are often stigmatised by native residents and seen as the source of a high level of poverty and urban sprawl. The initiative aims to bring together professional artists, residents, volunteers, and organizations in order to dispel negative assumptions about ger districts and to create a more attractive and friendly environment for its residents and visitors. Since its inception in 2020, Nomadic Red Corner has collaborated with European Union, Goethe Institute, the Ministry of Culture of Mongolia, Alliance Francois, the Embassy of the United States, the Embassy of the Czech Republic, the Sukhbaatar District Government and the Magic Land Community Center, creating artistic neighbourhoods covering around 24.000 sq.m area in Chingeltei, Sukhbaatar and Bayanzurkh districts, where artists created paintings, sculptures and installations. Various public art events, exhibitions and workshops have been organised involving youth living in these areas.
studioInfo: The Nomadic Red Corner compound has one extra Ger next to the residential dwelling, which shall be used for storing various supplies and materials and for a public meeting. Magic Land 2 Community Center has a library, coffee shop, conference room and classrooms for dance, music and painting. The outdoor area of the courtyard has a playground and basketball court.
accommodationInfo: The residency compound has two Gers. Each Ger has 3 beds, kitchen amenities, sheets, towels, shelves and other necessary supplies for accommodating 6 artists in total. Ger (often called a yurt) is a round-shaped traditional Mongolian housing with a cone-like roof, covered by felt under canvas, which is used for thousands of years as a dwelling by nomads in the steppes of the country. The wooden structure and furniture of Gers are beautifully designed and made by local artists, using contemporary and traditional elements. Artists are allowed to use showers and bathrooms located inside the community centre, which is located within 50 meters. As Gers are not connected to infrastructure, artists need to carry water from the community centre and use them for cooking, washing kitchen stuff, floors etc. Instructions for living will be provided.
technicalInfo: The project will make sure at least one Mongolian artist will be taking part in the residency program, who shall help international artists know the local art scene, meet artists and visit ongoing exhibitions and explore different areas of the city. The project team will also seek possibilities of supporting international artists, if they have special projects in mind, to implement with local artists.

name: Estudio Abierto
description: Estudioabierto is an artistic residence space designed for creative and reflective processes based on the meeting of local and world cultural actors. The study is made up of the collaborative participation of independent galleries, workshops, artists and artisans of the city with the aim of being a circuit where artists who come to Oaxaca can be immersed in the cultural activity of both reflective investigation of the place and the practical.
studioInfo: There is a possibility to collaborate with independent galleries in the historic center, workshops, artists and artisans of the city forming working links between actors of the cultural scene and artists who come to work and investigate local work. In the study-house there are three studies for research.
accommodationInfo: House with kitchen two bathrooms and 3 individual room studios.
technicalInfo: ​The residence has a network of production workshops for artists and craftsmen: Pottery workshop Engraving workshop Digital printing laboratory Textile workshop (wool) Carved in wood Elaboration of objects with reed

name: CASA NAATIK
description: Casa Naatik is an eco arts center located within the jungle of the Yucatan, in Mexico, where you can be in contact with nature. It is half an hour away from the city of Valladolid, the second largest in the state. The residency is neighbored by a small Mayan community of 250 inhabitants, one kilometer away. The residency organisers also offer a house in the city of Valladolid where you can stay if you do not want to sleep in the middle of nature. The residency offers the opportunity to work in areas such as, but not limited to: literature, sculpture, ceramics, visual arts, textiles, film and video, and relational art. There are also introductory workshops on permaculture, textiles, bookbinding, creating artist's books, film and video post-production. The program offers the opportunity to dedicate yourself to the planning and execution of projects.
studioInfo: Library with internet and computers, workshop in a semi-open space with basic tools, outdoor space.
accommodationInfo: The space includes three cabins in the jungle facility with internet, a shared dry toilet system and outdoor showers, orchards, and a community dining room. In the city, there is a house with two bedrooms, two bathrooms, kitchen, living room, internet, terrace with pool.

name: CHIOSC/ KIOSK AIR
description: Oberliht Association aims to grant support to young artists from Moldova by establishing platforms that allow interested artists, curators and cultural workers to initiate and carry out contemporary art projects with young artists’ participation (workshops, exhibitions etc.), thus addressing their needs, but also addressing different issues like public space, community art projects, networking and others, through visual arts but also through other artistic disciplines like literature or architecture. Following the series of projects titled INTERVENTIONS (2006-2008) Oberliht association launched the KIOSK project in 2009. Embodied in FLAT SPACE – a cultural information point and a platform for public participation, it aims to provide continuity to the previously organized activities and offer an alternative within a cultural sector dominated by institutions inherited from the Communist period. Installed on a tiny segment of municipal ground, squeezed in between cars aggressively taking over the sidewalks, FLAT SPACE plays the role of an active agent of bottom-up civic involvement, understanding cultural engagement as social action capable of producing a critical culture. The activities built around it address, in its immediate surroundings, the urgent question of public space. In a broader way the project offers the basis for the analysis of the cultural, social and political realities of one of Europe’s suburbs.
studioInfo: both, the FLAT SPACE ( http://chiosc.oberliht.com/apartament/ ) and the city of Chisinau, as a whole, substituting for the studio, serve as place of research, for producing and exhibiting
accommodationInfo: rented flat

name: Mongolian Contemporary Art Support Association
description: MCASA is a non-governmental organization established with the aim to support and promote contemporary art in Mongolia. The Association implements strategically important projects to improve competitive capacity of Mongolian artists at domestic and international platforms, through involving them in various training, exchange and grant programs, competitions and exhibitions; works to improve public education in art and raises public awareness on social, environmental issues through art. Mongolian Contemporary Art Support Association (MCASA) has launched an international call for the engagement of a curator and an artist for the performance art project NOMAD SPIRIT, to be organized in Mongolia. The project is funded by Swiss Development Agency and MCASA. The NOMAD SPIRIT project aims to raise public awareness on potential threats to vital environmental and cultural resources in rural areas of Mongolia, caused by mining activities. The selected curator and artists will are expected to travel to the environmentally damaged area and collaborate with local nomadic community on concept development. Performance must be held on the site and documented by the selected Mongolian artists. Video and photos of live performances will be exhibited in Ulaanbaatar for a month. Eligibility: Experienced in performance art Fluent English Open to different cultures and people Experience in environmental and social awareness projects is a plus. Swiss artists and curators are encouraged to apply. International artists must arrive in mid of August, 2016 and work for about a month. International travel expenses and accommodation in Mongolia will be covered by the project.
studioInfo: Gallery space with 2 large rooms.
accommodationInfo: 2 bedroom apartment.

name: Café Tissardmine
description: Cafe Tissardmine invites applications from artists of all disciplines for the 2021/2022 residency program. They accept applications from all disciplines. However, their supplies are limited - they run on solar power, so occasionally they are short of electricity and ask that all equipment is only charged in the day time. They have provision to show films (projector and primitive screen) but you need to provide your own computer. Generally they ask artists to bring all their supplies with them as even good quality paper is hard to find locally. Not all practices are practical in that area – for example it is not a place for internet based research. It is a place to recharge and inspire.
studioInfo: Cafe Tissardmine has a new studio! Built to accommodate up to 4 artists with a separate room for exhibiting/meditating/cups of tea and chats.
accommodationInfo: Cafe Tissardmine has a four room guesthouse around a central courtyard and a bivouac of 5 tents. All rooms and tents have ensuite bathrooms. They are powered by Solar energy and bring water from a well in the nearby oasis. Living is basic and run as traditionally as possible; bed linen and pillows will be provided. The weather is, in the main, warm to cool, calm and bright but with occasional sandstorms and even rain. At its most hot during summer (July and August) when the temperatures soar to over 50, Tissardmine is closed
technicalInfo: Not all disciplines are practical in the Sahara – for example it is not a place for internet based research. It is a place to recharge and inspire.

name: Yasmine Laraqui Studio - Residency Program
description: Yasmine Laraqui Studio is an independent creative space based in Casablanca, Morocco, dedicated to visual production, artistic research, and cultural programming. Founded by artist and writer Yasmine Laraqui, the studio functions both as a production space and a platform for experimentation at the intersection of contemporary art, visual media, and emerging cultural practices. The studio develops projects that include photography and video production, curatorial initiatives, exhibitions, and an international artist residency program. Through these activities, the studio aims to support dialogue between local and international artistic communities while encouraging research-driven artistic practices. Located in Casablanca, one of North Africa’s largest and most dynamic cities, the residency invites artists to engage with the cultural, social, and urban environment of the region while developing new work or research. Yasmine Laraqui Studio seeks to provide artists with a supportive environment for experimentation, reflection, and exchange, while contributing to the development of independent cultural initiatives in the city. The Yasmine Laraqui Studio Residency offers artists the opportunity to live and work in Casablanca while developing new ideas and artistic projects in an independent creative environment. The residency is designed as a period of research, experimentation, and cultural immersion. Artists are encouraged to explore the city, engage with its artistic and urban landscape, and use their time to develop new work, research, or conceptual investigations. The program is open to artists working across disciplines, including visual arts, photography, installation, multimedia practices, and research-based approaches. Residents are provided with accommodation and access to a working space. At the end of the residency, artists have the opportunity to present their work, research, or artistic process through an exhibition or public presentation organized by the studio. The residency particularly welcomes artists interested in engaging with contemporary cultural dynamics, urban environments, and evolving relationships between art, technology, and society. Through exhibitions and informal exchanges, the residency aims to foster dialogue between international artists and the local creative community in Casablanca.
studioInfo: Residents have access to several working environments during their stay. The residency apartment includes a shared working area that can be used for research, drawing, writing, and small-scale studio activities. The apartment can accommodate up to two artists at a time, allowing residents to work individually or collaboratively. In addition, residents have access to Yasmine Laraqui Studio, a production space located in the Palmier district of Casablanca. The studio is used for photography, video production, and contemporary art projects, and can accommodate a variety of artistic practices including installation, photography, multimedia work, and research-based projects. A separate gallery space is also available for exhibitions and presentations. At the end of the residency, artists are invited to present their work, research, or artistic process through an exhibition or public presentation organized by the studio. Artists are encouraged to propose projects that can be developed within the available resources of the residency. Studio access: flexible access depending on project needs and scheduling.
accommodationInfo: Residents are provided with accommodation and access to a working space during their stay. The residency apartment is a private space located in the heart of Casablanca’s historic center, in an Art Deco building. The apartment can accommodate up to two artists at a time. Artist partners or collaborators applying together are welcome. The apartment is situated within walking distance of several key areas of the city, including the central park, the historic Medina, and Casablanca’s vibrant nightlife with local cafés, bars, and cultural venues. Public transportation is easily accessible, with the tramway located nearby. The studio and exhibition space are located approximately 15 minutes walking distance from the residency apartment. The residency aims to provide artists with a comfortable and stimulating environment from which to explore the city while developing their work.

name: Nawat Fes
description: Nawat Fes offers funded residencies in the eighth-century medina of Fes, Morocco to U.S. and international creators in multiple disciplines. The initiative engages art to cultivate understanding among multifaceted cultures through the exchange of ideas. Hosted by the American Language Center / Arabic Language Institute in Fez, a member of the American Cultural Association, Nawat Fes is a new program that hosted its first residencies in May 2022. Through the American Language Center and its Arabic Language Institute in Fez (ALC-ALIF), Nawat Fes artists will have access to multilingual staff support and opportunities for engagement with the wider community of Fes. The ALC’s main facility in Fes’ New City includes a large garden with a café, library, and bookstore, where Moroccans and students of Arabic from around the world congregate to share ideas and participate in the ALC’s range of public programs. The ALIF Riad, a spacious traditional house built around a courtyard garden of orange trees, offers additional space in the medina available for exhibitions and public programs. Artist residents will live and work in the ancient medina of Fes, which is considered one of the most extensive and best-conserved historic cities of the Arab-Muslim world. Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Fes medina is one of the world’s largest pedestrian zones, containing narrow alleyways leading to ancient architectural treasures, traditional houses, artisan workshops and open-air markets. Within this unique setting, Nawat Fes provides a supportive environment for research, reflection, and artistic practice, allowing artists from around the world to experience and learn from Moroccan culture, and to contribute to the local cultural conversation. Nawat Fes offers four residency periods each year of roughly two months each. Artists are expected to arrive at the beginning of each residency period and stay through the end of the residency period. Please see the Nawat Fes website for residency periods.
studioInfo: Each artist has a simple, private studio space in Dar Bennis that is separate from their living space. Our current facilities have some limitations for visual artists and artists working in sound. In the future, we will explore partnerships that will enable us to expand access to dedicated studio space for artists working in visual arts, music and sound. •   Limitations of Visual Arts Studios. At present, simple visual arts studios are located in Dar Bennis. Studios do not have any special equipment. Because Dar Bennis is a shared live-work space, artists may not use materials in the studios that will create fumes. •   Limitations of studios for sound-based artists. Because of the shared nature of the live-work space, at the time of our launch we do not have facilities in which sound-based artists can play their work at full volume. Currently, musicians, composers and sound artists are welcome to apply who are able to work within the space productively using their own headphones and equipment in a way that will not disturb the other artist resident in Dar Bennis.
accommodationInfo: Two artists at one time reside and work on separate floors of Dar Bennis, a restored traditional Moroccan house in the old medina, tucked away not far from the main street. Each artist will have a bedroom, a private bath, and a basic studio in the house. The house has wifi, a shared kitchen, a laundry room and a roof terrace with a view of the medina. As the rooms in Dar Bennis all open onto an interior courtyard, perfect quiet in the living and work spaces cannot be assured. There are several great cafes nearby that also make excellent off-site working environments. Artist collaboratives should apply together by submitting ONE application per group, specifying the number of individuals on the application form. Nawat Fes can accommodate no more 3 artists in a collaborative group.

name: Culture Vultures
description: At the foot of the Middle Atlas Mountains in Morocco, Culture Vultures presents AiR Sefrou. Embraced by the community of the semi-rural market town of Sefrou, it is an artist-run residency set up in 2014, a place for Moroccan and international artists and researchers to reside among this community. The residency program is part of the portfolio of Culture Vultures, an artist-led initiative founded in Sefrou some years before. This market town lies 25 kilometers outside of the imperial capital and crafts hub of Morocco, Fez, while it is connected to more traditional ways of living. AiR Sefrou offers a self-governing resident the balance of focused time and space and to immerse oneself in a traditional Moroccan old city (medina). As a market town on the traders route across North Africa, Sefrou has received visitors from far and wide over millennia. As an organization that often facilitates encounters between the local and the international, Culture Vultures is grateful to Sefrou’s community who continually encourage, question and engage us. Located in the vibrant heart of North Africa, AiR Sefrou is surrounded by the rich tapestry of Amazigh, Jewish and Arab traditions, green landscapes, diverse heritage, rich history and a community renowned for its warm hospitality. The residency at the edge of the medina offers a perfect base for sociological research, mappings on multiculturalism or -lingualism, community-driven performances, a writers retreat, and creative and technical collaborations. AiR Sefrou welcomes artists and researchers from diverse disciplines such as visual arts, literature, design, architecture, performing arts, as well as academic and artistic research. Self-directed residencies are scheduled all year long, for a period from 3 weeks to 3 months. Programmed residencies for 2024 and 2025 are as follows: Application Deadline 15/03/24 - Commences 01/06/24 Application Deadline 01/06/24 - Commences 15/09/24 Application Deadline 01/07/24 - Commences 01/11/24 Application Deadline 01/09/24 - Commences 01/01/25 Application Deadline 15/01/25 - Commences 01/04/25 Application Deadline 01/03/25 - Commences 01/06/25 *For people applying on shorter notice, please email for availability.
studioInfo: Studios spaces for Open AiR residents are available (at a reasonable extra cost) if needed in the heart of the artisan quarter of Sefrou where carpenters and tailors work and Culture Vultures hosts an office for community heritage projects and a micro-museum on multiculturalism. Former residents have worked in these studios but most residents have preferred to work on roofs, in coffeeshops and open-air spaces in Sefrou as its (artisan) community have formed their main interlocutors to the incoming residents.
accommodationInfo: Artists are accommodated in an apartment on the edge of the ancient medina of Sefrou. The house has two bedrooms, a bathroom, a salon, a working table and a well equipped kitchen.
technicalInfo: Internet access, local contacts for printing, process and presentation of artwork.

name: Fondation Montresso*
description: In Marrakesh, the Montresso★ Art Foundation has been committed since 2009 to the establishment and development of an artists' residency: Jardin Rouge. Open to visitors, by appointment, Jardin Rouge aims to build a factory of links and sharing. Events are organised both inside and outside the Foundation, with a wide range of cultural and artistic institutions, to provide artists with exhibition spaces in which to present their work and to raise their profile in Morocco and abroad. In agreement with the artist, a selection of works produced during the residency is offered for purchase.
studioInfo: The residency program enables selected artists to develop a visual arts project by providing the technical, material and financial resources as well as a workplace.
accommodationInfo: The Montresso★ Art Foundation provides funding for the production of the artistic project approved by the selection committee. It will also cover transport, individual accommodation, meals, all necessary equipment and the provision of an individual workshop on the residency site.

name: New Zero Art Space
description: New Zero Art Space is the nonprofit visual art organization established in Yangon, Myanmar in 2008. The art Space promotes contemporary art and artists with an intention of promoting new young art spirits of the next generation. They are unique in Myanmar. The meaning of new Zero symbolizes new as the welcoming of new artists and zero represents the value of infinity.(Zero is the nature of the non-valued, yet increases into highly valued when combined with the other numbers). They aim to augment the abilities of each artist to increase their value and individual experience but they also foster cooperation amongst each other as artists to support the collective. New Zero Art Space, Yangon, Myanmar invites visual (and performance) artists from Asia, Europe and North America to the first Artist-in-Residency Program in Myanmar. The program is an opportunity to support artists from around the world who have a keen interest in Myanmar art and culture. The philosophy of the program also encourages an ongoing exchange with the art and culture from the artist’s host country. Due to the limit budget, the new zero board of directors and advisor will select some young artists and established artists from Asia, America and Europe.
studioInfo: Exhibition space, studio and living space are provided.
technicalInfo: A library full of art books, the other various kinds of books, DVDs, and Local documentaries for free.

name: Space A
description: Space A, a beacon of interdisciplinary art practice established in 2008 in Kathmandu, Nepal. Comprised of visual artists, interior designers, jewelry designers, musicians, and writers, Space A thrives on its unique diversity, birthing a plethora of magnificent ideas. Nestled in Babarmahal, Kathmandu, Space A is an autonomous, non-governmental, non-political, and not-for-profit artist initiative organization. Its mission? To provide a stable platform for critical analysis, reflection, open discussion, information exchange, collaboration, and interactive communication, thus enriching the landscape of contemporary art practices. Space A’s Kathmandu International Artist-in-Residency (KIAR) program offers immersive residencies for artists across disciplines—visual arts, performance, music, writing, and more. Set in the vibrant cultural hub of Kathmandu, KIAR fosters collaboration, critical dialogue, and artistic experimentation, providing a space for reflection and research in an inspiring interdisciplinary environment. KIAR is an opportunity to travel back in time and to relive in history as well as experience natural beauty. We are going to organize a one-month-long residency (30 days) and two-month long residency (60 days). Each time max. 4 applicants will be selected. If participants are interested, KIAR will arrange 7 days of trekking during the residency program. But participants will be responsible for all expenses for trekking. (Trekking: Annapurna base camp (ABC) or Langtang track or Mardi track) Residency Highlights: Private room & shared working space (rooftop, 2 studios and ceramic kilns) with Internet Connection Access to shared spaces: kitchen, bathroom, and weekly laundry service Optional 7-day trekking (Annapurna Base Camp, Langtang, or Mardi trek) Opportunities to host workshops or presentations Promotion through Space A’s platforms Strong connections with Nepal’s cultural and artistic community
studioInfo: Two different studios 15 ft.
accommodationInfo: Private room & shared working space (rooftop, 2 studios and ceramic kilns) with Internet Connection Access to shared spaces: kitchen, bathroom, and weekly laundry service
technicalInfo: Four residents max each time, and partners are welcome if communicated and confirmed in advance.

name: Artudio international artists residency (AIAR)
description: Artudio, a contemporary art platform at the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal, regards artistic creation as an essential cornerstone of a vibrant, equitable, and flourishing society. Through its distinguished International Artists Residency Program (AIA Residency), Artudio invites artists from all disciplines—visual arts, music, literature, performance, and beyond—along with curators, writers, researchers, and interdisciplinary experts to immerse themselves in a culturally, naturally, and artistically enriched environment. This program champions cross-cultural collaboration, exchange and fosters an inspiring ecosystem where creative and intellectual pursuits thrive. The AIA Residency accommodates two international artists simultaneously, offering flexible durations from 1 to 6 months tailored to the needs of each participant. The organisers encourage artists to conduct a workshop to young artists or students at Artudio or our partner institutions. They welcome visionary thinkers and contemporary artists from around the globe, spanning diverse disciplines including: Visual Arts (painting, drawing, mixed media, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking) New Media Art (video art, sound art, digital installations) Design (graphic, industrial, fashion, illustration) Writing (literature, poetry, art criticism) Curatorial Practices and Research Performance Arts (theater, dance, interdisciplinary) Creative Media (photography, vlogging, creative influencing) Artudio’s International Artist Residency Program is designed for visionary artists seeking to redefine creative boundaries, explore new forms of expression, and gain international recognition within a vibrant artistic community. The organisers look forward to welcoming you to Kathmandu for a transformative artistic journey.
studioInfo: (625 Square Feet) Dedicated workspace with individual desks along with additional shared studio space of (800 Square Feet) in the same building.
accommodationInfo: Spacious bedroom with balcony views of the Swayambhunath Stupa Shared kitchen equipped with basic amenities (gas stove, refrigerator, microwave, utensils) Shared bathroom with a hot water shower Dedicated workspace with individual desks High-speed wireless internet Access to a common washing machine Airport pick-and-drop service Weekly housekeeping services (dusting, sheet changes, restroom cleaning) Black-and-white printing (A4 size) and photocopy services Networking opportunities within Nepal’s art scene Organized exhibitions and presentations at Artudio with event invitations Monthly curated visits to galleries, studios, museums, libraries, and significant sites tailored to artists’ needs

name: Kala Yatra Artist Residency
description: Kala Yatra is an artist-run, not-for-profit collective that curates concept-based exhibitions, socially relevant projects, and artist residencies while also engaging the community through workshops and educational outreach. By promoting artistic thoughts and practices, Kala Yatra fosters important momentum for social transformation. Kala Yatra is a space for in-betweenness, fostering cross-border, cross-disciplinary, and multi-perspective exchanges in thought and practice. It is both a physical and conceptual journey - a process-driven exploration of art, culture, and Nepal’s socio-political landscape. Dedicated to diversity and equity, Kala Yatra provides a vibrant platform for artists from varied backgrounds, including those often underrepresented. It cultivates an environment of open dialogue and collaboration, encouraging brainstorming, shared creative processes, and the co-development of ideas. Through informal events and initiatives, Kala Yatra celebrates diverse cultures and perspectives while fostering an inclusive community focused on sustainable growth and lasting connections. Artists may embrace a non-productive mode, free from deadlines and formalities, to research, reflect, and explore their practice. Kala Yatra invites applications for its concept-driven, community-engaged artist residency program in Kathmandu, Nepal. Rooted in socially relevant practice and cross-cultural dialogue, Kala Yatra is a not-for-profit, artist-run collective offering space for reflection, experimentation, and transformation across disciplines. What residents receive: • Flexible self-funded residencies (2 weeks–1+ month) • Private self-catering accommodation with shared spaces • Opportunities for exhibitions, open studios, talks, or non-productive reflection • Access to a diverse, supportive art community • Possibility of reduced fees for SAARC artists • Open to visual artists, writers, performers, curators, filmmakers, architects, musicians & more This is a space of in-betweenness—where artistic practice meets community, culture, and critical inquiry.
studioInfo: Kala Yatra provides shared studio spaces for resident artists.
accommodationInfo: Residents stay in private, self-catering accommodations with access to the internet, a shared kitchen, dining area, and a small common workspace. The space comfortably accommodates three to four residents, and partners are welcome with prior communication and confirmation.

name: Kunstwerk Kolderveen
description: Kunstwerk Kolderveen facilitates artistic production by offering a space and tools for artists to produce artworks at an affordable price and stay over for a two month residency. Artists and curators can stay can apply, either for the production of an artwork or for research.
studioInfo: Shared large studio of 100 sqm with daylight, 6 meters high.
accommodationInfo: 60 sqm private apartment bedroom, kitchen, toilet, parking place, two bikes and internet. Ideal for a couple and possibly a small child. Animals allowed. No access for wheelchairs.
technicalInfo: Depending on your plans, the organisers can prepare the studio with wood working equipment, metal working, 3D printing, computers to work on VR, simulation and animation, or a small painting lab for encaustic painting. They will do this in consultation with you. In principle the studio is not manned by any technicians. If you require assistance or craft knowledge this is possible to be arrange for an extra fee and depending on availability of the technicians.

name: Gallery Mcube
description: AIR_MCUBE International Artists Residency Program, hosted by Gallery Mcube in Lalitpur, is one of Nepal’s most pioneering and exceptional artist residencies. Established in 2011, this non-profit initiative has become a creative haven for artists from around the world, giving them the opportunity to explore, experiment, and immerse themselves in Nepal’s dynamic cultural scene. Open to visual artists, writers, photographers, media artists, sound artists, composers, and multidisciplinary practitioners, AIR_MCUBE fosters an environment where creativity is nurtured and dialogue is encouraged. Residents are supported not only in developing their own artistic practices but also in exchanging ideas, collaborating across disciplines, and immersing themselves in the vibrant local context. Through presentations, interaction sessions, and critical feedback forums, participants gain valuable perspectives from peers, professionals, and the Nepali art community. More than just a residency, AIR_MCUBE is a transformative journey—one that rewards artists with new insights, cross-cultural connections, and an expanded creative vision. AIR_MCUBE International Artists Residency Program offers flexible stays ranging from one to three months, giving artists the freedom to choose a period that best suits their creative journey. Applications are open throughout the year in four cycles: January – March April – June July – September October – December
studioInfo: Gallery Mcube offers artists a creative and comfortable environment, with spacious, naturally lit studios of 300 sq. ft, a terrace, and a peaceful garden to inspire work and reflection. Residents have access to professional woodworking and metalworking tools to explore and realize ambitious projects.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation includes private, well-furnished rooms with shared kitchen, dining and bathroom facilities, fostering community and comfort. The residency also provides a gallery space for exhibitions, a café area, and high-speed Wi-Fi, creating a nurturing space for artistic growth and cultural exchange.

name: Valley of the Possible
description: Open call for RECONNECT- autumn cycle- which will take place from 6th of September to 17th of October 2026. For this ERF programme -hosted by Valley of the Possible & Bodemzicht Foundation at Gagel Farm - we welcome artists of all disciplines and cultural practitioners to apply for a residency stay of 42 days. Two EAT residents, two FARM residents and one RECONNECT resident will work collaboratively and side by side on the farm. All residents will work, cook, eat and collaborate with the Gagel farm team, have designated mentors, are offered free coaching and are invited to partake in interdisciplinary workshops in order to stimulate cross pollination. This residency also includes: accommodation, a €2.000 stipend per resident and an additional artistic production and research budget with a maximum of €1.000, access to a covered outdoor resident kitchen for experiments and gatherings, a broad European network in the regenerative movement, participation in a 'Holistic context' course, various public lectures and on site events at the farm, access to the vegetable garden and eggs and much more. Find out more about the application criteria for each different open call, and how to apply in our downloadable PDF on the websites of valley of the possible and Gagel farm. Application deadline closes 8th June, 2026 Once 50 applications have been received per open call, the open call will be closed due to the processing capacity of our organisation. Applicants will be notified by email around July 8th. Good luck with your applications and if you have any questions don’t hesitate to reach out!
studioInfo: There is no designated studio or working atelier except from the tiny house itself and a communal test kitchen.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation in a tiny house on Gagel Farm. Gagel Farm is a beautiful 45ha regenerative farm operating in a holistic context in Lochem, the Netherlands. The team is creating a landscape full of life: plants, animals, microbes and people whom are all given space to grow and work together on a thriving local food system. With 9 business lines: garden, orchard, tree nursery, animals, courses, activities, camping, catering and shop, they are not only working on a resilient company with beautiful regenerative products, but also on a resilient landscape for future generations. Gagel Farm brings together local, national and European farmers, citizens, scientists, entrepreneurs, artists and policy makers to meet each other in ways of regeneration.

name: Retort
description: Retort is an independent artist foundation and is situated in a lively area in the South of Amsterdam. It consists of 34 professional artist studios.
studioInfo: The studio is over 32 m 2  and has skylight over almost the entire length of the studio and tap water.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation is not provided.

name: Thami Mnyele Foundation
description: Established in 1990, the Thami Mnyele Foundation runs a unique three month artists-in-residence program in Amsterdam. The main objective of the Foundation is to advance cultural exchange between artists from Africa, the Netherlands and Amsterdam in particular. To this aim, the Foundation engages artists from African continent and diaspora of all disciplines of contemporary visual art (painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, video, film, audio and multi media) to work for three months in the Thami Mnyele Foundation studio, located in an old school building in the centre of Amsterdam. The Thami Mnyele Foundation Residency Award is therefore an ideal opportunity for concentration on work, reflection, research and discussion. The artist in residence receives a grant for living expenses and a budget for material and the travelling expenses to and from the Netherlands. In order to promote this cultural exchange, the Thami Mnyele Foundation mediates in meetings with artists and people associated with the Dutch art world. The selection of participants is done on a regular basis by an independent selection committee of experts, which is appointed by the Board of the Foundation. There are two residency programs the Full Residency Program and the Short Residency Program. Full Residency Program Full residencies are awarded competitively to artists from the whole of African continent and diaspora. The Thami Mnyele Foundation offers several Full Residency Program awards per year. Those selected are offered accommodation and studio space for a three month period. Artists who are selected for the Full Residency Program also receive: free housing free studio a reimbursment of return travel to Amsterdam cost of medical test for Covid-19 a monthly allowance which covers the costs for living and materials (currently amounting to 900 euro per month) medical and legal liability insurance for the period of stay free internet free museum card free use of two bicycles assistance in applying for visa an introduction to the Dutch art world and access to the Foundation’s extensive network. Short Residency Program Short Residency Programs are awarded to artists from the whole of African continent and diaspora, who have been invited to participate in cultural projects in the Netherlands and are in need of accommodation in Amsterdam for a short period. The Short Residency Program offers artists free studio and housing for a set period of time. The Short Residency Program does not include an allowance for living and material costs, medical and legal liability insurance and traveling expenses, nor does the Foundation assist in visa application.
studioInfo: The Thami Mnyele Foundation manages a studio annex living space located on the second floor of a nineteenth century school building. Situated in Amsterdam Oud-West, a lively and bustling area in Amsterdam, the studio contains a spacious work space and a separate living area, including a kitchenette, bedroom and bathroom. The studio is equipped with central heating, kitchen utilities, two Apple computers, bedding and sheets. The artist can make use of a bicycle and a mobile telephone during his or her stay.

name: AGA LAB
description: AGA LAB is an artist-run printmaking workplace. AGA LAB offers four artist-in-residence places, two with living arrangements and two without. The residency is open to both international as well as local professionals. AGA LAB’s Artist in Residence program offers space for research, experimentation and the development of new work. A weekly Artist Talk is organised to give participating artists a chance to reflect on their work and process, and prepare for an optional presentation to conclude the residency. The studio offers a wide range of printing techniques, technical expertise, a spacious non-toxic workshop, exchange with (inter)national colleagues, an urban agricultural garden with ink plants and many creative neighbours. For many artists in the graphic art world, AGA LAB is a starting point for their work and stimulates their free-range and creative research. AGA LAB expressively searches for the dialogue between artists, designers and other creative professionals on social developments. Former Artists in Residence mention the expertise of staff, the exchange with other artists, 24/7 studio access, large screen printing tables and great litho presses as reasons for the success of their stay.
studioInfo: Residents have 24/7 access to the studio. The residencies are connected to the spacious print studio which is located in an old, spacious school building which houses studios for creatives. There is a separate 80 m2 project space. The rooms have entrance to the courtyard.
accommodationInfo: The accommodation has a private bathroom and a shared kitchen.
technicalInfo: Digital printing; screen printing; textile printing; relief printing; etching; lithography; risograph printing and analogue darkroom.

name: NEAC - Nepal Europe Art Center
description: The mission of stichting NEAC is to generate awareness for and by Art(ist). They are connecting people from all around the world and from different art disciplines together and let them (re)discover the world of art. To open up visions of artist and society. They focus not only on a select group of insiders but they want to research the spectrum of art together with the society, to make them find new strength by experience.
studioInfo: They provide studio space for working in different disciplines.
accommodationInfo: 5 studio rooms.
technicalInfo: Workshop space for ceramics, painter rooms, lecture room, music room, library etc.

name: AiR Nieuw en Meer
description: Artist community Nieuw en Meer offers a guest studio for a fixed period of three months (not less, not more) where they welcome artists who work in the field of fine arts (music excluded). (January, February, March / April, May, June / July, August, September /October, November, December) Situated within the beautiful outskirts of Amsterdam surrounded by a park bordering the lake ‘de Nieuwe Meer’ The guest studio offers the ideal environment for reflection and concentration.
studioInfo: The guest studio is conveniently situated in one of the main warehouse buildings. It measures 48m2 and is equipped with a simple sleeping area, a kitchen with supplies, shower, toilet, floor heating and wifi.
accommodationInfo: The location of the premises is slightly isolated from the city in a nature environment. Riding a bicycle (which they provide) is highly recommended to be mobile. There is public bus transportation within a 10 min walk but you have to be able to be self sufficient since this is an artist run programme.

name: Farm Art
description: Farm Art is a small-scale, self-directed artist residency located in the rural village of Bellingwolde, in the north of the Netherlands. Farm Art is a living, working place shaped by care, attention, and shared responsibility. It offers artists time and space for rest, research, experimentation, and reflection, away from urban rhythms and institutional structures. Residencies are self-guided and may be entirely process-based, without the requirement of a final outcome. Farm Art recognizes our reliance and interconnectedness to nature. Artists are invited outside of the urban environment to engage and learn from her. The hope is for the mending of our cognitive dissonance, both collective and individual by fostering connection, care and community. Stays at Farm Art are characterised by the rural setting, immersion into nature and proximity to the German border. Visitors are hosted in small, well equiped huts in the garden. The property is surrounded by industrial farmlands, and contrasting with this is the small-scale food production of the garden. Participants are encouraged to engage with the local (non) human community thus creating a space for trust-building and voluntary interactions. Farm Art hosts one artist at a time.
studioInfo: An insulated garden hut with a woodburning fire, desk, simple cooking facilities, fridge etc.
accommodationInfo: Artists stay in a simple, insulated garden hut with a wood-burning stove, surrounded by a working garden. There are simple cooking facilities, small fridge, compost toilet, hot water and bicycle for residents use.
technicalInfo: -An ‘outhouse’ with a compost toilet, a washbasin and hot water. -A quiet rural environment that invites reflection and focus. -A ceramic kiln.

description: 1646 is an art space in the heart of The Hague. With its experimental, international and free public program, 1646 wants to contribute to an increasingly complex society by challenging existing systems and traditional views, to reflect on the questions that live among us all. The residency offers (inter)national artists and curators the possibility to stay and work/research at our location in the centre of The Hague. 1646’s residency aims to support innovative practices, develop global networks, and engage the local art community in The Netherlands.
studioInfo: Studio space of 5m x 3m inside the building. The studio comes with a wi-fi internet connection and residents have access to technical facilities.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation: a studio apartment nearby the gallery with private cooking facilities, internet and shared toilet and shower. Children and partners are welcome to join the residency.

name: OT301
description: OT301 prefers the residency to be mutual beneficial to all involved. Therefore each applicant is asked to explain in detail why he or she is interested in renting a space in the building. They are looking for people that take their stay seriously and that are ready to integrate and participate in the collective structure of the EHBK-association..With the participation in the residency program each artist will be: Taking part in curated events & exhibitions in 4BID gallery as artist and as curator Artist talks and presentation of the work in progress Participate in 4BID gallery’s activities as a temporary member of the group, with the opportunity to make decisions on the program in collaboration with the team Part of one show in 4BID gallery Weekly ‘Open Studio’ on each Wednesday from 16 – 18:00h meeting with the curators of 4BID gallery and participation to 4BID meetings every two weeks on Wednesday from 18h Further events & shows by interest & agreement possible, also in collaboration with the other initiatives in the building Further events & exhibitions at the locations of our partners by interest & agreement
studioInfo: A low rent studio/living space on the 2nd floor of the main building - a maximum stay of three months with at least one presentation in the building - participation in discussions and the program of OT301/EHBK.
accommodationInfo: The OT-residency space is located on the 3rd floor of the main building. It’s a cosy studio that is devided in two sections. A bedroom and a studio with a small kitchen. All modestly equipped. The size of the room is 42 m2, the bedroom is 14 m2, and the studio is 28 m2. The shower and the toilet are shared facilities in the hallway of the building. Important to note: The building can be noisy sometimes. It’s part of the building and it’s living and working conditions.

name: Rijksakademie van Beeldende Kunsten
description: The Rijksakademie welcomes applications from artists to develop their work over one or two-year periods in Amsterdam. The Rijksakademie houses a highly international, multi-disciplinary, experimental and critically engaged artist community. Residents are supported with a studio, a working budget and a stipend and benefit from an array of opportunities for exchange, including peer-to-peer dialogue and visits from a wide range of leading art professionals. They have access to technical workshops as well as an extensive library and a historical collection. There is guidance by technical specialists, who foster hands-on, innovative and collaborative approaches to making. Every year they select on average 22 artists for a residency, and most of the artists stay for two years, so the total community consists of about 45 artists. Half of the group is from the Netherlands, and the other half is from all around the world. What are they looking for? You have an original position in the field you are working in. This must be visible in the uploaded portfolio, which is the most important element of the jury process in the first round. Please try to make sure that your portfolio gives us a clear idea about the content and formal aspects of your practice. You have enough experience of independent practice (after education) to benefit from the critical environment at the Rijksakademie, but not too much experience that a residency cannot really add much in terms of artistic development, which is the main focus of the residency. You have a clear idea about how you would like to use the residency (what you need, and what you bring) and why that is important for you now. Having one- or two-years of time and space, facilities and feedback in an international and diverse artist community is a unique opportunity which can be a transformative experience for your work and thinking. You are willing and able to commit actively and full-time: to your own work but also to the highly diverse community of artists from all around the world you will be part of.
studioInfo: The Rijksakademie offers 45 studios.
accommodationInfo: There is access to affordable housing options.
technicalInfo: Technical specialists manage professionally-equipped workshops where artists can work and experiment with traditional and contemporary materials and techniques. Artistic, theoretical and technical facilities and expertise are the basis of the residency. In addition, advices on practical and financial matters like housing and residence permits are offered.

name: Kunsthuis SYB
description: Kunsthuis SYB is an Artist Residency based in Friesland, in the northern part of The Netherlands. SYB offers space, stimulus and support to artists and curators to deepen their practice through means of research, experiment and new collaborations. Residents are not obliged to produce a fixed artwork but are encouraged to converse with professionals and scientists from different fields to broaden their network and research and to share their work process. Every resident is in dialogue with a member of SYB´s programming committee. The committee consists of artists, curators and art historians. SYB also works with a group of young art critics who will write a text or review about each residency. There are two types of residencies: Residencies for visual artists, curators and artist initiatives living or working in the Netherlands. Summer residencies for foreign visual artists and initiatives.
accommodationInfo: A residency includes 24-hour access to a furnished apartment and studio space, organizational guidance, artistic feedback, publicity and a presentation at SYB.

name: atelierWG
description: airWG is an international Artist in Residence programme organized by atelierWG, a community of over 120 artists whose studios are located in two buildings of the former Wilhelmina Gasthuis hospital. Founded in 2015, airWG functions as a laboratory and platform for in-depth artistic development. The programme welcomes a broad range of art projects including interdisciplinary, curatorial and research-oriented ones. It provides artists with time and space to reflect, experiment, create and share their projects. LOCATION: Construction of the Wilhelmina Gasthuis hospital, named after the reigning queen at the time, began in 1891. Each medical specialty was given its own pavilion, including the women's clinic (pavilion 18) and the eye clinic (pavilion 19). After the hospital relocated in 1984, the pavilions 18 and 19 became studios for artists. The WG compound is located in the heart of Amsterdam, within easy reach of museums, galleries, theatres, cinemas, shops, restaurants and parks. Over more than 40 years, it has been home to artists, architects, designers, writers and musicians who have shaped and preserved its unique character. The community organizes a variety of art activities, including an annual open studio event, exhibitions at puntWG and the residency programme airWG.
accommodationInfo: 70 m2 studio, living room, fully equipped kitchen, bathroom, washing machine, storage space, internet, bicycle and garden (please note this is a non-smoking space) Note: The resident artist is responsible for the proper use of airWG's physical space and furniture, as well as the rational use of electricity, water and heating services. The lack of responsibility for the use of the services can lead to extra rates for the resident.
technicalInfo: A video projector, sound system, and basic materials for installation, paint, and maintenance.

name: Bierumer School
description: In a dynamic area characterised by drowned villages, wind turbines, rectilinear fields and meandering marches through nature, agriculture and (offshore) industry, Bierumer School offers artists space for production and presentation. Bierumer School is focused on experiment and development, where art asks questions and is not always looking for answers. A place for the imagination of the not immediately definable. An open and active refuge for artists of all disciplines. Bierumer School is part of De Noordenaars, a platform for presentation institutions and art initiatives in the Northern Netherlands. De Noordenaars consists, among others, of Academie Minerva, Kunsthuis SYB, Media Art Friesland, Noorderlicht, SIGN and VHDG. The Noordenaars stand for experiment, development of talent and the production of new art, and are responsible, among other things, for the Artist in Space programme. This is an experimental talent programme developed and implemented by the members of De Noordaars. These 12 art institutes from the North of the Netherlands work together and create new opportunities for talent within the visual arts.
studioInfo: The studio is a former classroom of 64 square metres. The presentation areas consist of another former classroom of 64 square metres at the front of the building and an (dark) attic of 500 square metres. Behind the building is a schoolyard that can be used, as well as a lawn in front.
accommodationInfo: There is a private living studio consisting of one room on the attic floor. This room has a kitchenette and also functions as a living room and bedroom. The shower and the toilet are on the ground floor.
technicalInfo: Internet is available. There are some beamers and tv-screens available.

name: DCR Guest Studio's
description: De DCR is a cultural incubator that also houses 40 permanent studios for artists and designers, including the studio of Satellietgroep, Zaal 3-laboratory for Performing Arts (formerly Zeebelt), sound studio Loos, Cloud Danslab and exhibition space Nest.
studioInfo: Each studios space includes a private kitchen and bathroom, shared washing machine and wireless internet. There are bicycles available and the DCR Gueststudios are located near the center of The Hague, on biking distance from the sea, Gemeentemuseum, Stroom, Mauritshuis, etc.

name: United Cowboys
description: The residency program of United Cowboys is embedded in the overall Artistic Goals of United Cowboys and offers artists from different disciplines the opportunity to develop and present their work at the Art House in Eindhoven. United Cowboys believes in the importance of contributing to further developments of (international) art circuits to stimulate collaboration and exchange in order to come to new forms of creation, participation and presentation. The Art House, with its two rehearsal studios, a smaller studio, a few offices and accommodation for longer stays, is perfectly suited to offer accommodation to artists in residency - both national and international artists - who can develop a project here, finalize it and open it to an audience. In addition United Cowboys invites artists in residence to join a dialogue with the artistic directors of United Cowboys and other artists from Eindhoven. The term 'Residencies' is used in the broader sense of the word: it goes beyond simply allowing other choreographers to work in the building in the sense of ‘place of production’. The idea is to extend the invitation to artists from all disciplines. More specifically: artists who work from a similar mission as United Cowboys or who join in their world-vision. Essential is mutual enrichment, nurturing and improving the exchange with various art forms. Note: the guest creator/artist does not have to work with United Cowboys. The point is an exchange between artists who lift themselves above the ‘usual’ and who together will find a way to showcase their mutual creations. United Cowboys has a strong bond with the cultural field in Eindhoven. The idea is that the temporary artist-in-residence showcases his/her work at the Art House, but also connects with the city cultural circuit. The audience also plays a role in the communication and openness. In order to meet the guest artist, meetings with the general public will be made possible, just as open rehearsals, questions-and-answer sessions, etc. With the exchange, United Cowboys wants to build a long-term relationship with artists/creators and international residency places. The important thing is that the investigation, the artistic process is central. The Art House as artistic ‘home’, the network as artistic platform, the whole an artistic web from which every fibre adds to innovation, communication and exchange. It is also important that a clear artistic profile is given to the place and the programme. The artistic team of United Cowboys will be leading and curating; they instigate the dialogue and stimulate the discussion. With Seasoning United Cowboys has already invited various artists from all disciplines over the past years and offered them a research place, a house to meet and discuss and a stage on which they, together with other disciplines, have provided multi-disciplinary evenings to the general public.
studioInfo: Art House, in the center of Eindhoven, is the work space, a creative hub and production space for artists from various disciplines. The well-equipped building offers performance, studio and rehearsal environments. WHITE SPACE The 160m2 White Space can be used as a flexible rehearsal and presentation space. It has fixed seating for a maximum of 80, with the additional option to open up the surrounding gallery for audiences. BLACK SPACE The 180m2 Black Space is an empty open black box space, which is suitable for performances or rehearsals, that require a flexible and intimate setting. STUDIO The 185 m2 Studio 3 is a light and open space, ideal for rehearsals, workshops, or classes for smaller groups. Download space & tech specs. Free Wifi in the entire building. Duo's are welcome, family and partners are not preferred. Up to five residents can be hosted at once.
accommodationInfo: 4 private rooms with shared bathrooms are provided.
technicalInfo: Apart from hosting the quarterly SEASONING events, United Cowboys invite artists to stay and work on-site. The space has several performance spaces, rehearsal rooms, a kitchen, a bar and a library.

name: Greylight Projects
description: Greylight Projects is a platform for arts and culture that focuses on the development and presentation of visual and contemporary art projects. Greylight Projects aims to encourage collaboration and connection among artists, bringing creators together and facilitating conversations. Open call for one residency of three months (1 January – 30 March 2026), organized by Greylight Projects (Heerlen, NL) in collaboration with the international dance festival schrit_tmacher. The residency offers space for visual artists, dancers, choreographers and performers to deepen their practice and expand their network. Guided by open curiosity, Greylight Projects and schrit_tmacher Festival invites makers to reflect on relationships within themes like: technology, humanity, environment and society. The residency is aimed at artists whose work engages with these questions through forms such as research, dance, performance, installation or other media. The residency encourages interdisciplinary approaches and forms that expand conventional boundaries of art and performance and practices that explore storytelling, personal or collective narratives, untold stories, revealing experiences that are often overlooked or unspoken. They welcome artists who are open to sharing their process with peers and the public. There are no restrictions in discipline or medium, as long as the practice resonates with the context of the program.
studioInfo: The residency offers a studio space of approximately 40m² at Greylight Projects in Heerlen. The studio also serves as the living space. Kitchen, shower, and toilet facilities are shared with others in the building.
accommodationInfo: Since 2020, Greylight Projects has been based in a former school building in the heart of Heerlen.
