Once a week there will be a cleaning service and you can have access to our laundry service. You have access to the remaining creative spaces of the house, such as the studio and the library, the gallery and the auditorium.
accommodationInfo: There are four sunny, spacious and private bedrooms available on the second floor of VIC, each of them dedicated to a different art process — Projects, Alchemy, Sketch and Jazz.
technicalInfo: VIC Aveiro Arts House possesses a sound system, projector, and electronic music studio with a synthesizer. They also have basic tools, such as drills, electric saws, and soldering iron. They facilitate access to human and material resources and integrate the artists within the local and national networks that are most relevant for each specific case, hence, in collaboration with partners they can provide for example exhibition or rehearsal spaces.

name: Quinta das Relvas
description: An artist-in-residence program, with access to workshops and study visits focused on the intersection between art and sustainability, and supported by a team of caring and experienced professionals. For the residencies they conceived a flexible program for each week that comprises activities and workshops such as: – introduction sessions to: Permaculture, Syntropic agroforest and other regenerative practices; – workshops and experience sharing on means for a more sustainable art practice, etc.; – study visits (Serralves Museum, Oliva Contemporary Art Center, Viarco – Pencil Factory, Águeda Arts Center; among others); – mentoring, support and advice; – an Open Studio moment for the local community (Please notice that the Open Studio moment will only happen once, at the end of the month); – Movie nights. Consider that all activities are suggestive and noncompulsory and rearrangements or adjustments can be made according to the needs and circumstances of the moment. You will always have a mentor or staff nearby for your questions.
studioInfo: As an art resident you will have access to the following: Visual art studio-atelier of 80m2 with natural light, equipped with washing station, heating and private toilet; Personal table and light; White walls with 4 mt height that allow hanging paper or canvas; Painting easels; Multimedia tools (tv screens, projector, DSLR camera and studio lights) – if available; Access to Analog photography studio; Performative art atelier 80m2 (if needed and available); All the outside garden areas; Access to a big range of natural materials (wood, clay, hay, etc) and plants (sustainable harvesting will be properly briefed; consider that each season will give access to different plants); All available tools and art materials on demand and with proper safety and working briefing (carpentry, drawing, available natural pigments); Educational material (pdf, available books, staffs’ brains, etc.). In order to ensure your belongings and art pieces safety all working rooms are opened with a secure code key.
accommodationInfo: All resident participants will be based in the headquarters of the NGO, a XVIII century farm, with an amazing natural heritage. Residents will be staying in eco-tiny houses. Studios and shared spaces are on a short walking distance. Some of the amenities are: Shared fully equipped kitchen; Shared bathroom; Common living room; Access to Wi-Fi internet wide band in working areas; 10 minutes walking from local commerce; 10 min drive from big supermarket and nearest town; Car will be available once for week for groceries and bikes for daily use; Pick-up from and to local transports. You can read all the information about the working spaces and accommodation on their website .

name: Ateliers Nos Silos
description: SILOS emerged from a need for a dedicated space in Caldas da Rainha where creative entrepreneurs, students and enterprises could gather to create, re-invent or re-imagine a product/service or pitch potential clients. The SILOS platform is wide opened to promote every structured form of creativity. Located in an old meal Ateliers Nos Silos has spaces with various configurations that might go from open space dynamics to rooms with 80m2.
accommodationInfo: Low-cost or no-cost artist rooms in the Arts Center of Caldas da Rainha, located in the middle of 4 Museums.

name: Aviário Studio
description: 4-week AiR in a creative playground in central Portugal to develop a large format printmaking project. Aviário Studio Large Format Printmaking Residency is open to both artists working in large format or artists willing to develop new work on a larger scale using Printmaking techniques, such as relief, intaglio, screen printing, transfer, and monotype. During the AIR, artists will have access to technical assistance and weekly project discussions in order to better achieve their intents.
studioInfo: Aviário Studio is a creative playground located in the center of Portugal, immersed in nature and just 2 km away from the town Ferreira do Zêzere. The studio has 6 rooms in total, each one about 100 meters square: 1 common room with kitchen and 3 toilets (one adapted for people with reduced mobility) 4 workshops: 2 are equipped to work images: silkscreen, printmaking, digital work, drawing, and bookbinding 2 are equipped to work object: wood, metal and ceramics 1 room for the development of projects with irregular dimensions and/or materials.
accommodationInfo: Artists will be hosted in a shared house in the center of Ferreira do Zêzere, 2 km/1,24 mi away from Aviário Studio. The house is on the ground floor, and has three double bedrooms, a living room, a bathroom and a toilet, a fully-equipped kitchen, and some outside space. Each artist has clean sheets and towels each week. There is wi-fi in the house. There are four bicycles to share. Each weekday there is a ride from the house to the studio at 10 a.m. and a ride back to the home from the studio at 6 p.m.
technicalInfo: Specific types of equipment available: Cutting Table 240 x 140 cm - 94,49 x 55,12 in Paper Guillotine 80 cm - 31,5 in Metal Guillotine 100 cm/39,37 in Polymetaal Press 260 x 140 cm - 102,36 x 55,12 in UV Light Exposure Unit 150 x 120 cm - 59,06 x 47,24 n 2 Drying Racks Screen Printing Table What is not included: paper, matrix (wood, metal, plastic,...), silkscreens (use, coating, and exposure), silkscreen inks, printmaking inks (we have black, white, yellow, red, and blue offset ink for proof prints).

name: Artemis Gallery
description: Inspired by the age-old tradition of familiar salt production in the south of Portugal and fueled by the boundless possibilities of new media art, they have forged a unique space where these two divergent worlds come together. Since their roots run deep in the tradition of the sea and salt, the residency is a tribute to the legacy that has shaped generations and community. The timeless art of harvesting salt from the earth, guided by ancestral knowledge and the rhythm of nature, forms the bedrock of our inspiration. The unique partnership with Artemis Gallery, a Portuguese commercial gallery focused on new media art, infuses innovation and modernity into our creative endeavors. The past and future can coexist, enhancing the other in a powerful fusion of creativity. SALT Residency wants to be a Hub for artists from diverse backgrounds in which they can learn, explore, experiment, and express. Here, you will find a melting pot of ideas, a crossroads of cultures, and a crucible of innovation. Program Highlights: The access to studios and facilities is designed to accommodate the different art disciplines' diverse needs. Mentorship and guidance from accomplished artists, curators, and industry professionals. Formative/educational component focused on the art market. Engaging workshops, artist talks, and panel discussions to broaden artistic perspectives. Opportunities for collaboration with local artists and engagement with the community. Open studio events to showcase the residents' works to a diverse audience. Networking sessions and connections to galleries, institutions, and potential patrons. The final exhibition will be provided for Artemis Gallery Lisbon. Educational Content Program The program will empower emerging and established artists with the knowledge and tools to thrive in the ever-evolving art market matters. This program will be led by the Artemis gallery owner and supported by the participation of guest artists and/or curators, and/or patrons who can share their knowledge, path, and experience. Module 1 - History of the Art Market (context - origins to contemporary trends) Module 2 - Definition of the Primary and the Secondary Markets (how this dynamic can impact the artist's career) Module 3 - Valuing Art (how to assess and determine the value of your art - pricing and negotiation) Module 4 - Art Finance (some financial aspects of the art world) Module 5 - Value Regulation (some mechanisms that regulate art values) Module 6 - Online Market, Art Fairs, and New Technologies in Art
studioInfo: The residency will provide studios for the artists that can develop different artistic mediums. It is possible to host duos of artists if they work as a collective. However, this information will be under approval by the selection committee. Not groups or families are allowed.

name: OSSO Associação Cultural
description: OSSO Associação Cultural is a collective that includes artists and researchers from various disciplines (Music, Dance, Fine Arts, Literature, Performance and Cinema). Since 2012, OSSO has developed transdisciplinary projects in collaboration with other artists and collectives, supported by partnerships with public and private institutions. Its experimental projects seek to explore artistic practices in conjunction with critical, aesthetic and political thinking that addresses the specificity of the contexts and territories in which it operates. OSSO is currently developing a project of Artistic Residences in the village of São Gregório, in the municipality of Caldas da Rainha, Portugal. This program comprises a range of artistic projects, research and programming activities in conjunction with local, national and international partners. This project aims to be a meeting point between artists and the public, actively dialoguing with the community through workshops, film screenings, concerts, performances, exhibitions, readings and any form of reflexive dialogue that involves, besides a creative community, a critical community. OSSO and its collective reinforce the interest in welcoming artists, national or international, whose practices are articulated with the notion of territory. The concept of territory is multifaceted and ambiguous. It relates to notions such as space and place, identity and community, dominion and control. It may refer to areas of land, but also areas of knowledge, activity or experience. In addition, territories inform identities, conditioning or generating values ​​between communities. They are in constant transformation, expansion and contraction, and thus generate new dimensions of convergence, conversion or conflict. Borders are places of tension and its movements are expressed by presenting the territory as a dynamic entity. Territories are also social constructs, products of agency that encompass physical, virtual, social, political, experiential and affective spaces.
studioInfo: THE STUDIO The studio, once a cellar, was recently refurbished to accommodate projects from various practices as dance, music, theatre or fine arts. This multipurpose space is catered to welcome small to medium scale projects. The studio has 60m2 (10m x 6m), a 4m lighting rig, and is equipped to welcome projects that require natural light as well as artificial (blackout). The studio is paved with a wooden floor which can be covered with linoleum (white or black) for projects in which such feature is key (eg: dance). THE WORKSHOP The workshop is composed of two different areas: Wood/iron and digital fabrication/electronic. The wood and iron area has 50m2 (11,5 x 4,5m) and 3,5m in height. It includes several worktables and a dedicated set equipment. The digital fabrication and electronic room has 9m2 and includes a worktable and a dedicated set of equipment.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation includes two double rooms, one single room, one kitchen / living room, a shared bathroom. The house faces an exterior patio and is surrounded by a small property with fruit trees and a threshing floor. Amenities include wi-fi reception, linen, towels, washing machine, and necessary kitchen appliances. The house also includes a fire extinguisher, a first aid kit, and bikes. 5 minutes can be hosted at once. Partners and kids are welcome – a bed and baby crib can be provided if required. The house, studio and workshop are cleaned once a week.
technicalInfo: For the realisation of their projects, residents may require continued support from the in-house technicians (audiovisual and workshop) as long as previously agreed and budgeted. However, at the beginning of each residence the organizers will ensure the presence of a technician to set up the technical rider or give any clarification on the requested equipment. STUDIO EQUIPMENT Video 1x video projector Optoma UHD 51 1x projection screen 2,21m x 1,28m [16:9 aspect] 1x HDMI cable (30m) Lighting 2x PAR projectors Drastic Light PAR 56 Short Black Round 300W [filament] 2x PAR projectors Varytec Event PAR IP65 4in1 14x8W [LED] 2x floodlights [work light] 1x profile spotlight ADB DW54 650W [filament] 1x DMX controller Stairville LED-Commander 16/2 2x dimmer BOTEX MPX-405 (4 Channel DMX Dimmer Pack) DMX cables Sound 1x mixing desk Mackie 1402-VLZ PRO 2x full-range speakers Mackie Thump 12 1x subwoofer the.box CL 112 Sub MK II 1x effects processor Lexicon MPX 500 1x graphic equalizer Behringer FBQ1502HD Ultragraph Pro 2x sound interface Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 1x sound interface Focusrite Scarlett 18i20 2x microphone stands (big), 2x microphone stands (small) 2x condenser microphones Oktava MK-012 (omni and cardiod capsules) 1x dynamic microphone AKG D321S, 1x dynamic microphone Sure SM58 2x nearfield monitors Prodipe Pro5 Bi-Amp Monitoring 1x headphones AKG K511 1x octophonic system, composed by: 4x amplifiers t.amp S-75 mk2, 8x JBL Control 1 PRO speakers, 8x transducers XLR, jack (TRS and TS) and RCA (DIN) cables Furniture 2x work tables (table and easels) [75cm x 140cm and 75cm x 200cm] application of linoleum flooring (exclusive for dance projects) WORKSHOP EQUIPMENT Wood / Iron Miter saw Jigsaw Circular saw Bandsaw Soldering machine Cutting table Sander Drilling machine Bench vise Power drill Screwdriver Angle grinder Compressor Digital Fabrication / Electronics 3D Printer (20cm x 20cm x 20cm) Soldering iron Single Board Computers (arduino e raspberrypi) Different sensors and actuators Laser cutting machine (210cm x 297cm) Oscilloscope Note: All the equipment listed in this document supports the residences that use the Studio and Workshop. Consumable materials are the resident’s responsibility.

name: Obras residencies
description: OBRAS is an independent, artist-run residency located on Herdade da Marmeleira near the village of Évoramonte in Portugal’s Alentejo region. The residency hosts a small number of international artists and researchers working across disciplines, including visual art, writing, music, film, architecture, performance, and research-based practices. The property has developed over generations and includes traditional Portuguese buildings, independent cottages, and working studios spread across the landscape. OBRAS was created to provide the conditions necessary for sustained artistic practice through time, space, and self-directed working environments. Programming remains intentionally minimal. Residents are given the freedom to determine the direction and pace of their stay, while opportunities for informal exchange take place through shared meals, conversations, artist talks, and twice-yearly open studios. OBRAS is an international artist residency offering artists and researchers time, space, and solitude. Located near the village of Évoramonte in Portugal’s Alentejo region, the residency exists to support sustained, self-directed work. OBRAS—a Portuguese word meaning work in progress—refers to the active state of making: work that is underway, evolving, unresolved. The residency is built around that condition, offering artists the space and time to focus on their work without prescribed outcomes or imposed programs. Each resident determines the direction and pace of their stay. The focus here is not on finishing something or producing a result, but on giving your work the attention it needs to develop. Residents live and work alongside a small international group while maintaining the independence necessary for concentrated practice. Surrounded by agricultural land and the marble quarries of the Alentejo, life here moves at a slower pace. The landscape becomes part of the rhythm of working. OBRAS exists to support serious work without pressure to produce or perform. The value of being here is not measured by what you complete, but by the quality of attention you are able to give. Practice is ongoing.
studioInfo: The studios at OBRAS are straightforward workspaces. Some are large and open. Others are smaller and more contained. Not every resident receives a separate studio. Spaces are assigned based on availability and the needs of the work. The rooms are simple: high ceilings, stone or cement floors, and natural light. There are no sinks or built-in technical infrastructure. Artists are expected to work within the limitations of the space. The land extends in every direction, and several defined exterior areas can be used for projects that need scale, air, or distance from walls. Some are structured by stone. Others are simply open ground. Wind, light, heat, and time of day become part of the conditions. Residents move between interior and exterior spaces depending on the needs of the work. There is no hierarchy between them.
accommodationInfo: Residents stay in private apartments or cottages located across the property. You will have your own living space and, if you wish, access to a separate studio. The spaces are simple and practical. Thick stone walls, tiled floors, and high ceilings help keep the interiors cool during the warmer months. Windows and doors open directly onto patios, gardens, and the surrounding countryside. Each apartment and cottage includes a small kitchen equipped with basic amenities: small refrigerator, cooking plate, microwave, coffee machine, electric kettle, and simple cookware. Water is from a private wells and is safe to drink. You are free to make the space your own, all they ask is that everything is returned to its original place before leaving.

name: AZAN contemporary art
description: AZAN residency program aims to welcome artists and introduce them to the Lisbon art scene with the feeling of a shared studio where artists can collaborate, share ideas and develop their work and research. Dialogue and experimentation are encouraged and projects related to the studio and its surroundings are welcomed. The key is to bring artists into a cultural context different from their own, in which they can thrive on cultural and social discourse and explore their own work, giving artists the opportunity to present their work and research. There are two formats to the residency program: living studio  (lodging and studio space) that can only accommodate one person at a time studio  (no accommodation, only studio space) Both residencies work by invitation or spontaneous application , subject to approval and availability.
studioInfo: Shared studio, kitchen and bathroom Informal and welcoming atmosphere Stays between 1 to 4 months; the applicant should indicate the preferred date of stay Studio Equipped with a table, chairs, a floor lamp and basic tools 30sqm 24/7 access to the studio + a fully equipped shared kitchen and shared bathroom
accommodationInfo: Living Studio Private bedroom with double bed Shared studio, kitchen and bathroom Informal and welcoming atmosphere The artistic lodging is best suited for artists, but curators, writers and filmmakers are also welcome to apply Stays between 1 to 6 month; the applicant should indicate the preferred date of stay; Maximum capacity: one person; AZAN has currently only 1 room for the residency Room 14 m2 Furnished (double bed, desk, closet, drawer dresser, bedside table) Air conditioner Sheets and towels included and change every 15 days; Cleaning every 15 days included Shared toilet and shower Access to a fully equipped shared kitchen with washing machine Extra services under request

name: Oficinas do Convento
description: The Artistic Residency Program is a project of promotion of artistic creation, centered in Art and Nature, which aims to explore an earth-connected knowledge, the construction of landscape and the traditional methods and techniques. The Residencies will occur in sites with a strong patrimonial and artistic value and should contribute to the rescue of materials and resources. They will be centered in Montemor-o-Novo, its historic and natural patrimony, and its inhabitants. The candidates can ask the Association for any information that can be used to the construction of their proposals.   Artist residency - The artistic have a place to sleep can use the toilets and kitchen, but needs to bring/buy his own materials, and can use tools Ceramica/Sculpture residency - paid residencies depending on the needs of the artist. Have to make the proposal so we can provide a cost estimation. Material and technical assistance provided.

name: Prisma Estúdio
description: Prisma is a volunteer-led and volunteer-operated cultural association in the most diverse quarter of central Lisbon (Martim Moniz). They are a collective of expert curators, cultural managers, and artists. The space exists to provide opportunities for emerging artists. Artists from various practices are invited to participate in the residency program. The program can host up to 5 artists at a time, they provide accommodation, a shared atelier space, access to support, and opportunities for collaboration with cultural actors in the city. The residency is run alongside an exhibition program and a schedule of cultural events in which residents are encouraged to participate and collaborate. The artists will be immersed in Lisbon’s vibrant underground artistic community, engaging in their eclectic program of events, schedule of exhibitions, and collaborating with community members. The residency welcomes artists and organizers from diverse practices and backgrounds, researchers, curators, and critics for 1-3 months. Either as a resident or for those already in Lisbon, a studio residency. They offer residents the possibility to explore techniques, concepts, ideas, and collaborations, to develop a final project. Throughout you will receive curatorial guidance and support from our welcoming community. For bookings exceeding three months or for emerging artists, please reach out to them for a reduced fee. At the end of the program, each resident will be offered the opportunity to exhibit their works in a final exhibition, publication, workshop, open studio, or performance in the gallery space in Prisma. The organisers are looking for community-minded participants, keen to become immersed in this project, who must be motivated and self-directed. This program is available to all cultural practitioners. You will make the most of this opportunity by spending time in the studio and participating in curation sessions. You are willing to engage and share knowledge through talks, seminars, workshops, or exhibitions. Here you can find more info for the 2027 Open Call .
studioInfo: Shared atelier space (70m2).
accommodationInfo: Artists-in-Residence will live in a shared apartment directly above the association with views of the castle. The apartment is fully furnished and shared spaces are cleaned weekly.

name: Hangar
description: The Residency program at Hangar encourages dialogue, exchange and experimentation. The program is non-prescriptive and process-based, allowing visiting artists to develop projects in response to their new environment, or to conduct research benefiting from Lisbon´s resources. The Residency Program is firmly established in the Lisbon art scene, promoting diverse cultures and practices through international and experimental projects. Hangar develops several International Residency Programs that give non-resident artists in Portugal or Lisbon the opportunity to live and work in Lisbon for a period of one month to three months (longer periods can be arranged.) The program aims to facilitate the international exchange and the exchange of ideas through artistic practice in the areas of visual arts, performance, photography and video. Through strategic partnerships in the international art world and institutions linked to cultural production and artistic research in various countries, mainly through the Triangle Network, Hangar program aims to strengthen the existing exchange between Portugal, Europe, Africa and South America. HANGAR is an Artistic Research Center, located in the area of Graça in Lisbon. HANGAR includes several platforms for action, including a center of artistic residences, studios for artists, an art education center, an exhibition and a public program. From the concept of unification of certain geographies, cultures and identities, HANGAR seeks to organize and produce the development of cross-disciplinary artistic projects in the Visual Arts, integrating public presentations and taking Lisbon as the focus of intervention. HANGAR is an independent space run by artists and curators. It is a place for experimentation, research and reflection on artistic practices. The space is a point of convergence of various areas of contemporary artistic processes. HANGAR aims to act as a catalyst of experience in the connection between artists, researchers and other artistic initiatives. It aims to encourage discussion of emerging contemporary art, stimulating the development of artistic and theoretical practices motivated by experimental and shared experiences.
studioInfo: No studio equipment is provided, but Hangar has some multimedia equipment to share and 24h hour wireless internet. There is a shared light-room (consumables not included). Hangar has contacts with organisations in Lisbon (photography darkrooms, video editing and print making facilities) that can provide equipment and services for visiting artists at reduced rates. Studios include basic furnishings (desk and chair). Access to office equipment (photocopiers, computers for email and internet) are available upon request during office hours.
accommodationInfo: Hangar offers 7 living and work studios for residency, 4 studios with private bathroom and kitchen facilities and 3 studios on a co-working shared format and shared kitchen facilities.

name: Duplex AIR
description: DUPLEX | Artists in Residence is an independent artist-run-space, composed of studios, a residency program and a gallery. Seeking to stimulate creative processes, experimentation and plastic production as well as the discourse that these dynamics originate, Duplex presents itself as a privileged territory for the coexistence of different artists, different productions and different ways of thinking about the work of art and its context. Valuing advances and setbacks, valuing error, failure, and disruption as participants in contemporary praxis, the entire structure and functioning of DUPLEX seeks, in addition to celebrate the final results, to recognize the conceptual and procedural richness of artistic creation, and bring the public closer to it. For resident artists, DUPLEX's artistic residency program allows a quick insertion in the artistic community of Lisbon, offering the possibility, time and space to develop and show their work. With guest visits, conversations, organized visits to studios or other art spaces, discussions and project support, Duplex seeks to adapt to the interests and needs of each group of residents, whom are expected to engage in the activities proposed during their time at DUPLEX. DUPLEX accepts self-proposals as well as publishes open calls. They are happy to receive artists working on any visual arts' area. They also receive curators as residents, usually coordinated with the current artistic residencies.
studioInfo: The DUPLEX building covers 1000 square meters and has three main floors. On the first floor, you'll find the gallery. The second floor houses 10 long-term studios for artists from Lisbon, as well as the office. On the third floor, there are 8 additional studios and a curator's office for the residency program. All the studios come with basic furniture, electrical outlets, and three walls that open to a shared social area. Each floor also has a small kitchen, bathrooms, places to clean art materials, and a terrace.
accommodationInfo: Duplex doesn't provide accommodation, but they will assist you in finding one through their network of cultural professionals that will be your hosts.
technicalInfo: Studios, a curator in residence office, a management office, fully equipped kitchenettes, bathrooms, terraces, communal gathering spaces, internet access, essential tools and materials, and a storage area for unused materials.

name: De Liceiras 18
description: DE LICEIRAS 18 is an experimental, independent, artist-run space located in an old residential house in the historical center of Porto, Portugal. Every month we host a group of international artists forming an ever-changing, dynamic temporary art community. It is run by the non-profit cultural association Eklipsefémero - Núcleo Artístico Independente. De Liceiras 18 is a monthly-based project, open for visual artists, designers, conceptual gardeners, experimental writers, sound hunters, improvisatory singers, performers, philosophers and (...) who would like to create in an old wood house in the centre of Porto. They welcome the creatives who are enthusiastic about spending one (or more) months within an exchange-based micro-art-community - learning, teaching, discussing and breaking any preconceptions; who are not afraid to erase barriers between private and public, to live and create in the same space; who are able to take inspiration from both possibilities and impossibilities, obstacles and miracles brought about by creating in such an informal, experimental, no-budget and anti-white-box space. Every month, DL18 hosts between 4 and 7 artists with diverse backgrounds, forming an ever-changing, dynamic temporary art community in the city of Porto.
studioInfo: Each participating artist receives their own simple habitable atelier. They have a little garden in the Musas community gardens that you are also welcome to use as a studio or a venue for your project.
accommodationInfo: The DE LICEIRAS 18 is located in a very old, two-story house in Porto, Portugal which seems to organically adapt to the form of the city itself, consisting of no perpendicular lines, with floors sloping and sounds of human and seagull daily life entering through wooden old windows, creating in the interior a constant quasi-musical blend of noises. The house is situated in a very particular place; although right in the middle of the city, its entrance stays hidden in a tiny bystreet, overlooked by tourists and bustling with local life. The everyday reality of the bystreet is even more curious due to a very particular combination of the house’s neighbours, formed of an old shoemaker's workshop, a motorcycle club and a traditional bar. The second façade of the house faces a brothel.

name: Zaratan - Arte Contemporânea
description: Zaratan – Arte Contemporânea is a not-for-profit space and an organization founded by artists in Lisbon city center in November 2014. Zaratan is a creation, production and promotion structure for contemporary art and a space of reflection and listening. In order to stimulate creativity and contribute to generate valid cultural processes, Zaratan has developed so far an heterogeneous and mostly free of charge agenda of events, that parallel to the regular schedule of exhibitions, presents video-projections, concerts, talks by artists, presentations and performances. Zaratan defends an interdisciplinary attitude and aims to promote a deeper comprehension of the artistic languages of the present with an independent structure. Artist In Residence programme Zaratan provides a private workspace, a creative and trilling artistic community, exhibition opportunities and professional development for international artists in Lisbon (Portugal). The artists-in-residence at Zaratan are given the opportunity to develop a project over a fixed period of time, and to reflect and consolidate their artistic practice. The goal is to give the artists the possibility to bring their work in an international context through exchange and collaboration within the local network. Eligibility Emerging and professional visual artists, performing artists, sound artist, curators and writers are eligible to apply. The residency program is designed for international or Portuguese artists residing abroad for the development of artistic projects, individual or collective. Zaratan defends a multidisciplinary and experimental attitude, where all the areas and the languages of the artistic expression are considered. Our goal is to mix experienced with emerging artists and give them the possibility to bring their work in an international context through exchange and collaboration within the local network. The artists-in-residence at Zaratan are given the opportunity to develop a project over a fixed period of time, and to reflect and consolidate their artistic practice. The artist or collective are required to undertake and carry out the research for a period ranging from a minimum of 4 weeks to a maximum of 12 weeks, Zaratan invites a variety of artists looking for diversity, across all mediums and disciplines, ranging from the emerging to the established. They promote a structure to focus, engage and work. During their stay in Lisbon, the selected artists will be required to meet on a regular basis with the curatorial team of Zaratan, who will also provide them with technical and organizational support for the entire duration of their research. Zaratan provides a flat with a private sleeping room and a private working studio on the top of the gallery, technical assistence, promotion/communication support and the possibility of an open public presentation of the residency process.
studioInfo: 2 private studios of 20 m2. A general purpose space of 40 m2 with a height of 8 meters in one side and 5 meters on the other side.
accommodationInfo: 2 private king-size beds.
technicalInfo: Basic working power tools, multimedia devices (printer, video-projector, audio and video recording devices).   Zaratan participates in the 2021 i-Portunus  EU Mobility Scheme for artists and cultural professionals.

name: Roundabout.Lx
description: Resident artists are invited to develop their own projects/artistic researches with autonomy, whilst benefitting from an environment of mutual exchange and collaboration. They accept artists and performers of all ages and stages of their practices. Roundabout.Lx is an urban open-plan studio in constant transformation, with the objective to adapt to the needs of each artist, allowing both exchange and privacy when needed. They have hosted up to 8 artists of different practices at the same time. When artists wish to show their work, Roundabout.Lx hosts open studio events, talks, performances and workshops. They are open to the public because they believe in the importance of exchange between international visiting artists and local artists. Roundabout.Lx's permanent resident Roug'Nough, is a publisher and a risograph printing house focused in artist books and small scale independent publications.
studioInfo: The studio used to be a timber yard, with a total shared area of 450 m2 and 5 m high ceilings, including a large common working area, a wooden movement floor, black and white dark room, tool workshop, mezzanines, desk areas, kitchen, toilet, shower, a small but very sunny and quiet outdoor area, wi-fi and access 24/7.
accommodationInfo: They currently do not have sleeping facilities in the space but do have a network of contacts through which they can help find affordable accommodation. They are open to host groups of maximum 6 people to live and work in the space for a minimum period of 2 weeks and a maximum period of 1 month between the months of May 2017 and September 2017.
technicalInfo: Darkroom

name: Buinho
description: Buinho was established in 2015 in the town of Messejana, with the status of a non-profit cultural association. It distinguishes itself by being the second MIT accredited fablab for the Alentejo region, and the only space with these characteristics in a rural area. The fablab provides access to a vast variety of digital manufacturing equipment as 3D printers, laser cutter, or CNC Mill, and the specialized support provided by our staff which enables visiting artists to further expand the boundaris of their artistic research. Buinho is more than just a fablab where private accommodation, working studios, Precious Plastic workspace and machine shop, and daily production support, all within a creative residency program are offered for artists and writers from different disciplines. The proximity of the residency program to the local community and local heritage is another of its distinguishing factors. Among other initiatives, Buinho offers a weekly cultural program promoted together with members of the local community. Opportunities for artists to engage with the organization's educational programs are also offered. All AIR residents have the possibility to organize an open studio event open to the general public. Buinho is the ideal place for those who want to adopt a more experimental attitude in their creative practice. The AIR program is designed and implemented by professionals with years of experience in cultural institutions and similar programs. Buinho AIR is a space of experimentation but also of social transformation, contributing to the increase of the attractiveness of rural territories.
studioInfo: Private accommodation with kitchen facilities (including fast speed internet connection, TV, kitchen utensils, washing machine, bed linen and towels, art and design library, drawing/design studio, wood, and metals workshop). Shared and private studios suitable for visual artists, designers, writers, etc. Working space (including internet connection, 3D Printers, Lasercutter, CNC, vinyl cutter plotters, woodworking power-tools, computer stations, projectors, easels, working tables, soldering iron for electronics, electric sewing machine). Precious Plastic workshop Support services for the development of the artist project involve free consultancy on production planning, and art & design resources, as well as dissemination of the project in Buinho’s website and organization of a public opening.
accommodationInfo: The creative residency program of Buinho provides private accommodation and shared work-spaces in two different locations: Sao Joao house is an XIX century shepherd’s house, remodelled in 2019 to offer a unique charm. It is located in the street of the museum, on top of a hill, offering from its garden a unique view over Messejana. It’s studios with high white walls and quiet environment offer the perfect setting for visual artists and writers. The second space, Buinho main studio, and fablab is also a traditional house, but was entirely renovated to provide a modern studio style residence. Here technologies give you a hand to experiment, learn and make. The fablab is equipped with all the necessary tools and machines (workstations, 3D printers, laser cutter, CNC, vinyl cutters, etc.) to enhance the possibilities of experimentation of our residents. Each house is fully-equipped and provide accommodation in individual rooms. They also provide some technical courses related to 3D Printing and laser cutting to the residents that may desire. Groups can be hosted. Partners and children are welcome.

name: School of Arts
description: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in partnership with the School of Arts will provide a residency to an international artist or curator to develop their work for a period of three months. The School of Arts of the Catholic University of Portugal is based in Porto and offers graduate and undergraduate courses in Film, Music, Sound, Photography, New Media, Heritage and Conservation. The selected candidate should be able to articulate/integrate the aforementioned research areas in the work to be developed during the residency. The selected artist is expected to engage in the activities of the School of Arts and be available to present their work processes to the students and in a public presentation, to be scheduled. The selected artist must also be available to be interviewed for research and communication purposes. The artist can freely set their working schedule, according to the availability of labs and materials that he might need, but he should be available to meet with the residency supervisors if it is requested in advance.
studioInfo: The School of Arts facilities include sound recording studios and equipment, editing rooms and filming equipment, a MoCap room, a Chroma Key studio, a fabrication lab, besides painting and sculpture studios.
accommodationInfo: Private apartment

name: Orto Creative Hub
description: Up to six residents are hosted at a time, joined by international volunteers who share a creative spirit, a commitment to ORTO’s ethos, and an affinity for nature. This coexistence creates a vibrant atmosphere of exchange - where spontaneous collaborations, skill-sharing, and friendships naturally emerge and continue beyond t he residency itself. In 2026, ORTO will further expand its programme of public workshops and talks, inviting local professionals from t he fields of philosophy, science, architecture, and the arts to engage wit h residents and the surrounding community. Through these encounters, ORTO aims to strengthen its role as a bridge between its inner life and the outside world - a place where ideas, people, and disciplines meet in dialogue.
studioInfo: Shared working studio (40 m²) adaptable to different practices (basic tools, shared equipment, ceramic wheel) Wood & metal workshop in the barn
accommodationInfo: Besides the main house, there are six private rooms (including two twin rooms for duos, partners, or families), and two shared bathrooms. Fully equipped common kitchen (20 m²) and communal dining area (30 m²) with a fireplace and a pizza oven. A welcoming patio with both shade and sun, full of vegetation. A perfect place for work, as well as for informal gatherings and late-night dinners. A tank with refreshing water adds more comfort during hot summer days.

name: Bucharest AiR
description: Bucharest Air functions as a non-profit organization, run and managed by artist Tudor Bratu; in 2021, the residency is shaped as a collaboration between Bucharest Air and Quote—Unquote. Bucharest Air aims at generating and maintaining a high-level platform for cultural exchange in Bucharest. Quote—Unquote is devised and developed by Infinite Conversation, an independent curatorial unit founded in Bucharest by Dan Angelescu, Irina Radu and Cristina Vasilescu. Quote—Unquote is in charge of all on-site residency related activities. These activities range from aiding and assisting residents in research, development, and production of work, to introducing and connecting residents to the Romanian art scene and to the city of Bucharest, as well as organizational activities related to the daily functioning of the Residency program. They are also engaged with the general further development of Bucharest Air, including the maintenance of the Residency network and content management. Tudor Bratu is in charge of fundraising and content-based exchanges with the residents. All four members of Bucharest Air participate in the selection procedure. Alumni of Bucharest Air are at times involved as advisers. Starting from 2012 and up until 2020, the residency's framework has been formulated together with artist duo Alice Gancevici & Remus Puscariu. Previous collaborations include artist Ioana Gheorghiu, between 2013-2015. Bucharest Air has developed a specific structure, which over time has become the customary way in which the residency collaborates with the resident artist throughout the duration of the residency. This general structure, which is outlined in the paragraph below, is subject to constant change and development, according to the specific needs of the resident. It is therefore by no means a fixed program, but one in constant development, to which the resident can contribute through specific questions and suggestions. Upon arrival in Bucharest, the resident is picked up at the airport or train station and is brought to the residency location, where all practicalities concerning housing, transportation, telephone, internet, and location are thoroughly discussed. During the first week of the residency, the resident is accompanied by the residency manager on a variety of trips through Bucharest, which have the aim of accustoming the resident to the city and its possibilities. After the first introductory week, the residency manager maintains regular contact with the resident, depending on particular and expressed needs: some residents prefer less contact, some prefer a closer working relationship, and these needs are always respected. Throughout the duration of the residency, the resident is invited to openings and events in Bucharest, and if so wished, also outside of Bucharest, during which the residency manager introduces the resident to the local art scene, different venues, colleague artists, curators, and critics. The residency manager also aids the resident in all aspects involved in the realization of specific projects. The Residency can host and collaborate with artists and other practitioners working primarily with new media and internet, performance, research-based work, video, and moving image practice, voice-based practice, lecture-performance, installation, site-specific (public space) interventions, and others, all relating to the layers, mechanisms, effects, and politics of language and voice. Bucharest Air is further open to collaborations with curators, critics, writers, anthropologists, alongside experimental filmmakers. They highly encourage transdisciplinarity through collaboration with fields of activity other than the artists’, in a process of understanding the ramifications of public speech in arts, society, cultural and political movements, mass media, and many other aspects. There are no age restrictions, and the residency is open to all nationalities equally. Projects and proposals which take into consideration the specific context of Romania will have priority over more generalist approaches.
studioInfo: Bucharest AiR has 2 locations. Bucharest Air choses the residency location considering availability and the resident artists' work or project-based necessities. The residency's locations are an 80 square meter ground level house, with a 500 square meter garden, located at the Eastern end of Bucharest, near the city of Voluntari as well as a 50 square meter apartment located near the city center.

name: The Romanian Association of Contemporary Art (ARAC)
description: The Romanian Association of Contemporary Art (ARAC) is a non-profit organization founded in June 2012, in order to produce and promote contemporary art in Romania and abroad. The team of ARAC supports and promotes contemporary Romanian artists by attracting funds in order to ensure financial resources – as part of ARAC's mission statement. An important objective of ARAC is to facilitate international cultural exchanges with artistic environments from other countries participating in festivals, fairs, residencies or any event that relates to contemporary art. ARAC is offering a residency opportunity for an artist to freely develop artworks for an exhibition in Bucharest. ARAC Art & Residency aims to introduce international artists and curators to the Romanian cultural environment. During its two-year programme starting in 2020, the project will feature artistic residencies, exhibitions, video & performance focused events and talks. The themes of this year’s residency and of the programme at large, are focused on climate change, migration and technology development. Applicants are invited to make project proposals on one of the three main themes. The residency is open to artists of any age, sex, race or nationality, working in any medium of contemporary art. The selection committee – a panel of contemporary art curators and artists – will review the applications and select the successful candidates in one session. The successful candidate is expected to reside and work in Bucharest for six weeks. At the end of the artistic residency period, the artist is expected to show the works produced during the residency in an exhibition at Anca Poterasu Gallery with the newly produced works.
accommodationInfo: Private accommodation in a 25m2 furnished room, with wifi, private bathroom and kitchen space.

name: U.N.A.G.E. IASI ART RESIDENCY
description: U.N.A.G.E. IASI ART RESIDENCY is focused on an intercultural exchange with international artists only from painting area. The main aim of Art Alpha Residency is to create various and complex events in Iasi, a cultural town with a lots of inspiration sources, to meet the local artists and the students from George Enescu Fine Arts University, to exchange ideas and to share experiences with them as for a future possible collaboration. The residency is organized by Ioana Palamar, Assistant Lecturer at George Enescu National University of Arts together with Lecturer Zamfira Birzu, Lecturer Cristian Ungureanu, Art critic Maria Bilasevschi and the support of volunteer students.
studioInfo: The artists-in-residence will work in the studios of the Faculty of Fine Arts and Design, together with the other students. They also have access to the library of the faculty, where they can use the computers and read the available art books. The faculty is located in Copou area, where transportation via bus and tram, small shops, coffee shops, supermarkets and restaurants are available.
accommodationInfo: The organizer will assist artists in finding accommodation in a flat. The accommodation room is private, but they might share the bathroom and the kitchen with the others.
technicalInfo: The residency artists can make an online research by using the computers of the university and they also have access to the books of the library.

name: BKF Residency
description: They offer the opportunity for a short term artist in residence program in Belgrade, Serbia and welcome all artistic disciplines and exchange of ideas between artists.
studioInfo: Separate apartment.

name: Casa de Creatie
description: Suceava Art Residency is a traditional Bukovina province ex-farm of 22,000 meters square that now is getting converted into an artist retreat. It is located in a quiet area of Suceava, that is the main city of Romanian Bukovina province and is run by members of Artfest Cultural Association (NGO) and Zidul de Hartie art group. It also works as cultural hub for local artists and writers and for small summer art projects and concerts. It is still a rustique place, near a forest. In the big garden there are growing all kind of fruit and forest trees. In the middle of it there is a lake where you can relax, work or get in touch with nature. The farm is still running partly, growing small parcels of organic vegetables, corn and potatoes and some chickens. You also can learn traditional ways of farming and gardening.
studioInfo: A large space as studio can be arranged in the old barn. Basic working tools are available there.
accommodationInfo: It can accommodate 3-4 guests at a time. In the main house you may stay in a two room apartment with kitchen, bathroom and terrace and in the fruit garden in a small new wood house with lake view (a room, bathroom, kitchenette and open terrace).

name: Footnote Centre for image and text
description: Footnote is an independent artist-run studio and art publishing initiative in Belgrade, Serbia. It is a space dedicated to experimentation, research and production in the field of visual arts and publishing. Their focus is on different and informal educational formats and collaborations between individual art workers, artist collectives and cultural institutions. Footnote offers a space and support for development of projects related to photography, moving image, visual essays, books, experimental publishing, installation and mixed-media. The facilitators at Footnote Centre have a combined experience in teaching at international art institutions and are committed to pursuing new models for creative studies based on critical insights, in-depth research and a genuine curiosity about the working of ideas, words and images. Open call The artist residency is aimed at multimedia practitioners at any stage of their career who want to spend a period of time living and working in Belgrade, Serbia. The Centre offers a calm place to live and work and a professional support in different areas of visual arts. The Centre has an in-house gallery, where the results of the residency research can be displayed, presented and discussed in various formats (exhibitions, talks, classes). Alternatively, they are able to provide connections to other art centres and galleries in Belgrade.
studioInfo: The house provides a space to work, learn, contemplate, and experiment. At residents’ disposal are desk spaces and a spacious area for presentations, temporary exhibitions or screenings. The house is covered with a fast Wi-Fi, and has all the essential facilities.
accommodationInfo: For the duration of the residency artists live and work in the house. Guests are offered a large private room with a balcony, a private toilet and a shared kitchen.
technicalInfo: The studio is equipped with digital printing facilities, bookbinding tools, as well as a variety of analogue and digital cameras and a studio lighting equipment. We are working towards expanding our production capacities towards adapting the basement and attic spaces into image and printing labs.

name: K.A.I.R. Košice Artist in Residence
description: International artist-in-residence program K.A.I.R. Košice Artist in Residence was implemented in 2011 as one of the key projects within the frame of “European Capital of Culture” by the NGO “Kosice 2013”. After the European Capital of Culture year, the NGO transformed to Creative Industry Košice, an organization, where K.A.I.R. had stable ground to develop the international activities and network of partners. In 2016, KAIR became an independent association. The residency program is for artists from all over the world and out of all artistic disciplines and expressions. K.A.I.R. gives them the possibility to work in the inspiring environment of Košice’s singular cultural surrounding to realize art projects, collaborate with the agile local art scene and present themselves to the local and national public. Media Arts Residency 2021 This specific residency seeks to create space for a media artist from one of the UNESCO Creative Cities to develop his/her own artistic project. The residency is an opportunity to create a new project or to continue work on something in development by shifting its perspective and embracing the open call’s topic. The open call is limited to the artists who are either born, live or work in any of UNESCO Creative City. The topic of the residency is determined as "Human Responsibility." In 2021, the residency program focuses on connecting individuals and sharing the responsibility to the world in the time of crisis. Artists can search for answers to questions: Is the current crisis causing a change in thinking and personal values? Or is it just temporary? What are the possible new or different forms of political and cultural group activities and coexistence? And how does the environment in which we live, including other living organisms, fit into this coexistence? How could the world slow down in the fight against the virus so that our society and economy respect our fragile ecosystems? What are the results and consequences of the process of moving between different places on Earth and beyond? How can the protection of human rights be ensured for all citizens? And what can we do to protect this and future generations? More information on this residency can be found on K.A.I.R.'s website.

name: Poton
description: Poton is an art and residency centre and a professional theatre group that operates in a small village of Batovce, Slovakia. Poton Theatre is the only Slovak professional theatre based in the countryside. It acts as a renowned organisation within the contemporary culture scene in Slovakia. In addition to its own productions, organisation offers its creative and inspirational space to other artists. The uniqueness of the space lies in its location - picturesque Slovak countryside, which offers many options for walking and wandering, beautiful sunsets and peaceful creative asylum for anyone. Centre of Arts and Creativity offers more than 1,500 m² of work space for artists and complete sound, light and projection equipment. During the calendar year, centre provides work space and accomodation for approximately 20 residential groups - for more than 80 artists. When selecting residents, the residency center team focuses mainly on visual art, site-specific projects, new media and performing arts, including contemporary dance and physical theater, but also on music projects and literature. Both emerging and established artists are welcome. Since 2015, it has also provided working space for art theorists. Centre has been providing residencies since 2008. More than 1,250 artists from Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, England, Romania, Argentina, Palestine, Israel, Ukraine, France, Russia, Poland, Germany, Iran have worked on new works in Bátovce. Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iceland and Mexico.
studioInfo: Residents have a choice of two options for working spaces - a large Theatre hall or a smaller Studio. The Theatre hall is designed as a classic theatre hall with a stage, space for an auditorium (without elevation), a balcony and stage background. Above the playing area there are traverses with a load capacity of 500 kg with a lights. There is a mobile elevation with height levels from 20cm to 70cm. The whole space is black. Dimensions of the hall: width: 9m, depth: 18m, height: 9m. The Studio space is mainly intended for smaller productions, seminars, discussions and work meetings. It has a maximum capacity of 50 people. For workshops and trainings, the maximum capacity is 10 people. The space is multifunctional with the possibility of projections on one of the walls. Black balletizol is placed on the floor. The studio provides blackout curtains. Dimensions of the studio: width: 5m, depth: 10m, height: 3m.
accommodationInfo: Residencies take place in the building of the Centre of Arts and Creativity in the quiet rural environment of the village of Bátovce in Slovakia. Residents' rooms and workspaces are located in the same building. There are single rooms, double rooms and triple room. The rooms are equipped with sanitary facilities (toilet, shower). There is a WIFI connection throughout the building. The center is equipped with a kitchen for preparing meals. There is a food delivery service and a supermarket in the village. In the wider area there are several tourist attractions (history, architecture, spas, swimming pools, shopping) –town Banská Štiavnica (30 km), town Levice (16 km), town Nitra (60 km), swimming pool Santovka (13 km), Dudince spa (25 km). The capital city of Slovakia - Bratislava - is 163 km away.
technicalInfo: The centre has extensive light, sound and projection equipment. The residents are instructed about the use of technical equipment in the beginning of the residency. If necessary, they can provide an external technician for longer assistance.

name: Krusce Creative Center
description: Krušče Creative Center is a creative property in the hills of Slovenia developing into a small art village where art is being created, shown and discussed. Its mission is to support, nurture and provide space for creation, research, education and residency, while encouraging connection between artists and creatives from different professions. Krušče Creative Center is a place of meaningful encounters with rarely combined worlds and perspectives, a space of inter-professional, inter-generational, inter-local and inter-national bridgings. Its regular activities include also research and educational programs in psychodrama and psychotherapy, as well as pedagogy and other fields that include group work. An important part of Krušče's program is a series of little festivals SPACES, BODIES, CURRENTS and WORLDS and Krušče Little Festival of Psychodrama - five days creative/educational/research retreats that explore creation of temporary communities through experiential workshops, lectures, talks and sharing art in a new context. Krušče Creative Center nurtures hospitality and long term collaborations. Guests are treated as friends and most of them return to continue to be part of centre's activities. GENERAL RESIDENCY is an artistic residency for creatives from different fields. The program offers artists space and time to focus exclusively on their work and creative process, with the possibility of an exchange through encounters with the group of co-residents that is being created in which different perspectives, ways of working and presumptions can be questioned and reflected. Krušče creative center is located in a remote natural setting where creative isolation is possible. One can dedicate one's time to be involved in the process of reflection, training/preparation, research or creation. Sometimes the most important and necessary thing is to stop: to drop all expectation and pressure to do, produce or create. Krušče is also a place for that. The general residency is an open/empty space and the center doesn’t structure time and work for the residents. It offers accommodation, working space and food (two meals from local organic ingredients). With enough residents present and interested it also offers curated artistic events, artistic coaching/mentorship, workshops/classes etc. The participation in these activities is voluntary.
studioInfo: “Studio” is a house where the studio is located. It’s on the ground floor, size 6x10 m and is also used as a performing space. It has a little library, sound system, projector and a screen, possibility for theatre lights to be hanged and comfy sofas. Ajoining the studio is a small/tea kitchen with all the necessary equipment to prepare food and a bathroom. The upper floor 12x8 m is a loft that can comfortably accommodate up to four people. It has a big working table, a hammock and a home library. The house is heated with a fire place (wood pallets). In the summertime there are plenty of possibilities to work outside in the natural setting (fruit orchard, grass fields, nearby forest) and especially in the open barn (6x12 m). Creative work is possible also at the little club, ground floor apartment and the kitchen of the big house.
accommodationInfo: “The little house” is the residency house. The house with funky wallpaper. It can host up to 12 people. Ground floor has two private “booths” for sleeping (french size bed in each), two toilets and a bathroom with two showers. Second floor has a fully equiped kitchen and a bedroom with kingsize bed and ajoining private bathroom. Both kitchen and bedroom have an exit to a balcony. The attic has 8 single beds and a balcony under the old chesnut tree. The house is heated with IR electric panels. “The big house” is the heart of the property. The ground floor has a big communal kitchen where everyone can meet, cook, eat and hang out. The central corridor was made into a tiny club with a little stage where concerts, performances, exhibitions or other events can be held. There is also a studio appartement on the ground floor. It can accommodate two adults and two kids. Apartment 10x5 m has a private bathroom and is suitable for longer residencies. It is big enough to do creative work such as writing, composing, preparing/researching for a project etc. The basement of the house has a boiler room, laundry room, a toilet, a shower room and a little spa consisting of steam sauna and a bath/pool. "The barn" is a summer workshop and performance space. Krušče Creative Center is a family friendly residency providing a crib for babies, high chair for toddlers, toys, children's books and lots of dynamic playground area all around the property.
technicalInfo: Every house has its own internet connection. The Studio has special floor that is suited for movement work. Sound system at the Studio (can be also moved outside to the barn). Gramophone. Possibility of using basic theatre lighting. Projector and a screen (located in the studio, but can be moved around). General tools. Lots of old materials from the houses (old metal and wood, remains of the old furniture, old machinery…).

name: Visegrad Artist Residency Programs (VARP)
description: Visegard provides various mobility opportunities consisting of exchanges, scholarships and residencies. The organization runs three different residency programs in visual and sound arts performing arts literature and journalism. Calls for each discipline are featured under the mobility division of their website.
studioInfo: This depends on the host organization.
accommodationInfo: Provided by host organization (mandatory and in the contract). Partners & family might be eligible, but it depends on the host organization (Visegrad Fund does not financially support partners and family of artists).

name: Instinc
description: As an independent artist-run space, INSTINC strives to sustain artistic independence and foster a vibrant community through inventive and daring partnerships. INSTINC encourages the exchange of creative practice among professionals in contemporary art through local and international collaborations. It aims to establish a platform where artists engage with the public through its exhibitions, workshops, artist-talks, and the renowned AIR program. INSTINC Collaborative Residency: INSTINC seeks for artists/creative individuals whose work embodies clear conceptual ideas and innovative approaches that resonate deeply with the contemporary cultural landscape. Initiated by Singaporean artist and INSTINC founder Shih Yun Yeo, this AIR program has served as the nurturing ground for artists from various backgrounds. Over the years, INSTINC has been a proud host to over 120 international artists between 2009 and now; celebrating the synergy born from internal collaborations among like-minded creatives.
studioInfo: Studio shared between you and another residing artist: Located in a prime site just beside PIE and Bukit Batok East Avenue 3, this studio offers a suitable environment for creators to focus on their production.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation will not be provided by the host.
technicalInfo: Printmaking Press, bathroom within studio, good light, huge windows, tables, easels, DIY Hardware Store nearby, easily accessible food at the 2nd floor.

name: Dear Human Ranch AIR
description: Dear Human is the visual arts and design collaborative formed by Jasna Sokolovic and Noel O’Connell in 2010. Jasna Sokolovic studied architecture at the University of Sarajevo and at the University of Belgrade in former Yugoslavia before immigrating to Canada during the war. She completed her studies in fine arts at Emily Carr University in Vancouver, British Columbia. Noel O’Connell is a graduate of the University of Wisconsin, Madison and holds an MFA from Rhode Island School of Design. He is a Fulbright scholar in art and architecture and spent six years studying and working in art restoration and ceramics in Thailand and China. Dear Human Ranch AIR is a creative space for artists, guests and friends to play with possibilities and materialize ideas. It is also an invitation to explore the ecosystem of the local meadows, forests and surrounding mountains. They welcome emerging and established artists from all disciplines to develop their projects on the ranch. Residents here can be focused on research and/or production as they so choose. All residencies are self-catered and self- directed. The Ranch gives you the chance to absorb both the natural environment and a creative atmosphere in perfect balance, to be rejuvenated and inspired without the distraction and pressures of daily life.
studioInfo: The studio is about 30m2, equipped with a brand new kiln (low fire), wood stove for heating in the winter, and a CNC machine for wood and other projects. It also has the most picturesque view on to the neighbouring hill.
accommodationInfo: The residency is located between three mountains, each beautiful in its own way. Hikes are just on the doorstep, and in just 15-30 minutes drive in any direction there are lakes, good restaurants and many well-known local attractions. The artists in residence will have sole use of the cabin, shared studio and also, can work outdoors if weather permits. The cabin has a living room, kitchen and a bathroom on the lower level and 2 ½ small rooms on the upper. One room has a double bed and another has a single bed. Additionally, there is a small open space that can be used as a writing/drawing room.

name: Tobačna 001 Cultural Center
description: Tobačna 001 is a new cultural center (part of Museum and Galleries of Ljubljana) that includes an art gallery, a museum collection, a studio and an apartment intended for artist-in-residence. Residency programme which operates from April 2011 and hosts international visual artists is independent and flexible: artists, by participating in lectures, presentations and workshops, merge with the local scene while also having time to focus on their own creative practice within a different cultural environment. The artist-in-residence programme emphasizes the significance of a multi-layered cultural exchange and the artist's integration into the urban and social environment of Ljubljana. Artists have the opportunity to make new contacts at gatherings and social events such as exhibition openings, time to explore and work on their project, and the opportunity to show their project formulated during the residency period.
studioInfo: Curator and artist shared space for working
accommodationInfo: private apartment

name: AiR Celeia
description: The AIR Celeia programme has been up and running since 2005. The programme encourages the development and promotion of the contemporary artistic and curatorial practices and is based on open dialogue, exchange and cooperation. It is conceived as a two-month residency for international artists and curators. The residency comes with a fee to the artist, space and time, as well as other structural conditions for artists to take on in-depth research, to develop and implement projects, on their own or in a group. It acquaints and connects its residents with local artistic goings-on, as well as those further afield. AIR Celeia residents have the opportunity to present their work in an exhibition venue run by the Centre for Contemporary Arts, which can take the form of a lecture, discussion, performance or exhibition. Selections are based on open calls and invitations.
accommodationInfo: A residential apartment (80 m2) is located in the old town centre of Celje, in the Art Quarter, a stone’s throw away from the Centre for Contemporary Art. The apartment is furnished, has access to a wireless internet connection, and comes with an available parking space.

name: Arte Utile (AU) Residence
description: raum AU is a physical and mental entity that as a potential public institution presents an appropriate addition to any urban environment – to coordinate the cities non-governmental production and to support active citizenship. Within the Arte Utile residency we try to activate the cultural heritage of Arte Utile by offering it to be discussed, researched, analysed and debated. Young theoreticians and artists are welcome to enter the artists archives. The AU residency can be a simple residency, where young artists can experiment their own AU arguments, but can be extended to a proper study of an artists opus and with that materials, that usually are left open, undone and never executed. Young, curious and open artists of every corner of the world are welcome to study the ideas of Arte Utile and to work in our social environment, a tiny city next to the Austrian border.
accommodationInfo: The apartment consists of one room (25 qm) and one bathroom (5 qm) with shower, toilette and bidet. Possibilities to cook are available at the raum AU, Bistros, Cafes and a bakery are at 2-3minutes walk, be it from the apartment or the raum AU. They host 1 resident at once. Artist-couples can be accommodated, if they share the same bed (additional fees apply).
technicalInfo: Basic technical equipment (you have the right to use the equipment when available): 1 video-projector, 3 dvd players, 1 loudspeakers, 2 small color TV-sets, 1 scanner up to A3, digitalizing equipment for VHS, Audiocasettes and Audio-CDs, Printer A4. Basic tools like hammer, saw, screwdriver, monkey wrench, screws, bulbs and lighting, white wall painting, roller are available. The central setting of the place make the other amenities accessible.

name: KUD
description: It has been developing its own painting, sculpture, video and theatre production within Autonomous Cultural Centre Metelkova mesto ever since. The association also organizes cultural events. It organizes youth program and informal education activities as well as the exhibitions in Gallery Alkatraz. It also collaborates with local artists in the Urban Art Projects. KUD Mreža is also fundraising for many other projects and maintains the ACC Metelkova mesto audio, video and print documentation archive. Since 2000, KUD Mreža has been organising Red Dawns, an annual feminist and queer arts festival. Association KUD Mreža welcomes new collaboration suggestions! We provide practical help to inexperienced event organisers and offer fundraising help to emerging artists. Since 2000, KUD Mreža obtains the status of an association working for the public interest in the field of culture.
studioInfo: The studio has an area of 40m2 which includes working and living area separated by a glass wall. It has basic furniture: a bed, tables, chares, closets, a refrigerator and a electric heater. On the same floor is a kitchen, a toilet and a shower, which are used by five studios (Studio Asylum, three art studios and A-Infoshop). There is an internet access. Basic tolls are also available.

name: GuestRoomMaribor
description: The GuestRoomMaribor residency programme invites visual and interdisciplinary artists to apply for artist residencies that will take place in Maribor (Slovenia) in the period of 2022 and 2023. Several dates are available for one-month honorary residencies in spacious apartment studios of Vetrinjski mansion in the centre of Maribor. Successful applicants will also get an opportunity to present their newly created work in their gallery space. GuestRoomMaribor is Maribor-based programme established by NGO Pekarna Magdalenske mreže  that has been offering residencies for Slovenian and international artists in Maribor since 2011. They focus on contemporary visual art practices while their programe mainly supports socially engaged, hybrid and experimental projects, as well as projects that relate to the local social, cultural, historical or political context. The aim of the programe is to open up creative processes, foster dialogue and direct contact with local communities, question established presentations of artworks and encourage collaboration with local artists and producers. In terms of content, priority will be given to projects that: (self) critically reflect the involvement of contemporary art in social, economic, technological, and environmental processes and power relations try to suggest non-normative ways of acting and thinking about the social and/or natural phenomena, including the artistic ones are research-oriented or understand the research process as an integral part of the artistic-creative process without reducing the latter to the research of the artistic medium or the visualization of data establish a reflective attitude towards the environment in which they are placed; in this case with the specific social, cultural, historical, or political context of the local community respond to the space in which they are placed in the process of creating or presenting the project.
studioInfo: Separate studio.
accommodationInfo: Free accommodation in central studio apartment (area 96 m2 and 76 m2, each of the studio apartments has a kitchenette and bathroom, floor heating, air conditioning, internet and a shared laundry room).

name: Center Rog
description: Center Rog Creative Hub is excited to announce the Designer in Residency Programme 2026 with this year’s topic: More Than Us. They are inviting designers, innovators, craftspeople, and makers from diverse backgrounds to explore the relationships with non-human agents — from AI to animals, plants, and other living systems — and to translate these insights into products that respond to the needs of a wider biological community. This 3,5-month residency offers an opportunity to engage with critical global topics while fostering creative responses through design.
studioInfo: The Rog factory, a symbol of the iconic Rog bicycles, is the most important piece of 20th-century industrial heritage in Ljubljana’s city centre. Thanks to both the way it was restored and the plans for its future use, the building retains its original function, updated for the 21st century: serving as a public production space for the cultural and creative industries, with an emphasis on design, architecture, engineering, craft, and applied arts. On the ground floor, there are nine production labs (workshops) equipped with both modern computer-aided technologies and traditional workshop equipment. Each lab has a lab manager and a team of qualified technologists who help users develop their projects. The list of all labs with their available equipment can be found here: https://center-rog.si/en/space/labs/.
accommodationInfo: Center Rog has 5 residential apartments, located on the third floor of Center Rog, measuring from 50 to 80 m2. Each apartment is equipped with a living room / workspace, kitchen, bathroom, separate bedroom and comes fully furnished. One of the apartments is bigger in size and thus intended for families, collectives, and a wheel-chair accessible bathroom.

name: Tankwa Artscape
description: Tankwa Artscape is an artist residency in the desert focusing on an artistic relationship with the desolate landscape and creating from there. Concept of the residency: Imagine a desert floor, undisturbed by human traffic. It’s not the absence of life that is so dramatically visual.
