It is a few million years old retrospective of ancient seabed and cataclysmic geological events in Earth history, and the footprint of storms and water flow in the riverbeds. Vast pans nudge aside scrub and vlei and gentle hills and land, which drop outside of the quick glance, towards a perimeter of deep-set mountain horizon. Across some of the expanse of tight scrub and dark flatland there is a bicycle track that may have traversed this space anytime between two weeks and twenty years ago; a rut has embedded itself into spongy soil between the rocks. Weathering has deepened the impression, the impact from which erosion has begun. You could say it defines the beginnings of consciousness, that bicycle track. It represents a challenge that will always be here: to what extent should this kind of impact be acceptable. And where is the compromise? As an artist - how to respond to this landscape in a way that pays respect to the unique desert aesthetic? The original ‘gate-keepers’ of the land here lived light on the ground. Who should be the present and future ‘curators’ of this landscape, and what responsibility comes with that curation? It is the artist who is able to leave another kind of impression, a way of seeing that can affect the conscious gaze of anyone passing or experiencing their work. In the end, if the art is offered with the right intention, the aim of this project has been fulfilled. Considering what is the ‘right intention’ is where the work begins.
studioInfo: The desert is the studio. The "Brakdak" is the workshop.
accommodationInfo: Tented camp in the Tankwa desert.
technicalInfo: No electricity, generator available.

name: Space Between A-I-R
description: Space Between aims to promote artwork by new emerging artists and those inspired by popular culture.Painters & illustrators; un circulated artists inspired by street culture and those with unique voices and practices are shown in the gallery. Space Between offers an Artist's In Residence program for visiting artists to Cape Town. The program offers the opportunity for artists to work on an exhibition proposal during their stay, liaise and collaborate with other local artists as well as contribute to the careers of emerging artists. The program is open to international and local graduate students, emerging and established artists, designers, creatives and curators. Those with practices rooted in street art and underground visual art’s culture; illustrators; installation artists; 3 Dimensional artists or painters are encouraged to take part in the program. A willingness to collaborate with local participants, artists, organizations as well as press is expected.
studioInfo: Sole use of a 21 m2 studio work space for the duration of your stay.
accommodationInfo: Assistance finding accommodation near the Space Between Gallery.
technicalInfo: 136 sqm gallery space. You should bring your own basic working equipment.

name: Oaklands Farm
description: Oaklands Artist in Residence is an artist-run residency program aimed at facilitating a unique and focussed working environment in the mountains 90km from Cape Town. OaklandsAiR offers an idyllic location for the conception, creation and completion of creative projects. The residency caters to fine art, landscape architecture, writing and research across all fields of study. Residents live and work on Oaklands Farm which is located in the mountains on the edge of the Limietberg World Heritage Site. Oaklands Farm is home to unique biodiversity, amazing walking routes and a refreshing rural environment in the heart of the Cape Floral Kingdom. The residency offers: - a private room in a residency cottage, shared with another artist. The rooms are spacious, and the artists share a common living room and fully equipped kitchen. - a private studio in the foaling barn. - a possibility to use the library and extra equipment at the Oaklands premises; - contact with the coordinator to provide local support and access to the local network; - a cultural program to explore the local art scene in Capetown.
studioInfo: The studios are located within the foaling barn. There is the option of a private or shared studio within this communal space. Large sliding doors separate the studios from the central passage. OaklandsAiR will work with the artist in residence to equip the studio for their needs. The studios have good natural light, ample wall space, a water source, internet connectivity and an electrical point. The foaling barn is equipped with an etching press. Artists are invited to access the network of creative practitioners in Wellington should they wish to use a ceramic kiln, lithographic press or screen printing workshop- all transport to and from Wellington must be coordinated with the AiR coordinator. OaklandsAiR welcomes research and experimental practices that are close to nature. There is space for traditional kilns to be built on the property, there is wild clay and there is an abundance of material available for natural dying and other nature focussed experimental practices. The studios can be equipped with a comfortable chair and desk should the artist in residence be focussed on writing and research.
accommodationInfo: OaklandsAiR is a rustic residency experience located on a family farm. Artists in residence are accommodated in one of the self catering residency cottages only 200m from the studios. Resident artists can also enjoy access to Vygie kitchen and dining room, a restaurant that is located in the barn next to the studios. The residency cottage is equipped full amenities: kitchen, hot water, WiFi. Bed sheets and towels are provided, as are basic kitchen necessities and appliances. Through simplicity and style, the cottage reflects on its surroundings and works with the natural landscape.

name: META foundation
description: In 2020, the META foundation was founded as a non-profit organisation to provide programming to August House. As such, the residency programme falls under the ambit of the META foundation. Fifteen years ago, when everyone was leaving the city, artists started moving into August House and making it their own. With a fascinating history in both the art world and real estate, August House is a sought after artist community in the city, with its gritty, stimulating surrounds that keep artists and visitors alike engaged with the urban vibes of Johannesburg’s inner world. The artists in August House, work across mediums and disciplines and are a mixture of well-known and emerging artists. With space for more than 50 artists, August House accommodates one of the largest contemporary African fine art communities in South Africa. August House Partially-funded Residency 2022 META foundation is calling for artists, creatives, or collectives looking to take up studio space in one of the largest buildings in South Africa, August House Studios, also known as the artists’ playground. The Partially-funded Residency Program is a 3-month program wherein the participant would be located at End Street Studios located on the 2nd floor of August House. We have 3 studios that we offer on rotation for residencies within the End Street studio space. Of course, there is a booking schedule for these and as such, it depends on when the artist wants to come. •   The residency period is 3 months long. The residency apartment will be available after 30 April 2022. Should applicants choose to come before this time, they may have to find alternative accommodations. •   The residency provides for a studio space and furnished accommodation within August House. •   The residency does NOT provide for transport, living, medical or material costs. •   There is uncapped internet in the building. •   A parking space will be provided. •   The artist is expected to contribute to the cost of the program, albeit a substantially reduced amount from renting space in August House. • A deposit is required 2 months in advance of attending or unless negotiated with the META foundation Director. •   During the residency, the artists are welcome to participate in any activities or events taking place at August House. The artist is provided with their own set of keys and is free to come and go as they see fit.
studioInfo: Studio 6 - 28 sqm in size Studio 7 - 50 sqm in size
accommodationInfo: The equipped residency apartment is located on the 1st floor of August House. The accommodation is a bachelor unit. It includes the following: • a bed and bedding • fridge • small stovetop/oven combo • microwave • kettle • crockery and cutlery • a heater • internet There is no washing machine or TV located in the space.

name: Driftwood Studios
description: Driftwood Studios is a small family residency where you will have private workspaces to develop be it in wood, metal, stone or ceramic media. They have also hosted writers and photographers. The Studio/Gallery is also big enough for drama workshops. Yoga, mindfulness and meditation classes are held regularly. Book an adventure nature walk down the hill on our beach. There is a canoe safari for birders, where you could easily spot all five species of kingfishers, a host of raptors, dolphins and whales. After a tough day doing art, treat yourself to very affordable massage therapy on-site. There is a network of artists and crafters, galleries and museums in the area that the organisers would share. The incredible bushman rock art can be visited with their local expert guide. Driftwood is in the village of Rainbow Valley, adjacent to a pristine coastal dune forest and a few minutes walk to the sea. The beach has dramatic sand dunes, beautiful stones and of course driftwood to inspire and refresh all visitors. There are good local shops 5km away, including a supermarket, butchery, pharmacy, eateries, a fuel stop etc. and the city of East London is 20km. Facilities and services inclusive of this price are, but not restricted to: En-suite bedroom with patio doors onto deck or paved area. Own kitchen, or shared if desired. For each artist a private workstation is provided with task lighting and drawing board or easel, whatever the artist requires. A workspace can also be set up in the main studio. Access to a variety of free/low-cost materials. There are beautiful driftwood and beach stones that can be utilized to a degree. However, you will need to purchase other art materials. Just ask and they can usually help source it for you at a preferential rate from local suppliers. Personal laundry and change of bedding & towels approximately weekly. There’s no TV but books and a hard drive of movies is available plus regular Netflix movie nights. WIFI throughout, sufficient for email, research etc. Airport/bus/train transfers to/from East London at the beginning and end of the stay if required. Transportation weekly to East London to places of interest, plus more regular trips to the local shops for those without own transport. Orientation of the area, from stunning beaches to local art suppliers, as well as the resources/equipment and skills at Driftwood Studios, focusing on your needs and interests. Community contact through a presentation of your work on a Friday before departure, usually for stays of at least 3 weeks. A quality image of artworks can be taken on their infinity curve. You provide assistance with food and a few bottles of wine and they will promote and organize it, including a slot with the local radio station. Driftwood has a woodwork room, pottery studio, forge and studio spaces for artists and the spacious Gallery. Fresh wholesome and sustainable food is a passion at Driftwood and they grow fruits such as bananas, protected as best they can from the forest monkeys (!), and their own salad vegetables and herbs. Enjoy free-range eggs from their own ‘happy hens’. Residents are asked to recycle and contribute organics to the garden compost. Driftwood Studios is an art studio facility developed and run by sculptor George Kockott’s wife Claire. Tragically George passed away in 2019. There is a display of his sculptures in the Gallery. Of course, George’s skill and influence are to be felt in all the spaces he built and created. Claire continues to run the residencies and live with their two teenage children in Driftwood House next to the Gallery.
studioInfo: Driftwood Studios has a woodwork room, pottery studio, forge and studio spaces for artists and the spacious Gallery, as well as workspaces in each unit, are set up to residents' requirements.
accommodationInfo: There are two self-catering units: 2-bedroom Forest House and 1-bedroom Driftwood Treehouse. Forest has a queen & single bed in the main bedroom and in the smaller bedroom there's a double bed. Both rooms are shower en-suite and share a kitchen and utility room. Driftwood Treehouse is one bedroom with a kitchen/diner, bath, and beach shower. Or stay in the spacious en-suite in Driftwood House which has its own entrance. Share the family kitchen and have dinner included.

name: Naughty Muse Studios
description: Naughty Muse Studios is an international art residency and creative co-working space based in Busan, South Korea. Naughty Muse Studios is run by international creators living in Busan. It aims to promote diversity in the region, bridge the gap between domestic and foreign artists, and showcase Busan’s unique culture and arts to creators worldwide. Established with after completing the government’s Oasis-visa project, which fosters innovative ideas and talent among foreign entrepreneurs, Naughty Muse Studios opened in July 2023. Since then, it has been running an international art residency program, organized and hosted numerous events and workshops, including artists networking events that brought together domestic and international artists, group exhibitions featuring artists from different countries and participated in city-run festivals. The residency program #getinspiredinbusan run by Naughty Muse Studios provides an opportunity for a self-directed creative experience that honors creative integrity. They trust individuals to know what they need in order to cultivate their individual talent, whether it’s to work, to experiment, or to simply rejuvenate. During the residency period we organize visits to exhibitions in Busan and other cities in South Korea, visit local artists's studios and cultural events as well as historical sites. Workshops with local craftsmen, critiques, exhibitions and other activities may be organized upon request.
accommodationInfo: Residents are provided with individual self-contained studio apartments. Located in the iconic Haeundae area, known for its beautiful beach, luxury hotels, and bustling nightlife. The purpose of this program is to introduce Busan to new and diverse perspectives, enrich community through dialogue, and to create deeper, more meaningful connections with each other through art, but most importantly is to showcase this beautiful place to a wider audience. For this purpose we have intentionally chosen to separate living spaces from the working space, hoping that it will stimulate the artists to walk around, discover hidden gems and fall in love with Busan as they did.
technicalInfo: Each resident is provided with their own working area within a shared studio space. A variety of tools and facilities, such as an etching press and silk screen facilities are also included. The number of residents at Naughty Muse Studios is intentionally kept low (4-6 people).

name: Gyeonggi Creation Center
description: Gyeonggi Creation Center (GCC) is an art sponsorship organization to support creative activities and researches by domestic and overseas artists. With a variety of facilities such artists’ studios, art and crafts workshops, artwork storage, a theater and a number of multi-purpose halls, GCC hosts exhibitions and open-studio events, community based art programs, art education, and international exchange programs. GCC acts as a platform to gather artists, curators and theorists from all over the world for international exchange and as an experimental and progressive contemporary art center to collectively engage and cultivate synergy among artists of various genres. For the Residency Studio Program, GCC selects resident artists through invitations and open applications from artists, curators, and theorists working in visual and media arts. Programs: Creative Residency Program : Artists in visual art, Design, Architecture, literature, Dance, Performing Arts, and media arts Research Residency Program : Independent and alternative space curators, producers for theater and music, researchers and critics.
studioInfo: Provision of individual studio (1 room for 1 person/team) combined with accommodation.
technicalInfo: Provision of joint creation space (media lab, carpentry room, archive space).

name: Africa Centre
description: This AiR programme has been designed to support and celebrate the achievements of artists from Africa who are provocative, innovative and highly engaged, both with social issues and their art forms. AIR partners with existing artist in residency programmes around the globe to award exceptional African artists with the opportunity to take up a short-term residency to focus on consolidating their work and developing new projects. Each residency partner selects one artist from a shortlist provided by the Africa Centre, following a continent-wide call for submissions. The costs of the residency and a round-trip airfare are included in each award. The residencies are available to all forms of artistic expression and types of artists, but each residency differs in terms of duration, structure and requirements. Since its inception in 2011, AIR has funded many African artists to attend residencies in Australia, Brazil, Ethiopia, Finland, Italy, Korea, the Netherlands, South Africa, Spain, Turkey, and the USA.
accommodationInfo: Studio and accommodation is provided in the partner residency centre.

name: Bodhi Khaya Residency
description: Bodhi Khaya Residency is an annual two-week, funded, artist-founded, artist-led and process-oriented residency. It was initiated by a small group of artist friends who, after being accepted into international residencies, recognized a lack of similar opportunities within the South African arts landscape. In response, they established the residency in 2021. Artists at Bodhi Khaya residency immerse themselves on three neighbouring nature reserves, Bodhi Khaya, Blomerus and Platbos, in the midst of an intense reforestation project, surrounded by old-growth Afro-Montane forests, fynbos, streams and regenerative farming projects. Participants are invited to explore, through dialogue, collaborative work and hands-on practice, how art can catalyze change—whether by nurturing sustainability, advocating for gender and racial equity, fostering social creativity, or regenerating lands scarred by exploitation. We envision art as a force for renewal, capable of restoring not only ecosystems but also our collective sense of belonging to the earth.
studioInfo: The nature reserve is the studio
accommodationInfo: Shared twin rooms, partially ensuite or with shared bathrooms. It's situated on a big and quite remote nature reserve.
technicalInfo: Internet connection

name: SeMA NANJI Residency
description: SeMA NANJI RESIDENCY was opened in 2006 by renovating unused sewage treatment facilities on Nanjido, Seoul. It runs various programs designed to revitalize international exchanges, and provides studio spaces for promising new artists to allow them to concentrate on their artistic activities in a stable environment. 20 local artists move into this facility each year, and 12 foreign artsits are invited to participate in the programs for three months in each quarter.
studioInfo: SNR has various facilities, including: Studios A and B, which have 25 workshops equipped with simple room and board. They are open 24/7 in order to facilitate the activities of the artists in residence Two exhibition halls: various contemporary art and project exhibitions by the artsuts ub resudebce are hekd at this space Outside workspace for shared-use Sculpture garden Laundry room, bathroom, communal kitchen, parking, etc

name: Montemero Art Residency
description: Montemero Art Residency is an organization dedicated to sustainable ecology and alternative art production. They believe that the experience of living and creating in a different context has to be facilitated through collaboration and exchange. Thus, they opened their facilities to artists for them to network and collaborate with professionals from other fields. The program offers a fully-equipped printmaking studio and other open spaces that are suitable for a variety of creative practices (from visual to performing arts and anything in between). Being located on a biological reserve near the Tabernas Desert, the location offers a unique perspective that aims to cultivate a personal connection with nature and how it functions, while further expanding the idea of eco-living. With minimal external interference, artists-in-residence have the opportunity to focus on themselves and their work in a way that more densely populated areas are unable to provide. The residency is open to people of all ages and backgrounds, and they welcome all those who are looking for space and time to explore new forms of interdisciplinary and intercultural collaboration. Although, the long-term objective of this program is to create an eco-art project, here some of their short-term goals: To create an environment and offer the facilities conducive to creative work, integrated with nature, a place to experience new perspectives and acquire new references. Promoting international collaboration and networking, to bring together people from different fields to share and promote ecological and cultural sustainability. Embrace and emphasize the experimental, the undefined, and unexpected states of creativity.
studioInfo: Montemero was the former atelier of German artist Wolfgang Simon. Wolfgang Simon studied from 1957 to 1962 at the Berlin College of Fine Arts. Simon practiced as an apprentice of Friedrich Schröder Sonnenstern. From the late 1960s to his last days, he lived in Andalusia and dedicated his life to the conservation of this land, forming the Finca Montamero Biological Reserve while continuing his work as a printmaker. As such, he equipped his studio for woodcut and linocut printmaking. During the residency, artists will have access to this studio, his archive, and outside areas that can be used for their creative practices. The residency is open to people of all ages and backgrounds, and the organisers welcome all those who are looking for space and time to explore new forms of interdisciplinary and intercultural collaboration. They cannot provide specific materials for artwork. The residency is in a rural area, so they recommend artists to travel with their own materials. Some basic materials/high-quality papers are provided in the printmaking studio, but anything further/specialized will need to be acquired by the artist prior to the residency. Materials located in the scrap yard are free to be used by artists. Depending on your practice they might be able to provide some materials for a small fee (prior notice is required). Feel free to reach out to them and discuss your production process and needs.
accommodationInfo: Montemero offers a private bedroom with shared living space to artists in residence. Additionally, a fully-equipped printmaking studio and workshop for basic fabrication needs (wood/metal-working) are provided, as well as a scrap yard where salvaged materials are kept that can be used for artists’ projects. The shared living-space includes a large kitchen, 2 full bathrooms (1 indoor/1 outdoor shower), laundry facilities, a small library/living room, a large covered patio, an open rooftop, a traditional solar-heated hot tub, caves, and several large outdoor areas conducive to any workflow.
technicalInfo: Montemero offers fully outfitted print studio and tool garage/workshop, a junkyard where salvaged materials kept, kitchen, library, large covered patio, gardens, 1 indoor and 1 outdoor shower, laundry machine, 2 toilets, 1 compost toilet, hot tub, caves, sunset spots, large rooftop.

name: Casa Tagumerche
description: Casa Tagumerche is a creative residency designed to support dedicated artists and writers seeking a private space to generate new ideas, complete projects or make artistic connections. The founders of the residency are Uschi Groos (professional photographer for many years who wants to interact with other photographers from anywhere in the world. She attended many workshops in the past and knows very well how to advance a group of people with the same interests) and Joachim Groos (who worked for publishing companies and is fascinated by the creative process of creating novels and stories). They both love the idea of spending time with artists, supporting them and also getting influenced from them, having interesting discussions and being part of creative processes.
studioInfo: A cottage in the garden with two working desks, writing desks in the sleeping rooms, large dining/working desk in the living room.
accommodationInfo: Two dedicated sleeping rooms with two beds each, one large sleeping couch in the shared living/working room. Two bathrooms, one kitchen.

name: Artist Residency TEMI
description: Artist Residency TEMI is a residency space for visual artists established on the former site of Temi Library by the Daejeon Metropolitan Government to revitalize its original downtown area through culture and arts. Based on today's keyword of convergence, Artist Residency TEMI will support its artists in engaging in creative activities, transcending various genres through its programs that combine local features and arts. By combining Daejeon's science infrastructure with arts, Artist Residency TEMI attempts to develop and manage distinctively specialized programs. It aims to be a special residency where artists can devote themselves to creation and further their individual skills. Through these efforts, it aspires to present an open platform and hub for not only its local citizens and artists but also people in other cities and around the world, through intercity communication, becoming a model for a new kind of creative space for domestic and global arts circles.
studioInfo: Studio: 42.57 m2 with height:3.3 m. Bed, 2 desks, 2 chairs, air conditioning units, fixture, sink and internet service.
accommodationInfo: They have 6 rooms and one is for overseas artist.
technicalInfo: IMAC, laser color printer, scanner, 3D scanner, 3D printer.

name: Cal Gras
description: Cal Gras is a house in a rural setting, open for research and cultural and artistic production, supporting creation. Cal Gras is a cultural center for artistic production, which also works as a rural lodge, therefore, is open to everybody that wants to enjoy peace and harmony in a creative environment. Their goal is to be a node and a meeting point for artists and, at the same time, professionalsofdifferent areas of the cultural industry. The non-profit association behind Cal Gras organizes a wide range of activities that can complement your stay and help you to get in contact with the socia, cultural and natural environment.
studioInfo: There are two 45 sqm studios. One is equipped for drawing and painting and the other one is meant for big scale pieces of sculpture, metal work or installations.
accommodationInfo: The house can host 18 people distributed in single, double, triple and quadruple rooms. As common spaces you will find a kitchen,na dinning room, a living room, bathrooms and a laundry room.
technicalInfo: Cal Gras has two spacious studios, a meeting room of 45 sqm, a 60 sqm library and a 60 sqm multipurpose room. In order to help artist get their materials, the organizers put them in contact with local providers.

name: BARIM
description: BARIM is a cross-genre collective of artists who are based in Gwangju, currently an art space, media space, and working studio in Gwangju, Korea. Established in October, 2013, and opened in Spring 2014, Barim deals with abstract to physical genres of the arts. Barim aims to focus on “process-based” works beyond existing genres of the arts, to create a community of artists, local citizens, and audience, and to support cultural and artistic exchanges between local and international artists through research. It also sets a goal to intervene and transcend different genres of the arts and to focus on process and discussion rather than completion. Self-funded Residency/program Barim welcomes independent residencies, projects, and programs aside from our curation. Regarding the program, date, and cost, please email them if you 4t: - artists/curators/researchers/musicians/choreographers/performers/critics who want to create a project at barim. - who are able to make an artistic proposal and responsible in producing a work, bringing a new perspective.
studioInfo: One open hall and a rooftop.
accommodationInfo: Not provided.

name: Seoul Art Space Geumcheon
description: A printing factory located at Doksan-dong, Geumcheon-gu was turned into Seoul Art Space_GEUMCHEON, which is a new concept art space aimed to be both an international residency and a joint project studio where experiments are made on global aesthetics and local characteristics, as one of Seoul Art Spaces. Seoul Art Space GEUMCHEON has been designed under the big cultural movement of Seoul city planning called ‘Urban Regeneration’ Other than the first and foremost goal of ‘Creative Support for Artists’ it started with the assignment of cultural revival and settlement by positively responding to the issues of the south west of Seoul where ‘Guro Complex’ is located. Read more on their blog . Due to Covid-19 pandemic, the international artists in residency program has been stopped for the time being.
studioInfo: The building is composed with 3 floors above the ground, 1 floor underground, and an annexed storehouse. 18 studios with cooling/heating, cooking facilities and Internet services available for resident artists. PS333, located on the 3rd floor of the building is a large space (200 seats) available for performance, conference, and exhibition provided with lighting and sound facilities. A largework space (Warehouse Gallery) for large-scale and joint art work is provided.
accommodationInfo: Hostel is provided with furniture and office-related equipment as well as guest rooms The lounges on the 2nd and 3rd floors are for rest and meeting other residency artists Fully furnitured kitchen, shower rooms and a laundry room for living conveniences
technicalInfo: Wireless internet and Media lab with the latest equipment are provided.

name: Electro-Etching Workshop Residency
description: The Electro-etching residency introduces the artist to an alternative technique of intaglio etching, using a completely non-toxic electrical process, and thus avoiding completely the harmful acids used in traditional etching. The electro-etching residency is located within the workshop and residence of the artist Alfonso Crujera, a master printmaker and specialist in the varied techniques of etching with electrolysis.
studioInfo: The workspace is free from toxic emissions and respectful to the environment. The studio, measuring 70m2, is naturally lit, containing all the necessary equipment in order to etch (electrolytic unit, etching-press, tables, tools, acrylic resists and oil based resists, proof inks, vegetal cleaning agent). The workshop is available to the resident artists 24 hours a day.
accommodationInfo: The residence is a traditional coastal farmhouse, lovingly restored by the artist. The guest artist has a private apartment consisting of a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, fridge, library, and wireless internet connection. From the residence as well as the balconies, you can enjoy the magnificent panorama of the sea and surrounding farmland.
technicalInfo: The resident artist will be introduced to the process of electro-etching copper and zinc plates instead of using traditional acids. (S)He will have access to the master’s direct and personal assistance and will have the opportunity to develop their current knowledge of non-toxic etching using electricity, applying these techniques to their own work. The artist will also learn how to assemble an electro-etching unit themselves, so they will be able to continue electro-etching in their own studio back home.

name: TPK
description: TPK is a research project in the field of contemporary art and thought. The project has three main activities: art training for children and adults, production of events for the promotion of multidisciplinary projects in the field of contemporary art and thought, and a studio programme for artists.
studioInfo: 12 studios: between 11 and 15 m2.
accommodationInfo: No lodging is provided.
technicalInfo: Exchange programmes are currently being planned.

name: B-Murals
description: B-Murals is an art center specializing in urban art based in Barcelona. A pioneering and unique project for its comprehensive approach, which combines support for creation, through the promotion of mural interventions, art residencies and exhibitions; with the community and educational work outside its walls. B-Murals has a vocation of connection and interaction with the territory as well as a universal spirit and an international dimension. The project was launched by Difusor, an entity that has been working for more than a decade in artistic promotion and intervention in the urban environment. The call is mainly aimed at visual and plastic artists, but also multidisciplinary artists who can apply their work to public space: urban art, visual arts, artistic research and interdisciplinary projects, especially those that seek a relationship and dialogue with the territory and the public space. The space offered within the framework of this call consists of a workshop of about 30m², located in the warehouse adjacent to B-MURALS’ gallery – one of the warehouses that are part of the old industrial complex of the Nau Bostik. The space has natural light, work tables, electricity, Internet connection (wi-fi). The warehouse has two 30m² individual workspaces and a shared kitchenette space at the entrance. B-MURALS offers the following resources to residents selected through this call: Workspace in the B-Murals residency studio. Shared studio with another selected artist, basic furniture: table, chair, and shelves. Access 7 days a week and the possibility of 24/7 access (to consult with the organization). Access to the exterior spaces of the Nau Bostik, especially the walls destined to host ephemeral mural interventions (to be agreed with the organization). Possibility of accommodation provided by their sponsor RESIDENCIA ONIX. You will share the studio with another selected artist. It is equipped with two single beds, a kitchen and bathroom, two desks, wifi, heating, air conditioning, and weekly cleaning service. Possibility of occasional use of the Nau Bostik Coworking facilities – at flex tables. Consultancy and follow-up sessions with the B-MURALS team on issues related to artistic production (related to the residency). Communication of the project on B-MURALS’ website, social media, and newsletter. Open studio: organization of a public presentation in a format agreed upon between the artist and the organization (happening, art talk, guided tour, performance, intervention in public space...) that allows for the public display of the artists’ work and development during the residency in an innovative format for the communication and exchange of artistic research. 2-week exhibition of the work produced during the residency, with support for production and installation. (Opening time following the B-Murals Gallery’s schedule).
studioInfo: Workspace in the B-Murals residency studio at Nau Bostik, Barcelona. Shared studio with another selected artist, basic furniture: table, chair, and shelves. Access 7 days a week and the possibility of 24/7 access (to consult with the organization). Access to the exterior spaces of the Nau Bostik, especially the walls destined to host ephemeral mural interventions (to be agreed with the organization).
accommodationInfo: Possibility of accommodation provided by their sponsor RESIDENCIA ONIX. You will share the studio with another selected artist. It is equipped with two single beds, a kitchen and bathroom, two desks, wifi, heating, air conditioning, and weekly cleaning service.

name: CURTIDAS
description: CURTIDAS is a small storefront in the heart of Raval, in the old town of Barcelona. The two windows to the street are exhibitory spaces from where to bridge the artistic processes with the urban, social reality. They foster creative research initiatives dealing with nature, transdisciplinarity, social interaction, and technology. They curate artists with a clear ecological engagement and who can transform ideas into shared physical experiences.
studioInfo: CURTIDAS is one space to live and work. It has a kitchen and a small bathroom. It is meant for artists that do not need too much space to develop their work: writers, programmers, researchers, sound artists, photographers, filmmakers, etc. It is located in a very centric and lively neighborhood in the heart of the old town of Barcelona.
accommodationInfo: The residency space is for one artist - it's a 45 square meter organized as a working space (with printer, drawing material, and bricolage tools) and a mezzanine with bed and basic living facilities.
technicalInfo: They provide a small library, printer, bricolage tools and a bicycle.

name: homesession
description: Situated in the center of Barcelona, homesession has initiated a residency programme dedicated to visual artists. Run by a curator and an architect from France, homesession hosts each year up to 10 artists from all over the world. The idea of this residency is based on a real integration to local life: the programme provide a flat and a studio and sessions with homesession’s curators for individually-tailored residency development. Homesession is an independant organisation that offer up to 4 grants a year, that cover accommodation and studio. The artists who are selected are interested in experimenting new ways of producing and discovering the city.
studioInfo: In 2012 Homesession adds a new space for its programme, consisting of a flat for residents, an exhibition area and shared offices. It's also located in the Poble Sec quarter.
accommodationInfo: The accommodation is an 18m2 flat situated in a 50m2 studio. It offers private sleeping room, private bathroom and working space.
technicalInfo: Tripod Scanner Monitor LCD 42” Projector Acer (no HD) 1 DVD Player BluRay 1 DVD Player standard 2 MP3 player Speakers (mini-jack) mini Hif Studio light

name: Herrera Gallery
description: Herrera is a dynamic contemporary art gallery and independent cultural engine based in the Sant Andreu district, located just 15 minutes from Barcelona’s city center. The space is dedicated to the promotion of interdisciplinary practices, serving as a vital link between creative experimentation and the public. They pride themselves on being an inclusive platform that welcomes creators at every stage of their career—from emerging young talent bringing fresh perspectives to senior artists with established practices. The organization is built on the belief that artistic growth happens through the intersection of different generations and backgrounds. By being strategically connected to the heart of the city while maintaining the authentic energy of a local neighborhood, Herrera facilitates a continuous dialogue between diverse artistic languages. They are committed to nurturing a diverse community of makers, ensuring that our gallery remains a space for bold ideas, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and the professional development of artists within the international contemporary scene. Herrera is an artist-run space in Barcelona offering flexible, year-round residencies tailored to each artist's specific needs. Their mission is to provide an accessible and authentic environment for research, production, and meaningful creative exchange between local and international creators. They welcome artists, creators, designers, curators, writers, etc at any stage of their career, from emerging voices to established practitioners. Located in a lively, traditional neighborhood just 15 minutes from Barcelona’s city center, Herrera combines the privacy of a dedicated studio with the energy of a creative hub, fostering transformative artistic processes and genuine connections. They bridge the gap between creation and exhibition, providing a platform where research, production, and public presentation coexist. Artists are encouraged to experiment without the immediate pressure of a commercial output; however, most residencies culminate in a public showcase or an open studio event to share the results with the community.
studioInfo: The gallery provides a versatile workspace within its main facilities. It is a white-cube style space with natural light, suitable for production and exhibition. Residents also have access to a shared coworking area for digital work and a private outdoor patio, which is ideal for painting or any artistic processes that benefit from being outdoors. The studio is equipped with Wi-Fi and basic tools for daily use.
accommodationInfo: The residency space includes two private bedrooms, a shared kitchen, and two shared bathrooms.

name: untitledBCN
description: untitledBCN is a Barcelona based arts organisation which opened in 2008 with the aim to create opportunities for emerging artists, organising cultural events and exhibitions involving artists from all around the world. untitledRESIDENCY is an opportunity for visiting artists to develop their practice whilst taking up residence in Barcelona for 1 month. untitledBCN provides studio and accommodation for the month, and introduce the artist to local working artists appropriate to their interests and discipline. This is an informal program, the artist is unsupervised yet guidance and recommendations are instinctively given by the untitledBCN team and coworkers when requested. untitledBCN has run untitledRESIDENCY since 2011, it is a program which provides opportunities for motivated artists to really experience the life and culture of Barcelona.
studioInfo: Shared studio with local artists (varied disciplines), with wifi available
accommodationInfo: Private room within a clean shared house, in an excellent location, near Gràcia & Sagrada Familia. Cleaner fee included. Wifi Please notify the host of pet allergies!
technicalInfo: You can discuss your needs and requirements upon application with untitledBCN. Between the gallery & studios they have a variety of facilities available depending on the requirements.

name: Piramidón
description: Since 1990, the C.A.C. Piramidon has been reinventing the concept of an art gallery. It is an art centre designed as a space for artists where both creativity and its diffusion converge as equals. Piramidon gives priority to the display and solvency of the artist's work, contributing to that end with the necessary stability for the artist's development. After passing a stringent selection process, the artists come to work at one of our center's 16 studios. In addition, two of the studios are designed to host artists who are residing outside of Barcelona, and in most cases artists from other countries.
technicalInfo: Exhibition of works in the exhibition hall. Information and communication of all exhibitions at the "Piramidón News", on the website and on social networks. Free access to the kitchen-office. Free use of the dining room and / or meeting room. Free use of the tools and machinery. Water and electricity services. Free wifi access. Printing facilities. Free access to the rooftop terrace. Reception messaging. Storage and temporary custody of artist personal belongings.

name: Hangar
description: Hangar is a centre for arts production and research, set up by the Association of Visual Arts of Catalonia (AAVC) in 1997. It provides support facilities for artists and designers and offers services adapted to production needs associated with the arts world. The centre is housed in refurbished industrial premises in the Poblenou neighbourhood of Barcelona. In addition to its international and national open call for accomodation, Hangar also offers studios, production grants and a series of training workshops for artists. Residencies Hangar offers involve many organizations and partnerships. It is essential to check their website regularly for available calls and particular criteria.
studioInfo: 30 m2 single and 60 m2 shared between 2 artists Work desks, power sockets, sink, Internet connection (wi-fi), showers and heating. Resident artists on long stays may use the following services free of charge: digital imaging lab and self-editing suite, a sound stage and multi-purpose space, as well as production advice from Hangar’s team of professionals. The resident artists also have an online publishing tool at their disposal where they can showcase their work, and a video channel .
accommodationInfo: Since the end of 2011, Hangar has a residency for artists that is located in the old house of the guard of the industrial complex of Can Ricart. The building has two floors of 80,99m2 and 62,59 m2. Each floor has two double bedrooms, a bathroom, a living room and a kitchen. Also the residency has access to a community garden shared with Hangar’ staff and users. The residence hosts a maximum of four artists together for short periods of time that go from one week up to three months. The intention is to host a minimum of two artists each time with the aim of facilitating the exchange of experiences and knowledge among the artists besides their individual research and production projects.
technicalInfo: Video Sony HVR-Z1 video camera. Records on HDV, DVCAM, Mini DV (can only be hired for use outside the centre by AAVC members) Sony HDR-FX1 video camera. Records on HDV and Mini Dv Sony HDR-HC1E video camera. Records on HDV and Mini Dv Wide conversion lens x0,7 for the camera Sony HDR-HC1E Stereo microphone ECM-HST1 for the camera Sony HDR-HC1E Battery video light HVL-20DMA Manfroto 344B tripod Manfroto 755MF3 tripod Edirol video mixer with 4 inputs and 2 channels FilmGear fluorescent tube box: 2 x 120cm with 4 banks and 1 x 60 cm with 4 banks. With tripods, extension cords and sand bags. Warm and cool light tubes available. Quartz light kit, 3 x 1200 W lights with tripods Audio Behringer XM200S microphone Sennheiser MKH416 microphone AKG D230 microphone AKG MPA III L microphone FoneStar FCM2600 microphone AKG C 417 lapel condenser microphone Shure MX400D table microphone Sony E3CM-MS907 microphone Sennheiser G2_ew100 wireless microphone kit: 2 units Rode stereo videomic for videocamera Stand and wind screens Sony MZ-NHF800 minidisc Digital recorder Zoom H-2 mp3/WAV Foto Kit of flashes elinchrom style FX 400 digital:3 Flashes Elinchrom Style FX 400,reflector 16 cm,protective Hood,1 Portalite 60 x 60 cm , 1 translucent Deflector, 1 silver umbrella 83 cm, 1 translucent umbrella 83 cm, 3 feet 88- 235 cm, 1 bag for transporting the feet and umbrella, 1 bag for transporting the flashes, 2 sets of fuses , 1 sync cable, 1 cone snoot + grid CANON EOS 5D MARKII + 24-105 mm. lens (**for this equipment you have to leave a deposit of 100€) Canon Power Shot S70 digital still camera Other Portable Internet streaming system Honda EU20i inverter generator (specifically for electronic equipment) with maximum output of 200 W Tricycle with kit for urban interventions

name: BAR Project
description: BAR project is an independent, mobile and non-profit organization dedicated to promote artistic exchange through local, national and international residencies and collaborations, and by developing a public program issued from curatorial and research projects. BAR project gets its name from one of the quintessential social gathering places in our culture in order re-contextualize it and be able to work from there. That place is the popular coffee and beer bar, thought as the right scenario in order to conceive our lines of thought. BAR project develops a residency program in Barcelona that is conceived as a platform for the internationalization of the local context by making connections between artists and other agents of the sector from a critical and independent perspective. By an invitation process BAR welcomes international artists and curators to come to Barcelona during different periods and following different types of residencies. BAR project is a platform which doesn’t have its own venue. Its residencies are possible thanks to different partners and collaborators, who are able to provide BAR’s residents with an apartment on the Eixample area of Barcelona, workshops, located in the production centre Fabra i Coats, and with material and economic budget. Furthermore, the different art centres within the city – institutional and independent- as well as a variety of agents of the local artistic scene, they all participate in the programs’s activities and visits.
studioInfo: Studios for artists are located in the premises of the art center Fabra i Coats. Contact the organization for more information on the details.
accommodationInfo: The apartment in the Eixample district has four bedrooms, a living room, a full kitchen and two bathrooms and a balcony. WiFi access and bedding is provided.

name: Espai Souvenir
description: Souvenir, is a space for artistic and cultural collaboration, with a focus on research, production, and the presentation of creative practices. As a dynamic space for the organization of cultural events, they work with artists from various areas of the contemporary art scene, be it performative, educative, or in the form of exhibitions. The space opened in the Gracia neighborhood of Barcelona in 2017 and is identified by its interdisciplinary and intermittent vocation. Espai Souvenir invites artists for their 2023 residency program to develop artistic production and research projects at the Souvenir artspace and is open to artists of all nationalities, the residency includes Open Studio. We offer workspace and a final open studio in the Espai Souvenir artspace located in the Gracia neighborhood, one of the most central neighborhoods with greater visibility and cultural life in Barcelona.
studioInfo: They offer InSitu workspace in the gallery space. A 35m2 space will be shared by 2 artists.
technicalInfo: At all times the artist may count on the advice of the R.A.R.O. team, for example, getting materials, accommodation, etc. They offer accompaniment, curatorial, and assembly assistance for the open studio or final exhibition where the work done during the residency will be shown.

name: Filou, casa-jardín
description: The residency is located in a tiny village in Spain, three-hour drive south-west of Barcelona, surrounded by pine forest, olive and almond trees, called Belmonte de San José. The objective of the residency is to bring art to their village, attract interesting people to Belmonte, and offer the artist a nice place to stay and work. Granted artists can stay 2 to 4 weeks, alone or with other artists in the following periods of the year: 8th of April 2024 – end of May 2024 1st of October 2024 – end of November 2024
studioInfo: 55 m2 studio and exterior space for creativity.
accommodationInfo: The residency offers an accommodation in an inspiring, peaceful, and beautiful environment with: few blank walls inside and out spacious studio to work in garden with nice views to relax in (or to work in..) kitchen is available. The village has a bar/restaurant and a small shop.

name: Blueproject Foundation
description: The Blueproject Foundation is a non-profit organization based in Barcelona whose main aim is to support and promote national and international artistic creation. This support is offered through a residency programme for exhibitions and performances that provides assistance for artists to promote their work that is both relevant to and a reflection of today's aesthetic, social and intellectual issues. From the present open call, 3 projects will be selected with an exhibition as a final result (with a maximum of eight weeks) and 3 projects of performance (for at least one public presentation). Priority will be given to new and original projects. Each participant can submit a maximum of one individual proposal and one collective. The production support and the residency must allow the conception, formalization, production and/or completion of the proposed project, using the facilities of the workshop if needed, with the objective of its following exhibition / presentation at the Sala Project for exhibition projects and at the Off Blue space for performance projects. Submitted projects may include any artistic-cultural field of any discipline, regardless the format or technique employed. Each project must be developed or completed in a period of residency of maximum of six weeks previous to its presentation / exhibition, at the usual open hours of the foundation (from Tuesday to Friday, from 10 am to 8 pm, and Saturday and Sunday, from noon to 7 pm). The period of residency for performance projects may be flexible and to be agreed according its work plan and the foundation calendar.
studioInfo: The foundation commits to providing a range of materials and human resources for the proper development of the projects: Use of the entire workshop space for a maximum period of six weeks (for each project) to develop the selected project. The use of this space includes free Wi-Fi, basic cleaning of the space and the tools and resources at the foundation's disposal.
accommodationInfo: Blueproject Foundation offers for the artists-in-residence and other guest artists El Taller, a private space located on the first floor of the foundation. This room of approximately 100 square metres offers the facilities and flexibility necessary for the realization of works and projects of the selected artists. The amount assigned is also to cover the accommodation and expenses in case of Barcelona non-resident artists. They have some arrangements to find accommodation for artists.

name: Tangent Projects
description: Tangent Projects is a curatorial initiative set up to work with artists on site-responsive exhibitions and projects. With a desire to add multiplicity to the current art archetype, Tangent Projects endeavors to showcase exemplary works in a variety of different media and platforms - including publications, exhibitions, performances, and online commissions. In offering the opportunity for digressions to be pursued, ideas and processes that might normally have been discarded in favor of the main discourse will have the potential to reach a conclusion. Without a commercial bias and with experimentation encouraged, Tangent Projects invites artists to explore the diversions and deviations within their artistic practice. In simple terms, the residency gives artists the leeway to "go off on a tangent". They are accepting applications for the studio residency programme for 2023/24. Residencies are for 3 months and the placements will be between: September - December 2023 January-April 2024 April - July 2024 Please let them know your preferred dates in your motivation text.
studioInfo: Studio space, relaxing room, reading room, common kitchen.
accommodationInfo: Tangent can offer suggestions for accommodation.

name: Domestic Data Streamers
description: Domestic Data Streamers started on the 22nd of September 2013 when a team of artists started working together on artistic experiments exploring the relationships between people and information. The principal ideas of what they did still remain the main drivers behind the studio. The team wanted to challenge the way we understand information today and how this can create profound change in the way we behave as humans. An experimental residency on data, music, writing and new media at the heart of Barcelona. Hey Human! is a nonprofit artists-in-residence program that provides time and space for inventors, artists and researchers to create, experiment, and cultivate new directions in their practice. A shared journey with the Domestic Data Streamers family to redefine the meaning behind the power of data using all kinds of arts. This program is designed to foster research and exploration rather than culminating in a final exhibition.
studioInfo: 24/7 studio and workshop facilities.
accommodationInfo: They offer a 2-4 weeks stay in Barcelona providing an accommodation plan with a team member of the studio.
technicalInfo: Side assistance from Domestic Data Streamers team members. A small event for the presentation of each residency result. Benefit from constructive feedback sessions every Friday with the Domestic Data Streamers team.

name: Bilbao Arte
description: Bilbao Arte is an artistic production centre belonging to the Culture Department of the Bilbao City Council and provides young creators with the means and infrastructures required to develop their artistic ideas through the availability of studio spaces, engraving and silkscreening workshop, digital imaging, sculpture, photography, a film set, documentation centre and projection rooms. The Centre offers grants for two modalities of time: Six month stay: January-June or July-December 1 year stay, starting in January: There are three types of grants available for individuals or groups: Studio assigment: continuous use of space for the realization of specific projects. The artist will receive 2.000 euros (for six months projets) or 4.000 (for 1 year projects) for materials and expenses. 10 grants avaiable. Production: it gives access to the infrastructures and workshops and consultancy in techniques and procedures. The artist will receive 2.000 euros (for six months projets) or 4.000 (for 1 year projects) for materials and expenses. 10 grants avaiable. Cooperation: the selected artists committ to cooperate as assistants of the workshops for 4 hours a day or a maximum of 20 hours weekly. In return they can use the premises for their own projects. The artist will receive 500 euros a month during 11 months (February - December). 4 grants available.
studioInfo: There are 12 studio spaces for resident artists. These studios are available to selected artists for a maximum time length of twelve months. Access to these spaces also entails access to the Centre’s workshops and as such, the infrastructure and advice of the professors in charge of the workshops.
accommodationInfo: There is a complementary accommodation grant for artists selected in any of the three previous modalities in a shared apartment with other artists. The esmitated value of this grant is 200 euros per month.

name: The Foundry
description: The Foundry is a non-profit residency with three aims: 1. to offer a space for people to work on their projects; 2. to host events organized by members; 3. to increase self-sufficiency and sustainability. The Foundry is not a hotel or tourist destination, but a space of work outside of the institutional confines of market and government funding. They offer open residency programs throughout the year.
studioInfo: Different spaces, for music, visual arts, work with metal, clay and other materials.
accommodationInfo: They currently have six bathrooms, 12 bedrooms (mostly doubles) with electricity and WiFi, a professional kitchen, several large rooms, and a huge field where people can pitch a tent. The Foundry is located in a valley surrounded by a river and a forest. For the regular groceries they go to Viveiro, a seaside town at 10 kilometers distance. There is a car and a bike, anyone is free to use them. Pets are allowed outside as long as they behave; if they cannot stay outside, please ask them in advance what are the possibilities. They generally organize food together, but you don’t have to join this system (which involves sharing bills and cooking once in a while) if you don’t want to. The organisers want to keep the Foundry as cheap as possible, so they have no staff; guests are expected to take care of the space together. To coordinate this, there are usually assemblies every few weeks.

name: AADK Spain
description: AADK offers an interdisciplinary program that opens up a space for analysis, research and creation in deep dialogue with its context. Thus, the location models the practices on, and modifies both its participants and the local communities. They aim to highlight the value of local knowledge as a means to re-think how rural environments can position themselves in an era of massive urbanization considering social, historical and geographical perspectives. The program is intended for all artists and researchers who wish to work with the notions of body, territory and spatiality. Throughout their stay, participants conform to a temporary community that shares experiences and processes fostering debate, collaboration, and a transversal perspective of their projects. The residency periods may be from one up to six months, being two months the minimum recommended for the full development of a project. Participants are encouraged to keep in touch with them after their stay ends, being our intention to promote their work in forthcoming exhibitions as well as in papers, conferences and/or publications curated by our platform. To date, the program has hosted more than 300 artists from different fields, positioning itself both regionally and internationally. The Residencies is an interdisciplinary program that opens up a space for analysis, research, and creation in deep dialogue with its context. Thus, the location models the practices and modifies both its participants and the local communities. They aim to highlight the value of local knowledge as a means to re-think how rural environments can position themselves in an era of massive urbanization, considering social, historical, and geographical perspectives. The program is intended for all artists and researchers who wish to work with the notions of body, territory, and spatiality. Throughout their stay, participants form a temporary community that shares experiences and processes, fostering debate, collaboration, and a transversal perspective of their projects. The residency periods may be from one up to six months, with two months being the minimum recommended for the full development of a project. Participants are encouraged to keep in touch with them after their stay ends, as it is their intention to promote the artists' work in forthcoming exhibitions, papers, conferences, and/or publications curated by their platform. To date, the program has hosted more than 300 artists from different fields, positioning itself both regionally and internationally.
studioInfo: Spaces are provided depending on the applicant's request and spatial needs. There are interconnected studio spaces varying in size, they can be requested for individual use or shared with other artists/collectives.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation options: individual apartment, individual studio apartment, big or small room in a shared house. The housing facilities are divided into two areas, consisting of a group of four apartments bordering Centro Negra and an old house in the center of the town. The latter was the former Video Art Museum, EDOM. The apartments are equipped with private kitchens, toilets and showers. They have a terrace for common use and direct access to the main building. The house has three bedrooms, two bathrooms and a kitchen with a living room. It is located in the heart of the village and has excellent access to all shops and stores. It is also ideal to immerse oneself in the daily life of Blanca. Both housing areas have access to washing machines and are equipped with bedding and towels.

name: Nau Côclea
description: Nau Côclea is a meeting point between culture and nature. The center is dedicated to research, production and the presentation of contemporary art and culture projects. Nau Côclea has a small residence space for creators and researchers. The stays are usually short, between seven days and three months. The resident artists carry out projects in collaboration with the center and the local people.   They offer two types of residencies: Production residencies: Nau Côclea will provide accommodation and studio space and some equipment. The artist will also receive assistance from the team, help in contacting material suppliers and will be put in contact with the local artist community. Sound Art residencies: specific for sound art and experimental music projects. Accommodation, pre-production support will be provided, as well as advie from the staff. The artist is expected to present the resulting work in the Musica 13 Festival, yearly organized by Nau Côclea.
studioInfo: Residents can also use the common office of the centre (50 m2 library and meeting place) and the workshop/rehearsal room (80 m2).
accommodationInfo: Residencies include accommodation for artists (maximum 4) in a small independent house situated in a rural area. The house has two double bedrooms, a small kitchen, a bathroom and a living room with a firewood stove.
technicalInfo: Depending on their needs and the centre's schedule, residents may use the audio-visual equipment, exhibition and work spaces. Some Nau Côclea resources (high-definition video camera, sound equipment, video projector, etc.) may be used. Consult the appendix for features of the spaces and the list of equipment.

name: La Pedrada de Noemi
description: The general idea is to make visible different artistic disciplines and interact with the visitors in an eminently rural environment, full of esthetic beauty in a singular location, and having as a result an inspiring and creative space to develop the senses for all who, actively or passively, participate in the project. Depending on the necessities of each artist, the organizers bridge the gap between the artists, researchers and the different associations of the village. Description of the residency programme: “La Pedrada” has been thought as a link element between the local people, the ateliers located in Agüimes and the artists residents in “La Pedrada”, being enriched with the knowledge and ideas that they all provide and, therefore, looking for the local raise of personal and cultural development. It aims to be a medium to connect traditional artistic currents and vanguards that develop outside the islands too. In an old house, now rehabilitated, and framed in a rural environment rich in cultural activities and with affined people, “La Pedrada”was created as a space to think, create, coexist and rest around art and its cultural possibilities in an adapted, peaceful, free and open surrounding.
studioInfo: Two shared studios in the main house and an outdoor area. You will alsto have the possibility to work in a separate studio, just few minutes away from the main house.
accommodationInfo: It has five bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, 2 ateliers , a patio and an exterior terrace. Private or shared room in a house totally equipped: kitchen, fridge, electricity, gas, water, living areas, cleaning service, service of towels and sheets. Situated in the historical center of Agüimes town, its construction is dated around the 18th century. Originally it was used as the court's dependencies and later on it became the local doctor's residence.
technicalInfo: La Pedrada de Noemi provides material for stone (hand tool, air, pneumatic hammer, and grinder smoler ( special insurance needed ), material for mosaico work and simple wood work.

name: The Unifiedfield
description: The Unifiedfield / el campo unificado is an independent art space and artist-run organization focusing on the experimental aspects of sound, video and performance art. They observe the world as a network of interdependent connections and they understand artistic practice as a vehicle that can transform life, the relation with ourselves, society, and the natural world. It previously occupied a traditional complex amongst rice fields in Yogyakarta (Indonesia), subsequently moving into a cave in Granada (Spain) before settling in an antique building nestled in Granada’s historic Moorish quarters, the Albayzín, where it ran an artist residency for three years. In 2013, The Unifiedfield initiated its Nomadic Artist-in-Residence Program in The Philippines where is currently working in collaboration with Balud Art Network. The Unifiedfield / el campo unificado is about to launch its third residency program and the first edition of an annual arts festival in Castellar de la Frontera, Cádiz (Spain). In October - November 2017, six international artists will coincide in an Andalusian home at a medieval fortress in the heart of Los Alcornocales Natural Park. For this program, artists are invited to work out of their comfort zone to experiment with collaborative processes and ephemeral interventions in the village and the natural surroundings. Besides the main residency in Castellar, there is also the possibility to develop a project in two different settings during other periods: Granada city: the residency will take place at an old charming apartment in Albayzín - similar to the one they had in their former residency in Granada between 2012 and 2014. This new program will focus on relational art projects in San Miguel Alto where The Unifiedfield is starting a community garden. A dome in a village in Ávila, near Madrid: for projects which use the dome as a Temporary Autonomous Zone for internal experiences / art processes to happen in nature.
studioInfo: Shared facilities and common spaces are available in the main residency in Castellar (for the other 2 locations, if you need more information, please send them an email). The focus of this residency will be interventions in nature and the village.
accommodationInfo: In Castellar: private bedroom with shared facilities and common spaces in an Andalusian home at a medieval fortress in the heart of Los Alcornocales Natural Park.

name: Konvent
description: Konvent is a late XIX century nun’s convent and textile colony that has been converted into a multidisciplinary arts centre. It’s a space for art and way of understanding and undertaking cultural practices that are rooted in the territory. Konvent is a creative space that breathes life into disused industrial heritage. It’s a former nun’s convent and textile colony that has been converted into an experimental laboratory both on a personal and artistic level where a diversity of projects converge, especially those which have no place in the frame of institutional culture. The residencies at Konvent have the goal of becoming a platform to aid artists and creators by providing the adequate conditions of space and concentration required for investigation in a unique environment such as the Cal Rosal textile colony. For 2023, they offer a new residency format in which they propose 7 different open calls with specific dates for each call. The intention is to give visibility and delve into certain topics, disciplines and contexts that they believe require special attention in the contemporary world we live in, as well as offer the possibility of establishing links with other communities, spaces and festivals. For the 2023 residency edition, they have chosen themes that move them personally, representing the diversity that exists within artistic creation and our society, choosing to emphasize groups and disciplines that have historically been underrepresented, and making true on the commitment that is given to us as a centre of and for contemporary art and culture, to evolve as a people and society.
accommodationInfo: Konvent is a not-for-profit organization with over 26 years’ history. The building is a XIX Century nun’s convent within a the Cal Rosal textile colony. In addition to being home to the nuns that had their dormitories, the chief nun’s room and cloister rooms, the building housed a school, hospital, chapel, sacristy, gardens and several services for the factory. All these spaces have been converted into exhibition, work and residency spaces, a unique and inspiring environment, that will surely leave a strong imprint on the creative process. Konvent will make available all its resources and spaces. Most of the workspaces have internet access. Konvent’s unique spaces can be viewed on their website.

name: CACiS El Forn de la Calç
description: The CACiS residence El Forn de la Calç annually hosts a selection of visual arts projects, performing arts, performance, thought, intervention in the landscape and research of new languages ​​related to sustainability and the protection of the natural environment (not exclusively artistic ). The CACiS residence presents the basic conditions for research and study in the middle of nature, so that the artist can find the ideal conditions of space, concentration and equipment. The uniqueness of CACis allows it to be a place where you can rehearse and do work that is not possible in other places. The philosophy of the centre and its vindictive nature make it a call where the projects and authors/res that are presented already have a clearly different profile. Every year, CACiS opens an international call for creators who want to stay in their residences to do research work during the following year. The call for the residency grant for research opens two times a year, the first semester of the year is presented in the month of December of the previous year, and to access the residency for the second semester the call comes out in June of the current year. This call allows creators from all over the world to develop their projects for a certain period of time time residing at CACiS that gathers the comforts and suitable materials to be able to carry out the selected works.
studioInfo: All the studios are designed by the principles of bioclimatic architecture taking into account comfortability, sustainability and power efficiency at the same level. They will be some materials and equipment for the artists to use in their projects.
accommodationInfo: The residency is integrated by two 2 bedroom apartments with bathroom with a common area of 30 square meters as living room and kitchen. They are equiped with washing machine and refrigerator.
technicalInfo: Located at the center are ancient lime kilns which have been restored due to their uniqueness, their good condition and their industrial and architectural value. The premises include also an open space for exhibitions or performances and 2 hectares of outdoors space for music or theatrical performances.

name: El Mirador de Akasha
description: The Mirador de Akasha is a self-managed Art Residence, founded in 2016 by the artists Daniela S. Checa and María Salmerón (Artemysa Salmerón). It is place to welcome artists from all over the world who love to travel and share their art with local artists. They offer a huge workshop with ceramic kiln even apart from other materials needed for the different disciplines that take place in the house (included in the AKASHA ARTISTIC CREATION SCHOLARSHIP) apart from numerous gardens and lookouts to inspire. They have different artists who collaborate with this Cultural Association as tutors and supervisors of the different workshops that are offered in the Scholarship, each one with its technique and methodology. As Cultural Association & Artists Residence "El Mirador de Akasha" aims to generate a transformation in the strategies of exchange, training and artistic creation, for professionals, art lovers and students of all media and artistic expressions. This program encourages the exchange of experiences and the importance of culture in the development of the community, so weekly, in its gardens and viewpoints, they take dozens of artists as a meeting place and artistic exchange of all disciplines and nationalities, called Jam artistic. It is a place where critical thinking is promoted and offers this space for the free creation in development of a project / author's work in the old part of the city of Granada, surrounded by a magical scenery of viewpoints and gardens, being an organic laboratory who experiences the possibility of creating a rural lifestyle, harmonious and inspiring while connected with the extensive cultural agenda offered by the city. The Mirador de Akasha continuously has numerous events and workshops aimed at transmitting values ​​linked to an awareness of the Ecological, Creativity, respect and Bioenergetics, Symbolic and Therapeutic Thought.
studioInfo: Large workshop to share
accommodationInfo: The house is a palace located in the emblematic Albaicin neighborhood of Granada, the birthplace of Flamenco and Andalusian art. It consists of eight individual bedrooms, all with beautiful views, four bathrooms, family kitchen and laundry area, cozy living room with fireplace and library, large shared work workshop and numerous terraces, gazebos and gardens that are sources of inspiration, from the which can be contemplated the panoramic of the whole city, the Mountains of Sierra Nevada and the Historical Monument World Heritage "La Alhambra". During the stay, the artists will have all the common areas of the house, private room and a large workshop for free creation seeking synergy among the inhabitants. The house can host up to 4 people, through 1 shared bedroom and 2 private attics with amazing views. Participants will be able to use the residence as their place to work, rest or meet with people.
technicalInfo: In the workshop there is a ceramic furnace and all kinds of material that can be rented.

name: INVE Experimental Arts Platform
description: INVE Experimental Arts Platform is a multidisciplinary organization founded in Valparaíso, Chile, emerging from a vibrant community of Chilean and Latin American artists and researchers. With 11 years of trajectory, INVE cultivates a distinctive approach to contemporary arts, centered on collective experimentation, process-based creation, collaborative research, and innovative production methods—while equally prioritizing the exhibition, distribution of artworks, and audience mediation to connect processes with diverse publics. INVE’s curatorial vision fosters dialogue between artistic practices, critical reflection, and new forms of presentation, supporting artists from performing, visual, and audiovisual fields through residencies, seminars, talks, screenings, exhibitions, public performances, and distribution opportunities. Key programs include the international experimental video festival Proceso de Error, the Aberrante video and film cycle, the Cuerpo y Territorio performance laboratory, the Experimento INVE video creation residency (with 8 years of experimental cinema residencies in rural spaces), Ve en la Ola boat-based screenings, and Vórtice experimental video training lab. Since 2022, INVE has expanded its activities to Spain, strengthening its international outreach and building bridges between Latin American and European artistic communities through transnational exchanges and shared practices. Residency BASE - Before Form - Practice as a space for research and self-care Two editions in 2026: July 14–18 and September 9–13 in Valencia, Spain. BASE offers artists, curators, and researchers a shared territory of encounter — a pause to reconnect with the nature of their own practice.
