Here, the intimate and the collective intertwine, opening a space where each process can resonate in its own singular way. In this edition, practisioners are invited to a five-day retreat in a countryside house surrounded by nature, just outside Valencia, Spain. Through a series of practices designed to activate and support your creative process, the organisers will share: — Site-specific walks and drifts — Body-based activations — Observation practices — Writing sessions — Reflective spaces rooted in your own technique — One-on-one mentoring A program designed to help you reconnect with the core of your artistic methodology, within a carefully held environment and a horizontal approach to learning. At BASE, you step into your own time — a space to momentarily step outside linear dynamics, to ground your practice and observe it from a renewed perspective. A place to recognize coherence between life and work, as a creative being in constant transformation, expansive and free. The organisers understand this residency as: — A process-based laboratory of exploration — A space to move through questions with openness and safety — A community grounded in listening, generosity, and care — A parenthesis within the accelerated and hierarchical rhythms of society A place where: — The body is approached as an archive — Memory becomes material — Practice unfolds as a field in transformation At BASE, a state of sensitive exploration is activated. Throughout the residency, each participant will be able to: — Engage in dialogue with their practice from a broader perspective — Identify creative blocks and open new possibilities — Expand their creative language — Discover new ways of relating to their process — Situate their work within their context of interest Creating is also a way of imagining other ways of being in the world. And doing it together is a way of sustaining them.
studioInfo: The residency provides all materials and essentials needed for the proposed creative exercises — including readings, collaborative activities, and body-based practices designed for reflection, movement, and rest. Once selected, participants will receive detailed guidance on what to pack and practical suggestions to ensure a comfortable and enriching stay in the area.
accommodationInfo: The residency takes place at Masía La Toba, a restored traditional house immersed in nature, with direct access to a clear-water river suitable for swimming. Located in the province of Castellón, approximately two hours from Valencia International Airport. The surrounding landscape also offers opportunities for hiking and exploration.

name: arteventura
description: Deep in the Spanish inland, on a wooded estate of 25 hectares, lies the ecologic artist’s residency arteventura: A distinct philosophy of autonomy and back to basics form the foundation of the residency. The residency is for anyone who is professionally involved with art. This could be a visual artist, a writer, a performer, a playwright, a composer,… An artist that signs up individual or some artists that want to collaborate together to a project.
studioInfo: The finca covers an area of 25 ha of century old oaks which the visiting artists can fully enjoy at any time. In the front part of the finca there is a converted old ruin into a 300m2 communal studio with an indoor and outdoor workspace. The inner part of the studio can be divided into separate sections with mobile panels. In the outdoor part, a working-bench with accessories is available.
accommodationInfo: Each resident has its  own selfcatering apartment. Artists who apply individual will never share their apartment  with other residents. Artists who apply as a duo will share the 2 bedroom apartment. There are maximum 4 artists  at the same time (except if you come as a group): • 1 artists per flat of 40m2. • 2 artists, applying as a duo in the two bedroom apartment. You can find pictures of the different apartments under ‘live and workspaces’ Individual apartments of 40 m2: There are 2 individual apartments dispersed along the finca, with a distance of ±30 metres from each other and a short steep hike from the studio. Each apartment has it’s own kitchen, bathroom, 2 single fold up beds and a terras with view. These apartments are only suitable for 1 artist. They are set up as a flexible working are. Artists who prefer to work in their own flat can ask for extra tables. Two bedroom apartment: Next to the studio on the top floor, you can find an apartment with 2 (flexible) bedrooms , a big kitchen, 2 bathrooms and an individual terrace. The apartment can be used by a single artist (1 bedroom + 1 workspace), or by a duo (2 bedrooms) that wants to work on a joint project. Outdoor kitchen and/or additional working area: A fully equipped outdoor kitchen, build in an old ruin and situated on a quiet place on the Finca, is always available to all residents. Artists can also use this place as an additional working area. Wifi wifi is available but can drop out and is sometimes very slow. In Aracena you’ll find bars with free wifi.
technicalInfo: The artist is expected to bring his/her own materials. However, basic materials are available in the studio. In case residents need anything while on location there is a good specialised arts and crafts shop in nearby Sevilla, where they can order materials online. Further-more orders through Amazon are also available. It is also possible to buy some drawing materials (cheap, no name-brands) in a local supermarket in the village or visit the local crafts and tools shop. Organizers can help residents with their special requests and are in touch with several local craftsmen mainly working with metal, wood and cork. The studio assistant will help residents if and when necessary (e.g. installations etc).

name: Ses Dotze Naus Foundation
description: Ses Dotze Naus (the twelve vessels in Ibicencan) was created to foster and develop contemporary culture on Ibiza with a strong international profile. Our name is metaphor for the artists as vessels we bring to Ibiza to interact with the island, contribute ideas, and create cultural and social value. The Ses Dotze Naus Foundation develops artists’ residencies, exhibitions and public programs; contributing to the island as a place for creation, production and enjoyment of contemporary art. The foundation brings artists and thinkers to research and produce projects within the context of Ibiza, its narratives, and its culture. La Carpintería, their space for production, exhibition and encounter is located in an active industrial area. The foundation is firmly focussed on the future of the island, always having in mind its rich heritage while embracing its global audience. This is an open call for a two-phase residency hosted by SES DOTZE NAUS and available to: one visual artist or curator in based in the Balearic Islands; and two visual artists or curators based in Spain or elsewhere in Europe. During the first phase of their residency, participants engage with the island through research and exploration, fostering a rich contextual understanding. The second phase invites participants to return to the island to finalize their projects: the artists will produce their works, the curators will continue their research, and both will hold public activities and present the results of the projects developed during the residency. This framework enables participants to engage deeply with the island of Ibiza and its communities and to develop—or further expand—a project in dialogue with its context, encouraging new perspectives and ways of thinking that are inspired by the island. The residency takes place in two locations within the municipality of Santa Eulària des Riu, a district of Ibiza: accommodation on a 30-hectare farm in the center of the island, near the town of Santa Gertrudis de Fruitera; and workspace at La Carpintería, the Foundation's center for creation located in the Can Bufí industrial area near the city of Ibiza. The centre hosts creators from various disciplines.
studioInfo: Workspace at La Carpintería, the Foundation's center for creation located in the Can Bufí industrial area near the city of Ibiza. The centre hosts creators from various disciplines.
accommodationInfo: The residency takes place within the municipality of Santa Eulària des Riu, a district of Ibiza. The accommodation take places on a 30-hectare farm in the center of the island, near the town of Santa Gertrudis de Fruitera. The resident will be hosted in one private room in an apartment located on the property. The apartment has 2 bedrooms each with its own private bathroom and independent access from the garden. Shared kitchen and living room.
technicalInfo: Dimensions and furniture will be defined according to the needs of the project. Technical resources available include projectors, speakers, machinery, tools, and other equipment. Resources: SES DOTZE NAUS Foundation will also provide the selected candidates with the following resources: • Production assistance : to cover any potential needs for the public activities and presentations. • Travel: vehicle at your disposal throughout your stay. • Airport transfers. Support and guidance: The Foundation team will also offer support and guidance throughout the residency, sharing its knowledge of the island, facilitating connections with individuals, organizations, or local projects relevant to the work, and organizing informal meetings, among other forms of assistance.

name: PACA_Proyectos Artísticos Casa Antonino
description: PACA_ Proyectos Artisticos Casa Antonino was established as an artist run space, managed by Virginia Lopez, in an old country farmhouse in the rural area of Gijón, Spain. Casa Antonino is the true heart of the project, which uses it to maintain a domestic and familial dimension. PACA_ is a project focussed on contemporary art, environmental practices and artistic education, with international artist residency programmes. The objectives of PACA_Proyectos Artisticos Casa Antonino are to promote environmental and ecological practices and sensibilities in contemporary art; to carry out activities related to training, profusion, distribution and education; to create collaborative networks between local bodies, national and international institutions, universities, cultural foundations and institutions through interdisciplinary projects; to enhance local cultural organisations, fostering a dialogue between artistic communities and other members of society. The basis and common thread running through the diverse artist residencies organised at PACA is the activation of artistic experiences that promote relations with the local community, the region and its history. Site specific/site oriented interventions are planned for the various spaces of the farmhouse and its surroundings, so that the artistic practice, research and experimentation not only has a poetic and aesthetic value, but can also generate new ways of interpreting the territory with which it dialogues, through cultural, social and environmental values. PACA residency offers a workspace, housing, and include support, information and feedback from staff, other resident artists and PACA community: artists, curators, researchers. They always try to offer ideal conditions and artistic support for artist research and take specially care about connections between artist and local cultural agents. The house (traditional farm house called "Casa Antonino") has three bedrooms (one single and two double rooms), bathrooms, kitchen with firewood stove (kitchen), a living room, garden with water well and washing site. Residents can also use the common library of PACA and all the open space to work or produce site specific projects.
studioInfo: PACA Equipment/Resources: PACA Library, shared studio (working space) of 80 mq with: internet connection, computer, Epson print and scanner, Tascam digital recorder and microphones (contact and hydro-microphones), painting and generic tools, sink, work desk, video-projector, tripod, small dark room for analogical photography (photographic enlarger, no chemicals provided). Residents can also use all the open space to work or produce site specific projects: 1Ha with orchard and vegetable garden Support services for the development of artist project: logistics; curatorial and technical support -depending on project; dissemination of the project in PACA website and in PACA books publications and organization of public presentations in collaboration with museums and institutions related with artist’s project.
accommodationInfo: Housing in PACA : 3 private rooms (2 double rooms) + shared spaces: garden , land (1Ha), kitchen-living room, studio-library) + heating, electricity, internet costs and food (all meals will be prepared and decided by members of PACA, trying to include in the menu local products from PACA and surroundings, no alcoholic drinks included). The organizers have pets (dog and cats) in their private area and shared studio, but not in artist in residence area for accomodation.

name: Can Serrat
description: The international residency program invites writers and contemporary artists from all over the world for residencies of short and mid-term durations. Can Serrat holds open calls throughout the year and chosen projects are selected by a jury. One full grant for each call modality and several partial stipends are available. There is also an option to apply for the ‘ongoing call’ at any point during the year, but bear in mind no grants or stipends are provided for this option. The residency program supports writing and artistic production in process, offering time, space, individual and collective support, and a professional network since 1989. Monthly activities are organized to activate the individual projects in production and allow for connections amongst the residents, with the surroundings, and with locals: conversations, a book reading club, experimental translation exercises, visits to relevant spaces, a dinner open to the local community (summer time only), studio visits, and project presentations, to name a few. The organized activities reflect an interest in being present to process, research, question, doubt, understand, be curious, and debate. Can Serrat would be a good fit for someone who is looking for a studio space in a rural environment and who is interested in community living, art/literary connections, collaborations, process, and slowness. Unlike other programs, there is no obligation to produce final work or set up an exhibition at the end of your stay. Despite this, most residents still do. That’s because residents are free to self-organize any other relevant activities. The staff may also organize or propose relevant impromptu activities based on the interests of the group. As a live-work space, with many individuals and groups passing through throughout the year, Can Serrat experiments with sustainable ways for maintaining the household as well as being present for the work and content of everyone's practices. Part of the communal experience includes participating in the general cleaning of personal spaces as well as common areas.
studioInfo: An antique wine cellar, located on the ground floor, (260 m2) has been converted into a multi-use studio with facilities for printmaking and performance. 2 shared multi-use and inter-disciplinary studios (35 and 75 m2), all located on the first floor. During months of highest occupancy, please be aware that studio space will be limited (approx 15m2 per artist). Ample outdoor workspace (both covered and open). Manual printing press (80 cm wide), blankets, and a paper press. Various basic tools are available for use, but it is suggested that experienced printmakers bring their own tools. Basic printmaking knowledge is advisable as there is currently no studio technician. Please note the printmaking studio is NOT set up for acid etching. Equipment which can be used freely by all artists includes: easels, drawing boards,, projector, and various hand tools. Materials that must be brought or purchased locally are inks, plates, varnish, personal specific tools, paper, canvas, paints, brushes, etc. Please share studio space and common materials according to occupancy and respect other artists’ privacy and creative process while working in the studios.
accommodationInfo: 12 rustic and charming bedrooms of various sizes, for single, double, triple or quadruple accommodation. Linen and towels are provided upon arrival and residents can use the washing machine located in the bathroom area to wash their sheets, towels, and other personal items during their stay. It is expected that each individual clean their bedroom during their stay and before departure. A community bathroom with sinks, 3 private toilets, and two private showers are available on the ground floor, and cleaned on a weekly basis, as well as other common spaces like reception, living room, kitchen, etc. In addition to 1/week cleaning service, residents are expected to chip in with household chores. A base of food supplies is provided. Monthly deliveries of dry goods are made, as well as a weekly delivery of fresh fruits and vegetables. A communal dinner is prepared on Friday evenings and for all other personal items, a grocery store is within walking distance of the residency. There are a number of restaurants located in and near the village that offer lunch menus at very affordable prices. The residency kitchen has a microwave, toaster, water boiler, coffee machine, pots and pans for cooking, and plates and utensils.

name: Espacio Lavadero
description: LAV is an international artist residency program at Espacio Lavadero, based in Granada (Spain). The objective is to accommodate contemporary artistic creation, serving as support for the current artistic sector of emerging international artists. The residence offers a space for creation and also a place for exhibition and dissemination. Their space provides a comfortable and comfortable place, based on coexistence and community, with independent work areas and an exhibition room for specific events.
studioInfo: The creation studios are located in Espacio Lavadero, where each artist has a work area where they can develop their personal project. The work area has tables and chairs, bathroom, internet access and tools such as easels, screen, projector, printer, etc. It also has a microwave, refrigerator and coffee maker.
accommodationInfo: The apartment is dedicated exclusively to the residence of artists. Located in the centre of Granada, and very bright, it is an ideal space for our artists to feel comfortable. The apartment is designed so that two residents can live together simultaneously, and includes: Two private rooms Kitchen Bathroom Terrace Internet access Bed linen Air conditioning

name: Who Cares?
description: Who Cares? is a program supported by Creative Europe focusing on care practices, seeking to permeate through the participating organisations' infrastructure and programmes. The initiators ask: who we are caring for, in order to build in interdependence with the communities with which they develop our activity as art production centres? It is a collaboration of Idensitat (Barcelona), SPACE (London), Rupert (Vilnius), Grey Area (Korcula) and Centro Huarte (Navarra). In the framework of the European project Who Cares? Centro Huarte offers an international residency program for two or more artists that will take place from 1 September to 24 October 2021 . When coming from abroad, the residency may be brought forward or extended with 2 more weeks. This residency will take place in Habitación in Centro Huarte. Habitación is a hybrid project between residency and exhibition, in which artists make use of the work space and it is open to the public on weekends. During the process, the artists will share their work and process also on the Who Cares? website and will get a personalized assessment by a mentor working on the theme they propose. Topics We are looking for a project developed by two artists or more, established as a collective, that explores art as a place for dialogue and exchange of methodologies, delving into care, affects and knowledge transfer. An approach to the local community for the development of the process will be positively valued. Since the possibilities of physical encounters have been radically reduced in the last year, initiatives that understand artistic practice as a tool of collective resistance to go through this period of disruption and social change will be supported. In other words, projects are encouraged to investigate care and affective practices in relation to the current moment we are living. Topics to be addressed may include (but are not limited to): Affective and care networks, in relation to the local area Mental health, psychic pain, social discomfort Adaptation and self-recovery, body capacity Sustainability of life in times of pandemic Art as a generator of other ways of being Economic precariousness, but also affective and emotional precariousness Artistic tools for interpersonal transformation Ways to silence fear and curb hatred The political dimension of affects and emotions Eligibility Two artists or a collective from any field, based in Europe. Preferably fluent in the local languages (Spanish and/or Basque). Exceptionally, a project could be chosen for artists who do not have a knowledge of these languages, but have a great experience in working with collectives. The deadline for submission of proposals is May 27, 2021, at 23:59 (UTC +2). Projects submitted after that time will not be considered. The selection will be communicated within a maximum period of 1 month from the closing date of the call.
studioInfo: Work space at the Centro Huarte, including existing technical and technological resources: https://www.centrohuarte.es/centro-de-produccion/laboratorios-de-produccion
accommodationInfo: This residency will take place in Habitación in Centro Huarte. Habitación is a hybrid project between residency and exhibition, in which artists make use of the work space and it is open to the public on weekends.

name: CALLE MAYOR 54
description: Calle Mayor 54 is a residency program starting 2017; renovated 1920's house where artists are invited to reflect and produce art in a small village surrounded by nature. Calle Mayor 54 is a private initiative whose objective is to boost the art in remote areas. It is opened to visual artists with no age limit, nor restriction on nationality. Artists are selected by an application process. Calle Mayor 54 is located in the centre of Lumbier, which is a small village with a population of approximately 600 in winter, and 2.500 in summer. If you would like to attend a lot of parties, meet many artists, go to interesting art exhibitions, then, maybe Calle Mayor 54 is not for you. If you would like to have a quiet studio, time and space for reflection, share daily life with three more artists and enjoy nature, then this could be a place for you.
studioInfo: Living and working space are mixed. Three studios are for non-dirty stuff. There is one extra studio for dirty stuff. Unfortunately, and by the moment, there is not space for superdusty works, as plaster dust, wood dust etc.
accommodationInfo: 2 studios connected with bedroom 1 big studio + separated bedroom 1 shared bathroom 1 shared terrace with a view 1 shared kitchen and dining-room
technicalInfo: There is mid 20th century piano and a sewing machine.

name: Ey!Studio
description: The Ey!Studio AiR residency program takes place at Ey!Studio, an independent creation space located in Carabanchel (Madrid), one of the city’s most active areas for contemporary artistic production. Since 2017, Ey!Studio has hosted more than 65 artists, consolidating itself as a space for work and artistic development. The residency offers a private studio that combines accommodation and workspace in the same space, designed for independent artistic practice and individual research. Each resident manages their time, creative process, and use of the studio autonomously. Projects developed during the residency may receive visibility through publications on Ey!Studio’s website and social media, as well as possible future participation in screenings, exhibitions, or collaborations with independent spaces at national and international levels. There is also the possibility of selling work produced during the residency through an associated online gallery. The program is open to artists, curators, and researchers of any nationality and discipline, with a particular affinity for the visual arts. Residencies last from 2 weeks to 3 months, with 1 to 8 residents per period, across different programs.
studioInfo: Office: The 40 m2 space is air-conditioned and has a large dining table and an armchair for relaxing, reading, etc. The office is equipped with a fridge, microwave, two induction hobs, capsule coffee machine, kettle, toaster, and other kitchen utensils. They do not have a washing machine, although there is a laundry 9 minutes from the studio). Polyvalent Space: A 40 m2 multi-purpose space. This space can be used for workshops, exhibitions, video viewings, visits by professionals, presentations of publications, etc. (If Space 3 does not have a resident artist, depending on availability, it can be used as a workspace by the other resident artists without additional payment).
accommodationInfo: The studios are designed as private spaces that combine accommodation and workspace in a single unit, intended for individual artistic practice. Studio 1: Approximately 20 m², with private WC in a shared bathroom. Studio 2: Approximately 20 m², with a private bathroom for exclusive use. Shared area: Communal kitchen.

name: Enclave Land Art
description: Enclave Land Art OSAL, is a non profit association created in November 2016. Its aim is to build international projects linked to contemporary art and any other creative expressions. With an educational purpose, their philosophy is to spread contemporary culture. Enclave wants to encourage any kind of people to create sensitive synergies between contemporary art and the world that surrounds them. Open call artistic residency 2021 Enclave Land Art and the Vall de Gallinera council (Alicante, Spain) with the support of Cultura Resident from Consorci de Museus de la Comunitat Valenciana and the Direcció General del Cultura i Patrimoni de la Generalitat Valenciana, are glad to announce the open call for the 3rd Edition of the Enclave Land Art Residency. Submissions should focus on the dialogue between human beings and nature so as to create an artistic Land Art itinerary in the area. 7 projects from different artistic disciplines will be selected to be developed and produced in the natural environment during the two weeks of the Art Residency, sharing experiences, ideas and a common goal. All projects must take into consideration people's interest in contemporary arts, aiming to give greater value to the area of Vall de Gallinera, promoting a deep and permanent conscience about the historical, cultural and traditional aspects of the territory through a dialogue between art and nature. Concept "Truly memory does not consist at all of a regression from the present to the past, but rather in a progress from the past to the present." Bergson H., Matter and Memory, 2006. The power of intangibleness in art could be considered to be the core of creation and transformation: perception, habits, culture, language, time or memory can be channels used to define artistic research. This symbiosis between tangible and immaterial is what, along with history, builds the identity of a territory. There are many important elements in Vall de Gallinera apart from its geologic structure and its natural heritage, like for example the vestiges from prehistory up to the civil war, passing through Iberian villages, funerary steles and medieval castles. This historical legacy, traces of human beings along the millennia, has been preserved in this enclave thanks to its natural idiosyncrasy. They are the physical result of a non-linear time that presents a dialogue of human beings with nature through its layers. These layers could be metaphorically a book (nature itself) where the territory's inhabitants have written their story and defined their identity. Nature has since forever been a spiritual source of research and inspiration for human beings. It is not a coincidence that one can see trees in the forms of the columns in the churches, or caves in the arches, and many other examples. This union appears represented in different styles and functions, and in what remains when time and various factors alter them. Due to this connection between absence/presence that is preserved nowadays, the inner identity has been reinforced with nature as witness. These are the elements that the selected artists will be invited to reinterpret through their projects. Enclave Land Art aims to start a new chapter, leaving a contemporary trace to continue this dialogue with the environment through contemporary art. The relationship with what remains, together with what is not visible but nonetheless is present and forms part of Vall de Gallinera's people, represents who the locals are nowadays as a result of the path trodden. Disciplines Installation, land art, photography, anthropology, research, sculpture, performance and any other artistic manifestation or line of work in which the artist-territory-nature dialogue can be found within the specific nature of the environment in which the work will be developed and of the proposed idea. Open to artists of any age and nationality. For further information Enclave Land Art’s team suggest to upload the extended version of the open call. Timeline Duration of the open call: - From the 15th of August until the 10th of October 2021. Preselected Artists interviews: - From the 15th until the 19th of October 2021. Announcement of the Selected Artists: - 20th of October 2021. Residency period: - From the 22nd of November until the 5th of December included. - Projects will be presented to the public on the 4th and the 5th of December 2021.
studioInfo: Shared studios and a natural park to work.
accommodationInfo: Shared rooms (2 beds) in a full board basis.

name: Flame & Estudio Inverso residencies
description: Flame Asociación Cultural x Estudio Inverso is a dynamic creative partnership combining cultural advocacy, infrastructure, and five years of proven studio management in Madrid.Asociación Flame is a newly formed NGO dedicated to securing and promoting physical spaces for the contemporary arts. Founded by the owners of our Carabanchel industrial warehouse facility, Flame provides the long-term vision for international art events, festivals, exhibitions, and digital artist promotion.Estudio Inverso serves as our expert operational partner. Founded five years ago as a successful 10-artist "open walls" collective in the central Malasaña district, they expanded operations last year by joining forces with Flame’s founders to open an additional 13 specialized open studios within our newly renovated Carabanchel warehouse. Together, this joint venture bridges institutional support with hands-on studio management, embedding international resident artists directly into the vanguard of Madrid's contemporary art scene Flame x Estudio Inverso is an independent, monthly contemporary art residency designed to embed international creators directly into Madrid’s most dynamic cultural hubs. The program operates on a unique dual-location urban concept: residents live in the central, trend-setting neighborhood of Malasaña—ideal for cultural immersion—and work in Carabanchel, the recognized epicenter of Madrid's underground contemporary art scene. Based within a newly renovated industrial warehouse featuring 13 independent open studios, our primary objective is to provide visual artists and researchers with the optimal infrastructure for independent project development, peer-to-peer cross-pollination, and local professional integration. Key Highlights & Activities: Production Space: 24/7 access to a dedicated workspace within an active, collaborative open-studio warehouse. Scene Promotion: Regular, strategic features across our established social media channels, giving artists direct visibility to Madrid’s network of curators, collectors, and art professionals.Funding Support: Provision of comprehensive, itemized invitation documentation to fully support artists applying for external mobility bursaries (such as Arts Council England or Culture Moves Europe). The residency serves as a seamless, professional launchpad, combining a premium living environment with deep roots in the Spanish contemporary art market.
studioInfo: The creative workspace is located at Calle Blandón, 1, in Carabanchel, the recognized industrial epicenter of Madrid’s contemporary underground art movement. Residents enjoy 24/7 access to a dedicated studio space within a newly renovated 320m² industrial warehouse, which is subdivided into independent open studios ranging between 16m² and 20m². Operating under an open-walls concept, the facility features exceptional natural light, a front area utilized as an active exhibition space, and communal amenities including a fully equipped kitchenette and toilets. Additionally, the warehouse features an on-site recording studio, which is highly suited for musical or sound artists and can be accessed via separate bookings. Fully equipped with high-speed Wi-Fi and electricity, this collaborative environment is intentionally designed to foster critical dialogue and peer-to-peer cross-pollination while embedding international creators directly into Spain's contemporary art market.
accommodationInfo: Residents are hosted in Malasaña, one of Madrid's most historically vibrant, safe, and culturally rich central neighborhoods. Accommodation consists of a premium private bedroom inside a secure, high-quality, and fully furnished shared two-bedroom apartment. The apartment is fully equipped with high-speed Wi-Fi, modern appliances, and utilities, all included in the residency fee. Located just steps away from independent galleries, cafes, and restaurants, the living space provides the ultimate urban cultural immersion, with direct, 25-minute Metro connections (Line 5) leading straight to your dedicated workspace at the Flame x Estudio Inverso warehouse in Carabanchel.
technicalInfo: The facility features a versatile, high-ceiling layout with a maximum vertical clearance of 3.3 meters in the highest sections, offering ample vertical space for large-scale installations and visual art production. Structural security is maintained via a heavy-duty, lockable metal accordion gate system at the primary entrance. For comfort and climate control, the warehouse utilizes freestanding heating units alongside portable air conditioning systems, complemented by direct access to a communal roof terrace for outdoor breaks and ventilation. Standard electrical supply outlets are distributed throughout the workspace, and essential amenities include fully functional toilet facilities and a communal kitchenette. This configuration balances industrial functionality with necessary daily comfort for long-term project development.

name: Artist and Researcher in Residence Guiniguada
description: Artist and Researcher in Residence Guiniguada is open for artists and academic researchers. Their ideal of the residency is providing a place for recharging in a rural setting, and at the same time, also providing a micro-community for exchanging ideas. Rural retreat in a village in Northern Midhills of the island of Gran Canaria - a traditionally agricultural area, not the touristic coast. Focuses: botanics, food production / carbon chain, natural tints, landscapes, colonialism, transatlantic multiculturalism, gender issues, art of light.
studioInfo: Studios are individual and with a view on the valley looking Northwest.
accommodationInfo: Accomodation in the studio, individual or shared only with partner.
technicalInfo: Large desks, wall surfaces, outdoor working spaces.

name: casArte El Hierro
description: Bimbache openART / Asociación Bimbache P.O.C.S. is a registered non-profit and non-government organization dedicated to sustainable ecological, technological and socio-cultural development. Members and associates include leading artists, scientists, thinkers, representatives of different spiritual traditions, politicians, organizations of disabled persons and regular people around the world. Laboratory of human sustainability: Once a year Bimbache openART creates a festival in El Hierro. Artists from different places come, live and work together with people from the island. The purpose is to connect professionals, community-based artists, students and regular people in a live-and-learn experience so as to investigate sustainable possibilities of music and arts as a vehicle for social activism and civic engagement. The annual BIMBACHE openART summer laboratory and global academy offers open spaces, interdisciplinary round tables (tagoror), workshops and courses designed not only to improve technical skills but also to increase our understanding of the human being. The intention is to illuminate various ways in which artists and others can define and support their own course of creative activism and shape their own personal strategies for progressive social change. Residency: casArte El Hierro, the Zero Meridian Art Space, is a sanctuary for artists and thinkers to question and expand personal boundaries of perception. The residency program provides a place to connect with like-minded practitioners of other disciplines and cultures as well as with El Hierro’s sustainable way of living, its community and the art of nature. The hosts provide a space where people can reconnect and come into action to work together for the biosphere, humanity and peace. The residency program is open to people of all ages and backgrounds, and the hosts welcome all those who are looking for space and time to explore new forms of interdisciplinary and intercultural collaboration. Or who simply seek to expand their own creative inclinations. casArte's vision is: to create an environment and offer the facilities conducive to creative work, integrated with the natural surroundings and community, a place to experience new perspectives and acquire new references. to promote international collaboration and networking, to bring together people from all walks of life to share and promote El Hierro’s ecological way of living as well as its rich natural and historic heritage, and to further its development as a beacon for ecological and cultural sustainability. to provide and nurture a safe place where representatives of all disciplines and cultures can leave their customary comfort zone and encounter each other as a source of mutual inspiration. to preserve the local artistic heritage, to restore the old while developing new skills, practices and traditions of community self-reliance. to embrace and emphasize the experimental, the unsure, the insecure, the undefined and unexpected states of creativity.   Residencies at casArte are self-directed. casArte offers no formal calendar or program. Residents must take it upon themselves to decide the level of their productivity and participation. casArte invites and encourages residents to present the work done during the residency at the annual Bimbache openART festival. casArte is collaborating with universities and other institutions connected to art, sustainability and science. The organization recently signed a convenium with the Faculty of Fine Arts of the University of Castilla-La Mancha and strive to collaborate with other institutions to give students and teachers worldwide the opportunity to benefit from the unique qualities of our beautiful island of El Hierro. Applicants who are interested in this collaboration should feel free to contact the casArte staff.
studioInfo: The space can be used for music, painting, sculpture, writing, research, retreat/meditation. It is not big enough for performing arts such as dance but the surrounding nature can provide for that and a larger space for yoga, dance etc. can be provided at El Sitio in La Frontera upon request.
accommodationInfo: 3 bedrooms:1x 2 individual beds; 1x double bed; 1x single bed 1x sofa in the bodega / gallery 2 work /living rooms 1 kitchen with eating area 2 bathrooms various outdoor spaces and terraces Groups up to 6 persons are welcome. Partners and family are welcome under the condition that everyone will somehow be involved - discuss this in advance with the hosts.
technicalInfo: Wi-fi and basic painting materials are available, everything else that is needed must be brought by the residents.

name: Matadero / El Ranchito
description: Matadero Madrid is a living, changing space catering for creative processes, participatory artistic training and dialogue between the arts. It was created as a contribution to reflection on our contemporary socio-cultural environment, as well as to support processes for constructing the culture of today and tomorrow. Set in one of the most important industrial architecture sites of early 20 th century in Madrid, it aims to become the city’s biggest centre for contemporary creation and a leading international space dedicated to present-day creation. Matadero Madrid is an initiative by Madrid Council’s Department of the Arts, in collaboration with other public and private entities. El Ranchito is a research project promoted by Matadero Madrid aimed at developing new strategies for fostering art institution-based creation and reflection by providing residencies for international artists, establishing connections with multiple local cultural agents and launching open calls as tools for energising the art scene. There are two open calls: 1. Artist in residence . Madrid’s cultural stakeholders are the ones who provide El Ranchito with a list of foreign artists with whom they would like to work or develop a joint project. El Ranchito offers a residency in Madrid of three to six weeks with a per diem allowance throughout the stay. The project resulting from this work may receive funding from El Ranchito in a subsequent stage and form part of its schedule of activities. 2 Workspace for artists . Different work modules are available for the city’s artists and collectives that may need them to develop a new project over a period of 3 months maximum. The number of artists benefitting from this call will vary according to the square metres of space and time requested.
studioInfo: The workspaces are in between 60 m2 and 120 m2 big, integrated in an open space

name: La Térmica - Creators
description: 'Creators' is La Térmica's artistic residency program. A commitment to supporting plastic and visual artists with a two-month scholarship, work-study, accommodation, food and financial support for the development of their projects. This is an annual call that brings together six artists every year at the Contemporary Culture Center of the Provincial Council of Malaga with the aim of promoting their projects. A total of 42 artists have been part of this international project since it has been carried out since 2013, with a total of six group exhibitions developed and exhibited at the Center as a result of the artistic work of the artists in residence.

name: IN-SONORA
description: In conjunction with the 11th edition of the IN-SONORA art exhibition, Medialab Prado is proud to announce an open call directed at audiovisual artists, asking for their participation in a collaborative production residency at the Medialab Prado headquarters. The residency period will extend from March 9 to March 22, 2020, in the Medialab Prado Headquarters in Madrid. Medialab Prado is a public workspace centered on the production, research and dissemination of cultural projects that explore forms of experimentation and collaborative learning in the advent of digital networks. It is also owned by the City of Madrid’s Department of Culture and Sports. During the residency period, Medialab Prado will provide the resident with a bedroom and a workshop area for the development of their project, as well as provide access to the institution’s facilities and available tools. Open call participants whose projects (textual, photographic or visual) are selected must have their works licensed under a creative license that allows Medialab Prado the right to publish them in any physical or digital format, within the maximum territorial and temporal boundaries of the law and in accordance with what they deem to be the best method for their distribution. Once the works have been selected and presented within the course of this exhibition, the artist is obliged to allow any other participating individuals to utilize their work as a basis for the development or performance of any other derivative works. Participation in this open call implies the absolute acceptance of all its aforementioned policies. Agreement with selected participant: Selected participants agree to the finalization of adequate documentation covering their proposed projects. Selected participants agree to stay for three weeks between the dates indicated above. Accepted projects must embrace and encourage the participation of other individuals or creative who may be interested in attending any open workshops. Selected participants agree to lead the open workshops conducted for other registered participants. Basic information regarding the projects, concerning both their processes and results, is to be recorded in the Medialab-Prado collaborative work platform The participant must keep his/her code in a public access repository, allowing for the reuse of their free license. The organization agrees to encourage and support the use of free programs for the development of projects. Once the residency period has concluded, participants agree to withdraw their materials within a maximum period of 15 days. After this period has passed, Medialab Prado reserves the right to do with them whatever it deems most convenient.
studioInfo: During the residency period, Medialab Prado will provide the resident with a bedroom and a workshop area for the development of their project, as well as provide access to the institution’s facilities and available tools.
accommodationInfo: See Studio Information.

name: Pico del Pañuelo
description: Pico del Pañuelo is a part of a wider project called Culture, Art and Society, which they define in the following terms: Creativity and art at the service of social change Social involvement Imaginary and cultural semiotics Collective thinking Dialogues with art Cultural projects that help build individual and social awareness, and change Cultural projects that help express and reflect on the social reality Projects for cultural innovation and social dialogue
studioInfo: There is no specific studio. Residents can work on their laptops, or with the help of the organization, they can rent a theatre studio nearby.
accommodationInfo: An apartment with two rooms, lounge and kitchen.
technicalInfo: They will contact and/or provide contacts with resources the residents need.

name: Cel del Nord
description: Cel del Nord provides a physical as well as a virtual environment, removed from the expectations of everyday life – a distraction-free, and inspiration-rich space to do extraordinary creative work. They have an atmosphere of inclusion for artists who might have followed unconventional paths in the arts. By taking part in the programs, creative people join an expanding network of peers to connect with and seek support from them. Ce del Nord offers an evolving program of events and activities for residents and past-residents. Vision - A physical and virtual environment, removed from the expectations of everyday life. - An atmosphere of inclusion for artists who might not have undertaken conventional career paths in the arts. - A constantly expanding network of peers for our residents to connect with and seek support from. - An evolving program of events and activities for residents and past-residents. - Financial self-sufficiency for the organisation balanced against affordability for residents. Purpose - To provide a physical or virtual structure inside which creative ideas and practices can be tested, explored and expanded. - To connect creative people so they can nurture peer-to-peer relationships. - To support groups and individuals in finding solutions to creative blocks and hurdles through encouragement and guidance. Values Cel del Nord values artists based on their commitment to a creative practice above all else. For example; - Those who have made a career of their creative practice. - Those who have made a career of their practice even if that career doesn’t include selling art work. - Those who commit to a practice whilst also undertaking paid work. - Those who commit to a practice alongside caring for dependents. - Those who have committed to a practice later in life. Transparency Cel del Nord is a white-European founded and run organisation. As of June 2020 they subsist on voluntary contributions, fees and donations while pursuing arts funding. They strive towards cultural sensitivity and actively seek to create a program that is inclusive of people from all backgrounds and promotes cultural racial equity. They do not consider an artist’s sales, social media following, prestige or attendance at high-brow institutions as part of their selection process.
studioInfo: 50m2 area with 4m high ceiling Large windows on opposite walls Natural northern light Four bright overhead lights Portable work lamps Sink with hot and cold running water
accommodationInfo: Two private rooms and one room shared between two. Shared facilities.
technicalInfo: Two Mabef M07 H-Frame adjustable easels with boards and clips Short throw video projector and stereo system Pegs and drying line Empty wall space (for pinning things) Nitrile gloves, rags, newspaper, glass jars, turps, vegetable oil, baby wipes Gelli plate and roller Modest library Large outdoor space / outdoor desk space Superfast WiFi

name: a cobert
description: a cobert is a place for artistic creation, production and research located in Moià (Barcelona) that supports artists through residencies, workshops, and critical thinking activities. Rooted in feminist and community-based values, the organisers aim to make art accessible and closely connected to everyday life, collaborating with local communities, schools and cultural organizations to strenghten the regional artistic and cultural ecosystem. The organisers are interested in emerging artists and experimental and critical practices, seeking to give them the space, resources, support and display to grow and keep on creating in a meaningful and ethical way. a cobert’s residency programme provides artists and researchers with the space, resources, and support needed to develop creative and research projects in a unique rural environment that fosters focus and experimentation. Beyond artistic production, the program emphasizes public engagement, community participation, and knowledge exchange, making contemporary art accessible to local audiences as well as promoting national and international circulation. The residences are aimed at artists and researchers over the age of 18, as well as groups of people in creative processes, from any field and artistic discipline: plastic arts, visual arts, performing arts, literature, cinema, performance, science and technology, gender studies, history, etc. They do not host musical projects due to their specificity. The residences are open to people of any nationality and language as well as without age limit or distinction of origin, current residence, gender, sexual orientation, etc. They work with small groups, with a simultaneous stay of between 2 and 4 people, to make coexistence between projects something non-distorting and to be able to offer the care, space and artistic advice that the projects require with quality and dedication.
studioInfo: The studio is a 28 m2 room that opens to an outdoor garden. Video, sound, and visual arts equipment, as well as a library, all accessible to resident artists. The space includes an individual desk and a large table for groups or meetings.
accommodationInfo: The accommodation is located just a few metres from the studio, at Cal 13 Bis. They offer an individual room with access to fully equipped shared spaces: kitchen, living room, terrace, bathroom.

name: las dunas
description: Motivation Because there is a local need for an international platform for art and we want to share with others their space, facilities and expertise. Offering tranquility and the opportunity to simply have space and time to focus on their own work in a place surrounded by an incredible beauty. The space House located 1 km from the Natural Park of Las Dunas de Corrubedo in a family farm with swimming pool, tennis court, large garden areas and barbecue area with outdoor table made by stone. It has independent pedestrian and road access. Although the house/studio is well connected by public transport, they offer a bicycle, because the place is isolated surronded by an incredible beauty over the Natural Park of Las Dunas de Corrubedo. Las Dunas Air Program Each AiR program is embedded in, and conditioned by its specific situation. Which conditions determine most the profile, the content and the purpose of the las dunas AiR program? How the house is located in the countryside, the studio is quiet and it can be used only for the artist who is selected. It is possible that he or she brings his or her family (there is space for four) There are not other users or artists, although how this residence is made by artist for artist after the interview we can manage to support artistic and professionally our Artist in Residence. There is the possibility to meet the local community and make some workshops (children and adults) presentations and exhibitions. For your work they offer art and culture library. a connection with spanish and portuguese artistic and cultural organizations. participation in group exhibition or event. publication on our virtual networks. assistant to help you with your projects. working spaces and facilities. information about galician art scene, exhibitions and culture. printer and office material. basic art materials. For your everyday life they offer: welcoming wine and fresh fruit private/double bedroom (incl. towels and bedlinen). fully equipped kitchen facilities. bikes. pick-up service for arrivals and departures. wi-fi connection in all spaces. barbecue, pool and gardens. laundry facilities. weekly cleaning services.
accommodationInfo: Working and living space are under the same roof and location. It has two bedrooms, one of them equipped as a study, bathroom with shower, fully equipped kitchen, fireplace, washing machine and closed living room with fantastic views towards Las Dunas.

name: El Corralito
description: Every year, El Corralito promotes different residency programs in different modalities for projects by emerging artists. In this way, they seek to consolidate contemporary artistic practice, both locally and nationally. El Galliner is the name of the creative space where the residences take place, an open space where people have access to support and accompaniment from the organization. The main objective is to offer support to young people so that they can develop their own research in the arts, as well as to bring them closer to the network of cultural and artistic resources from the city. El Galliner is a space that works dynamically, depending on the artistic projects. A diaphanous space where you can develop your research in visual arts such as painting, drawing, design, fashion design, photography, or audiovisuals. They can also inquire about other fields.
studioInfo: The El Corralito creative space, known as "El Galliner," spans 230m2 and is divided into a central, open, and multidisciplinary area, two office spaces, a dining area, and restrooms. The entire space is shared with other ongoing projects, providing artists with the opportunity to coexist with other creations happening simultaneously.

name: Land of Enchantment: The residency
description: Land of Enchantment is a Cultural Asociación that supports artistic development, ecological awareness and well being. Through art workshops, performance nights and residencies they (re)learn together what it means to live sustainably and in harmony with each other, and the land. The homebase is a rustic eco home surrounded by forest near the coast of poetry, cliffs, wild storms, lighthouses and crystal beaches. They believe that the planet needs as many dots on the map as possible where humans, animals and plants can thrive in harmony. The center is meant to be one of these dots. The residency programs stem from the mission to transform rural locations into vibrant artistic hubs. Therefore the events are meant as a meeting space between the local community and international artists. Every start of the season they welcome 3-10 residents to work in community on their practice. You come to the essence of your work, re-align your workflow to the seasonal rhythm, get things done and be inspired by the landscape of Costa da Morte and the fellow-creators in the house. The common ground is to use creation as a tool for well being social justice, personal transformation, building community or ecologic awareness. Including Daily movement practices with work out, dance or yoga Access to shared music & art studio Weekly group intervision & optional 1:1 mentorship for your project Nutritious meals prepared together in community Fill your cup with inspiration by Galician traditions, cuisine & poetry Hike along the majestic lighthouse path of Costa da Morte Ocean bathing and silent walks through the forest Performance nights with the local community by the fire Co-creation with 3-10 kindred spirits Daily rhythm 8:00 Meditation & journaling 8:30 Movement: work out / dance / yoga 9:30 Creation session 1 12:30 Lunch 14:00 Creation session 2 17:30 Mini masterclass: every weekday led by one of the residents who shares an inspiration (book, exercise, practice,..) 19:30 Dinner
studioInfo: 35m2 Sound & Movement studio for solo rehearsals, performance nights and morning practices, PA system, guitar, amp, mics, stand. 18m2 Writers space 30m2 Open garage/workspace with 4 armatures for sculpting
accommodationInfo: The residency is close to many beaches of la Costa da Morte, cliffs, lighthouses and rivers. The property is on a land of 1 acre surrounded by forrest on the edge of a little village in province A Coruña. The house has four double bedrooms (four private bedrooms with double beds and one shared bedroom with two one person beds) with a shared mosaic nature bathroom, a wild camping place, a bell tent, compost toilet, outdoor shower and plenty of space to park a van.

name: Casa Planas Creative and Cultural Centre
description: The Cultural Center of Creació Casa Planas is the result of the efforts of three creatives to restore an old photography factory and transform it into a necessary platform for the city of Palma. Casa Plan promote culture by creating a platform for experimentation, research and creativity. Through visual, musical and scenic art shows that we organize from Casa Planas, there is a constant criticism of the ways of interpreting the culture and the "museification" of it, questioning the formal and aesthetic registers of art. At the Creation Centre Casa Planas, it is available to have research residencies for creators and thinkers around art. The duration varies depending on the needs of the project. Art mediation projects that have a direct social relationship with our field of work and our neighbourhood, or projects that are related to the theme of archives, postcards, landscape, tourism and memory and which bring life into the Casa Planas archive and keep it from falling into oblivion, are especially valued. There is a special focus on the areas of visual media, performance and art mediation. Casa Planas develops workspaces, research processes, the possibility of roundtables, knowledge-sharing workshops, meetings between artists, curators, collectives and other professionals in the sector in this programme.
studioInfo: Available studio space of 15m2 Access to the extensive photography archive of Josef Planas (best tourist photographic archive of images from 1950-1980) -access dependent on the project. Access to the activities available in the cultural centre as well as the coworking space.
accommodationInfo: Studio only, maximum 2 residents at a time, no groups, partners or family
technicalInfo: Wifi internet, printing facilities, projector and A/V equipment, old photographic cameras, video cameras and monitors, meeting room, exhibition space and community spaces.

name: L'Estruch
description: L’Estruch, Fábrica de creació de les arts en viu is a Sabadell council equipment with more than twenty years path that reaches a broad spectrum of the contemporary artistic practices. L’Estruch is distinguished by searching permeability amongst disciplines such as dance, circus, visual arts, performance, sound experimentation and technologic development. Its results nourish the international artistic circuit but also other spheres as the social, academic or industrial ones. Nauestruch is the specialized area in visual arts and performance, with specific attention in proposals that work with body politics. The goals of Nauestruch residencies are: Supporting artistic practice. Supporting the professionalization of the artistic sector. Being a space for exchange between Sabadell, its cultural context and its resident artists. Establishing links between local artistic community and others from national nor international ones. Blurring limits among disciplines, genders or the diversity of cultural manifestations. Creating a temporary group of work and decision made up by the residents.
studioInfo: Private working space depending on the needs of the project.
accommodationInfo: Accommodation in a shared room.
technicalInfo: Transdisciplinar working environment. Conceptual assistance for the development of the proposals. Introduction in the cultural context of Sabadell and Barcelona. Promotion and dissemination made by Nauestruch. List of materials

name: NAT Art Residence
description: The Residence: The house is located in Tagle, Suances Town Hall, Cantabria, in the north of Spain. They are immersed in a geographical space full of human activity for many thousands of years and with an important heritage of Palaeolithic art. Altamira, Monte Castillo and Covalanas are the best known examples of the many existing caves in the region that preserve our first works of art. Many thousands of years ago, a first person looked for the elements, generated the pigments, elaborated the tools, selected the space, observed the environment in detail, decided that he / she wanted to capture, went into the depth and darkness of a cave and, once there, in an awkward position, he / she created. Creating means making something out of nothing. The origin of art is what guides the organisers in their art programs, taking it as a reference for a new beginning and nature as the starting point to achieve it. It is always a good time to start, restart, explore changes, look for new languages, or simply step out of our comfort zone. Surrounded by this magic and its surroundings, our residents from all disciplines of the arts will develop their projects here. Andrea Juan and Gabriel Penedo Diego will carry out continuous monitoring and support on the evolution of your project to encourage and stimulate its development until, at the end of the residency, you have transformed it into a work. They offer to the Artists: • Accommodation for 12 nights in a private room. • Amenities consisting of food and cleaning supplies for individual or general use such as coffee, tea, milk, cookies, oil, rice, etc. Fresh products or those not included in the detailed list in the annex “Price and Conditions” will be paid by the resident. • Transfer of the group to and from the city of Santander (or its airport) on your arrival and on your departure. • Visit at the National Museum of Altamira, including tickets and transfers, accompanied by Andrea and Gabriel. • Visits, in two days, to the caves with Rock Art of El Pendo, Las Monedas, El Castillo and Covalanas. Includes entrance fees, transfers and lunches and the full-time guide of Andrea and Gabriel. • Guidance and advice in the development of your work through individual and group talks, daily visualization and monitoring of your work in progress by Andrea Juan and Gabriel Penedo Diego. • Artists will be included to this site, in “Artists”, spreading the works carried out during your residency. Artists are able to know more about us here: www.circleproart.com/en-gb/nuestros-directores And about the house here: www.circleproart.com/en-gb/nuestra-casaa0775b89 The spots are of 12 nights / 13 days. NAT ART RESIDENCE 2026 dates: May 4 to 16; May 18 to 30; June 1 to 13 and June 15 to 27.
studioInfo: All disciplines are accepted in Nat Art Residence. Visit at the National Museum of Altamira, including tickets and transfers, accompanied by Andrea and Gabriel. Visits, in two days, to the caves with Rock Art of El Pendo, Las Monedas, El Castillo and Covalanas. Includes entrance fees, transfers and lunches and the full-time guide of Andrea and Gabriel. Guidance and advice in the development of your work through individual and group talks, daily visualization and monitoring of your work in progress by Andrea Juan and Gabriel Penedo Diego. Artists will be included on www.circleproart.com/artistas site, in "Artists”, spreading the works carried out during your residency. Also, artists can see on our website www.circleproart.com/en-gb/charlas some video Talks where resident artists tell us about their experiences and show their works. There are Talks in English and Spanish. Studio / Workspace There is a studio with a large window overlooking the meadow, but our goal is for artists to work and develop their works in the natural environment in amazing landscapes: beach, cliffs, meadow, sea, river and marsh. They have a green area around the house for the artists to work. They can set installations and site specific, develop their projects, or just to paint or draw there.
accommodationInfo: Artists stay at a beautiful house, nestled in a wonderful rural environment, on the coast of the Cantabrian Sea, in Suances, in the north of Spain. This is the home of resident artists, and our operational headquarters, studio, meeting and exhibition space. The house has three bedrooms, a full bathroom, a toilet, a kitchen-dining room, a living room, a covered outdoor studio, an exhibition room and its own green space. The stone house, an old farmhouse of more than 100 years, has been restored by us to provide it with all the comforts that make it comfortable to be at ease, enjoy the environment and dedicate yourself exclusively to create. The house is located in a wonderful natural environment 700 meters from imposing cliffs and about 1000 meters from Tagle beach. It is located 2 km from Suances and 7 km from the Altamira National Museum in Santillana del Mar. Sea, beach, cliffs, forests, caves, rivers … Spaces that will be the perfect inspiration and support framework for your works.
technicalInfo: For more information, refer to their conditions .

name: Isla De Crear
description: Isla de Crear is a creative centre that combines a range of different disciplines in order to explore creating and crafting in a new method, away from commercial constraints or industry guidelines, based on the principles of the Fantasism manifesto. They are open to people of all ages and backgrounds, and only ask that you have a keen interest in proactively seeking strange and unique connections, through interdisciplinary and international collaboration.
studioInfo: Apart from your en-suite accommodation and shared living spaces, they offer 8 different workspaces, a 50 sqm dance studio with a wooden floor, which can be used for rehearsals, a 300 sqm workshop space with machinery, some materials that can be repurposed, access to an office and supplies, a library, outside spaces, animals and their support and advice, but they ask that you read the Fantasism manifesto and ensure you subscribe to it. They also have a wood workshop and metal welding area. The machinery can only be used by people with relevant experience at dedicated hours.
accommodationInfo: They offer all creatives a private en-suite bedroom (with a toilet and shower), with a shared living space, which includes: a kitchen, a large living room, laundry facilities (to be used in agreement with the team), a library and many indoor and outdoor working spaces. All activities will be arranged with the other creatives and the team that live on the property. Creatives are also required to adhere to cleanliness and behave in a courteous and non-discriminative fashion. Rooms should be kept clean and returned in the same state they were when arrived. Isla de Crear is located 6 km from the nearest town of Úbeda, and comprises a large scrap yard, which you will be allowed to use at the discretion of the team. Apart from the communal kitchen, you will have the option of opting for other meals cooked by the team.

name: Nectar
description: Nectar presents its Artist Family Residency, a program designed to support artists who are also parents, providing a space where they can develop their practice without having to put their family life on hold. They recognize that many artist residencies are not accessible to parents, as they often require extended time away and logistical challenges. As a result, many artists find themselves reducing or even pausing their creative work. To address this, Nectar Family Residency offers an environment where art and family life can coexist. The program provides accommodation, studio space, meals, and creative workshops for children. While artists focus on their work, their children can explore creativity through activities led by educators and artists. The residency aims to foster new ways of integrating artistic and family life, encouraging a balance between both. It welcomes artists with children aged 2 to 15 years old, accommodating between four and eight families. Additionally, artists may bring their spouse or partner, whether they are an artist or not. With this initiative, Nectar reaffirms its commitment to inclusive artistic creation, supporting families in an inspiring and enriching environment. What includes: - One-week residency for the artists-parents - Studio facilities - Accommodation (Private room per family) - Food supplies* - Children Workshops - Swimming pool - Other activities -Studio Visit *The Food supplies covers the three daily meals plus snacks/coffee/tea/juices/alcohol and non-alcohol drinks. In 2026, and in its third edition, Nectar is thrilled to announce a total of four Family Artist Residency weeks! The program will take place in the province of Tarragona, in inspiring and magical locations surrounded by nature, offering families the perfect environment to create, connect, and share. The four weeks are organized in two consecutive pairs, giving families the possibility to join for one or two weeks in a row. > June 27 – July 4 > July 4 – July 11 > July 20 – July 27 >July 27 – August 3
studioInfo: Studio spaces vary according to the proposed projects and media. Individual space and shared working studios are located in the main house. Indoor and outdoor spaces are open to the artist’s practice. Artists are also encouraged to use the nature and the environment that surrounds us as their workspace.
accommodationInfo: Each family is provided with a private room (or two, depending on the number of family members). The rooms are spacious and comfortable. Bathrooms are usually shared between 1–2 families.
technicalInfo: Library Printer Tools for wood and metal Projector and projector screen Depending on the activity, the organizers can provide different materials for the artists

name: Centro Huarte
description: Located in Huarte (Navarra), 4.5 km from the center of Pamplona, the Huarte Center, inaugurated in October 2007, is the first cultural facility in Navarra specifically designed to promote and disseminate contemporary art through exhibitions, activities, and residencies, paying special attention to the current art scene, emerging art, and multidisciplinary creation. The building was designed by the architects Franc Fernández, Carles Puig, and Xavi Vancells, a collective created for the practice of contemporary architecture established in Barcelona. The construction was completed in 2006, and the official opening was held in April 2007. Initially managed by the Ordóñez-Falcón Foundation, chaired by Enrique Ordóñez until 2009, who envisioned an art center that would transcend the merely exhibition space, linking artistic practice with education and reaching new audiences. After the Government of Navarra became the manager of the Huarte Center and it underwent an impasse, in 2011 Javier Manzanos was elected director, who promoted several pedagogical projects, as well as local projects, dance, and other exhibition works. From August 2016 until August 2022, the Center was directed by a collective of women formed by Elisa Arteta, Nerea de Diego, Betisa Ojanguren, and Oskia Ugarte, mainly focused on the creative process rather than the exhibition product. Since the end of 2022, the Foundation has approved Oskia Ugarte's solo management project, which continues to advocate for a center for artistic production, education, and research with a commitment to relate the different contemporary artistic agents to the community through mediation. 2023 Open Call: IDENSITAT and Centro Huarte will each offer a residency to an artist or a collective to develop a project within the social contexts of the towns of Huarte and Barcelona. The residencies have been conceived as hybrid, combining on-site presence with any off-site work to ensure the completion of the project. The on-site period will last approximately five weeks, to be carried out between September and December 2023, t.b.d. according to the availability of the selected artist or collective and the promoting organisations, depending on the project, with the further possibility of fulfilling the five-week period non-concurrently.
technicalInfo: The project will be carried out within a five-week residency, divided into one stay of 1 or 2 weeks, and a later period of 3 or 4 weeks’ stay, both to take place between September and December 2023, the details to be specified taking into consideration the availability of the selected artist or group and the promoting organisations. The spaces available for the presentation of results and the performance of activities related to the project will be, apart from the Centro Huarte itself, the venues managed by the Mancomunidad de la Comarca de Pamplona (Commonwealth of the Pamplona Region), the Batán and the Molino de San Andrés (Atarrabia- Villava).

name: Theertha
description: Theertha International Artists’ Collective offers residency facility for visiting artists, writers and scholars for short and long-term stays in Colombo. Theertha is an artists’ led collective initiated in 2000 to work with contemporary artists to promote and encourage experimental art. Its own art space, Red Dot Gallery showcases innovative and experimental art. Theertha regularly holds sponsored international art residencies and exhibitions.
accommodationInfo: There are 2 rooms(Non AC), a well-equipped kitchen and studio space. Library, Wifi.

name: Bee Time
description: Bee Time artist residency explores the intersection of art and ecology. Their programs focus on researching the interrelationships between beekeeper, bee and landscape in a particular region, thus studying the influences of local culture and agriculture practices on the honeybee and vice versa. They introduce participants to concepts of bee centred beekeeping, and applied systems thinking. Working out of the understanding of the honeybee colony as a super-organism – a being with many individual bees comprising a unified consciousness, participants have the opportunity to practice self-organising social models inspired by hive consciousness by working together in a non hierarchical way.
studioInfo: The hosts have four large studio spaces in old Moorish water mills, next to a Roman aquaduct, various waterfalls, and swimming holes. They also work outside a lot in apiaries and in the outdoor spaces by the mills. Artists can let the hosts know what their needs are in terms of spaces and they can endeavor to find them the most appropriate space. There is a common kitchen space where hosts and artists cook and eat communally.
accommodationInfo: The hosts rent a house in the village which has four large bedrooms, with shared occupancy.
technicalInfo: There is an extensive library of bee related books for artist's use. The hosts can provide technical assistance, printing, and certain materials, subject to prior discussion.

name: hybrida.space
description: hybrida.space is an art/curatorial initiative launched by artists Giorgos Tsiongas (GR) & Joar Torbiörnsson (SE) in 2021, focusing on creating virtual/physical ground & open-ended curatorial frameworks, where artists can develop and show new work. They see a growing need for art practitioners to engage in an open, playful, transparent, and non-hierarchical exchange with one another, and to create fluid boundaries between different roles such as curators, organisers, and audience. As hybrida.space, they are seeking ways to facilitate this need by bringing creative individuals together and creating constellations, in which artistic freedom and experimentation are key components. Hence, their working logic follows the path of a curatorial and artistic experiment: a wager pushing the boundaries of what really makes a residency plan or an art exhibition. They are motivated by the question: how can one generate and sustain experimental ways of working in the art field? As an artist-driven initiative, they strive to offer the opportunity for peers in different stages of their careers to connect and to develop work under the following beneficial circumstances: they are given the freedom to experiment and an opportunity to create and display their work in an alternative context. Moreover, they get a chance to expand their (international) network and open up to new audiences. They also believe that artists should always receive fair pay for their work. They favor an open and experimental approach in regard to curation, collaboration, and making exhibitions. One that is all-inclusive in terms of medium, mode of production, nationality, gender, and ideology. They endorse collaborations based on mutual respect and meaningful exchange, starting from the common drive to create and reflect.
studioInfo: There will be a varied setup of electrical and handheld tools available on site. For what can’t be made on-site, there is a possibility to use professional workshops in the nearest city (Karlstad, 40 minutes drive). The area covers 300.000m² and they have access to a large two-story garage and the natural environment in the area, for the purpose of making and showing work.
