Since July 2012, allartnow closed its door in Syria to open it to Syrian refugee families and starts to work in different places in the world as a nomdic space. Click here to read an article about allartnow in 2014, "Tomorrow will be the beginning of a new life". If you would like to follow their updated events, please check their Facebook page.

name: Shinehouse Artist-In-Residence Program
description: The Dawn Theater Art Village is one of the few art villages in Taiwan with performing arts groups as its core operation. The team invites artists from different fields, both domestic and international, to reside in the historic site of the Wan-Zuo Dawn Theater (formerly the Taiwan Sugar Warehouse). Within these buildings rich in historical memory, a space has been created for dialogue and interaction among artists, the environment, and the public. Grants: NT$12,000 - NT$30,0000. Next to financial support, accommodation, a workspace for exchange and work, as well as assistance for rehearsals and exhibitions are provided.

name: Tsung-yeh Art and Cultural Center
description: Tsung-yeh Art and Cultural Center in Tainan City is the result of the fusion of an old sugar refinery with multicultural ideas to form a unique space. With years of effort, Tsung-yeh Art and Cultural Center has established itself as a center for arts, crafts and culture while producing valuable creative works in Tainan. Through providing the working space and encouraging resident artists to communicate with the locals, they hope to promote this historical site not simply as a place for exhibitions, but rather an important gathering site for international arts and artists. The theme for 2027 is “Site-Specific Art”. Artists shall observe the following contexts of Tainan City before creating works. The hydrology (including river basin and water management system), physiography (archaeological studies, soil, meteorology, or topographical variations), ecology (aquatic, amphibian, and terrestrial fauna and flora in the area), humanities (indigenous, agricultural, river-related, or ecology-related culture).
studioInfo: shared artist studio (with tables, chairs, and room partitions).
accommodationInfo: During the residency, each artist will be provided with: (1) a suite for accommodation (no charge for the room, utility bills, showering facilities. Personal items, such as towels and toothbrushes, are not provided). (2) a bicycle. (3) an exhibition space (including the setting of lighting rails, air conditioning, and relevant equipment). (4) a shared artist studio (with tables, chairs, and room partitions).
technicalInfo: (1) multimedia devices (used for the exhibition, including projectors, monitors, speakers, and lights. For more details, the list is posted on the official website). (2) a shared artist studio (with tables, chairs, and room partitions). (3) hardware tools required for creating artworks, such as electric drills.

name: Off Tropics
description: Off Tropics is a self-directed residency in Chiang Mai, Thailand, designed for artists, curators, producers, cultural organisers, writers, researchers, composers, filmmakers, and cultural practitioners seeking time, focus, and space for sustained work. Situated in a quiet residential area surrounded by greenery, the residency combines accommodation with a private studio environment suitable for writing, composition, research, editing, sound work, and small-scale artistic development. Founded by artists working internationally across sound, performance, and moving image, Off Tropics emerged from a desire to create the kind of place often missing between commercial accommodation and institutional residencies: an affordable environment where concentrated work, rest, and reflection can coexist. The residency is intentionally flexible. Residents may use the space for artistic research, project development, writing, remote work, or simply as a temporary base from which to engage with Chiang Mai's cultural landscape. Depending on availability, informal studio visits, artist conversations, introductions to local practitioners, and additional artistic or technical support may be arranged separately. Off Tropics prioritises autonomy, long-form thinking, and the conditions necessary for meaningful creative work.
studioInfo: The residency includes a private live/work studio located in a quiet residential area of Chiang Mai. The space comprises a 36 m² loft with sleeping and workspace areas suitable for writing, research, composition, editing, and project development. An additional 36 m² ground-floor studio provides flexible space for larger or messier projects, alongside a private 25 m² kitchen and living area reserved exclusively for the resident artist or group. Facilities include high-speed internet, monitoring speakers, an 88-key digital piano, dedicated workspaces, kitchen facilities, and a private garden of approximately 100 m².
accommodationInfo: Accommodation is fully integrated into the residency. Residents have access to a private loft featuring a queen-size bed, bathroom, workspace, balcony, and garden surroundings. The property is located in Hang Dong, approximately 20–30 minutes from Chiang Mai city centre. The accommodation is intended for one resident or a couple and is not suitable for larger groups.

name: Tsung-Yeh Artist Village
description: Since the Bureau was established, and the Tourism Bureau was set up under the Tainan City Government, the affairs in regard to tourism originally under the governance of the Tainan County Government Cultural Affairs Bureau have been put under the charge of the Tourism Bureau. The Tsung-Yeh Artist Village in Tainan City is the result of the fusion of an old sugar refinery with multicultural ideas to form a unique space. With years of effort, Tsung-Yeh Artist Village has established itself as a center for arts, crafts and culture while producing valuable creative works in Tainan. Through providing the working space and encouraging resident artists to communicate with the locals, we hope to promote this historical site not simply as a place for exhibitions, but rather an important gathering site for international arts and artists. Tsung-Yeh Arts and Cultural Center takes the concept of ‘Site-Specific Art’ as its theme for the AIR program in 2021 . Artists shall create works before observing the following contexts: hydrology of Tseng-wen River (including river basin and water management system), physiography (archaeological studies, soil, meteorology, or topographical variations), ecology (aquatic, amphibian, and terrestrial fauna and flora in the area), humanities (indigenous, agricultural, river-related, or ecology-related culture).
studioInfo: In 1999, the former Tainan County Government designated four buildings, including Red Brick Office, Wooden Guest House, Red-brick Dining Hall, and Wooden Official Residence, as Municipal Historic Landmarks. They are now transformed and renovated to house various exhibitions of crafts.
accommodationInfo: Furnished four-bedroom / one-bathroom house within the living room space and nearby the Madou city center Internet access, electricity and a fully-furnished kitchen
technicalInfo: TsungYeh Arts and Cultural Center has become a popular venue for cultural events and a focal platform for artists to exchange ideas and exhibit their artworks since it was open to public in 2001. Performances and expositions are held regularly in the historic buildings. From 2010 to 2015, TsungYeh has launched AIR programs to invite in craft artists. Art-in-residency is essential to involve local community in as well as to vitalize traditional crafts. Visitors can learn the skills of crafts and discover the pleasure from hand-made experiences. The Tsung-Yeh Artist Village provides accommodation, studio, basic equipment and exhibition space to satisfy artist needs. During the Artists in Residence Program, they encourage artists to build up the interaction with the local cultural environment, which including folk beliefs, traditional arts, history and industrial development. These resident artists should organize some cultural events and activities for interacting with local community frequently.

name: Surface Arts & HOF
description: HOF Art and Surface Arts presents a residency program in the heart of Bangkok’s budding art district. HOF Art and Surface Arts bring artists together from around the world to concentrate on producing ideas, generating new work and new audiences. They aim to support the artists through their explorations and encounters to expand their practice. The space is in the Sukhumvit area and is a focal point for both emerging and established artists, providing a space for exhibitions and events with two galleries and a café bar. They also have ten studio spaces, along with the resident accommodation, rooftop kitchen and social space. They accept applications from contemporary artists with an interest in urban environments and Thai culture. They aim to support the production of ideas and art works to develop understanding between cultures.
studioInfo: Large airy industrial style studios.
accommodationInfo: Private rooms with A/C.

name: Taipei Artist Village (TAV) & Treasure Hill Artist Village (THAV)
description: Since its foundation, Artist-in-Residence (AIR) Taipei aligns with international artist-in-residence sites, provides artists from both Taiwan and abroad with residence opportunities, and creates an open platform that also acts as a web of solid, international connections, drawing in diverse communities in various disciplines to exchange and broaden each other’s perspectives. After two years of postponement affected by the Covid-19 Pandemic, the 2024 AIR Taipei Open Call provides a unique artist-in-residence site for domestic and international artists to apply: the Treasure Hill Artist Village, a historical architectural community located by the Gongguan waterside. Additionally, AIR Taipei builds a partnership with the Puppetry Art Center of Taipei, encouraging international artists to apply the opportunity to explore Taiwanese puppetry art and culture; the selected artist is provided with resources and supports from both institutions. On the other hand, AIR Taipei has collaborated with its international partner institutions to support domestic artists to connect with the global art scenes and provide a return flight ticket, accommodation, studio space, and allowance in the International Artist Exchange Project. In 2024, AIR Taipei will continue its partnership with Tokyo Arts and Space and BankART 1929 in Japan, the Silpakorn University in Thailand, the City of Munich in Germany (DAC+AOA+GI), the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec and Ciné Tapis Rouge in Canada, expecting to facilitate more diverse interactions between artists and art spaces, generating greater prosperity.
studioInfo: TAV features living quarters and studios (33-46 m2) for 12 artists, as well as a dance studio, a piano room, a dark room, a photo studio, a wood workshop, a recording studio, an exhibition space and two multifunctional halls THAV has 14 studios, where either Taiwanese or international artists can work and live, as well as a rehearsal room, a wood workshop, exhibition spaces and outdoor exhibition spaces
accommodationInfo: TAV THAV

name: Atelier Meso
description: The apartment is open all year round, and they adapt to the needs and rhythm of each artist. The resident stays alone in the apartment, ensuring focus, privacy, and full immersion in their work. Occasional events may be organized in agreement with the resident, depending on their interests and projects. While the residency is based on autonomy, the organisation remains available to support the artist throughout their creative process, whether through practical assistance, connections, or artistic guidance.
studioInfo: The living room hosts classes, exhibitions, workshops, music jams, film screenings, and other cultural events.
accommodationInfo: They provide each resident with a private bedroom and a dedicated studio space. The space acts as a refuge for those who wish to step away from their daily routines and fully immerse themselves in their artistic practice. The apartment features a large multipurpose living room, a spacious balcony, a garden, and an accessible rooftop, offering multiple areas for reflection, work, and conviviality.
technicalInfo: The studio is equipped with the essential materials for creation: a large working space, painting supplies, paper, tools, and a filming station to document artistic processes and finished works.

name: Studios 94
description: STUDIOS 94 is a multi-studio creative hub in Chiang Mai, bringing together artists, designers, musicians, and makers from Thailand and around the world. Split between the Creative STUDIOS, 94 Gallery, and SOFT TOUCH Studio, the five-story space supports emerging and independent creatives through affordable studios, residencies, workshops, and contemporary exhibitions. Founded by an artist, the hub is built on collaboration, accessibility, and meaningful visibility, offering a welcoming environment for making and sharing work. Carefully curated with restored vintage furniture, handmade details, and playful objects collected from local markets, STUDIOS 94 feels both intimate and inspiring — a space that celebrates curiosity, experimentation, and the intuitive freedom at the heart of contemporary art. STUDIOS 94 invites applications for our 2026 Residency and Studio Programs. Located in the heart of Chiang Mai, our multi-story facility serves as a professional nexus for international and local creators, integrating studio practice, exhibition opportunities, and community exchange. Founded by an artist for artists, STUDIOS 94 provides the infrastructure and visibility necessary to elevate your practice within Thailand’s creative capital. They offer two distinct tracks tailored to the needs of emerging and established practitioners across all disciplines, including fine arts, textiles, sculpture, and interdisciplinary research. 1. The Residency Program (2-Month Cycles) A structured immersion combining research, production, and a group exhibition. Duration: 2 months (Month 1: Research/Practice; Month 2: Practice/Production/Exhibition). Accommodations: Private on-site bedroom with an integrated dedicated studio desk. Outcome: A culminating Residency Exhibition at 94 Gallery, inclusive of opening nights, an artist talk and guided studio tours. 2026 Cycles: May–Jun | Jul–Aug | Sep–Oct | Nov–Dec. 2. The Studio Program (Monthly) A flexible, professional workspace for artists seeking focused production time and community integration. Duration: 1 to 9 months (commencing the 1st of each month). Workspace: A dedicated studio desk within our shared professional Artist Studio. Outcome: Participation in monthly Public Studio Showcases and community events. 2026 Availability: April through December. All residents and studio members receive: Access: Daily studio access (9am–9pm) and use of shared workshop areas. Facilities: Full use of communal lounges, kitchen, and rooftop. Professional Development: Eligibility to facilitate workshops or skill-shares; marketing and promotional support via STUDIOS 94 platforms. Engagement: Artist-rate discounts on in-house workshops and events.
studioInfo: Located directly on Huay Kaew Road, the primary artery connecting Chiang Mai’s historic center to the contemporary Nimman district, Studios 94 functions as a professional environment designed to integrate artistic production with public visibility. This strategic location places practitioners within a high-traffic creative corridor, offering a professional base that is both globally accessible and locally connected. The multi-level hub features a street-facing contemporary gallery, specialized media and workshop studios, and on-site residency accommodations, providing cohesive infrastructure for long-term projects and cross-cultural exchange. By offering a range of spaces—from private desks to versatile rooftop terraces and a dedicated gallery shop—the facility eliminates logistical friction, situating artists directly adjacent to major art supply resources and a thriving network of peers. Studios 94 serves as a vital catalyst for professional development, where the stability of a well-equipped workspace enables ambitious creative projects to progress seamlessly from initial experimentation to public exhibition.
accommodationInfo: All residency bedrooms are private double rooms with workspace and shared bathroom access. Each room is uniquely designed to feel comfortable, calm, and homely. Early applicants receive the first choice of available rooms. Peach Bedroom 3rd Floor · Huay Kaew Road Facing A warm, earthy double bedroom in red and beige studio tones. Soft light, textured fabrics, and a private balcony overlooking Huay Kaew Road create a cozy yet inspiring atmosphere — ideal for artists who enjoy an urban view and natural light. Shared bathroom (with one neighbouring bedroom) Toilet + Bathtub + shower Mango Bedroom 3rd Floor · Side Street Facing A calm, blue-toned private bedroom studio designed for focus and clarity. Neutral accents and a dedicated workspace create a peaceful environment for long studio days. Shared bathroom (with one neighbouring bedroom) Toilet + Bathtub + shower Rooftop View Bedroom 4th Floor · Top Floor A cozy industrial-modern space in grey, beige, and chrome tones. Located on the top floor, this bedroom offers privacy, elevated views from the top of the building. Features a private balcony and extended movable storage cabinet for added flexibility. Shared bathroom Toilet + Shower only (no bathtub)

name: The Land Foundation
description: Initiated in 1998, the land (more direct translation from Thai to English would be, the rice field) was the merging of ideas by different artists to cultivate a place of and for social engagement. Though initially the action to aquire the rice fields were initiated by two artists from Thailand, the land was initiated with anonymity and with out the concept of ownership. The land was to be cultivated as an open space, though with certain intentions towards community, towards discussions and towards experimentation in other fields of thoughts. The foundation aims to promote and support artistic and cultural activities, natural farming, and self-knowledge through the Vipassana meditation techniques.
technicalInfo: There is currently no specific AiR program - nevertheless, the land foundation welcomes anyone interested.

name: Halka art project
description: Halka art project is a self-sustaining art organisation based in Istanbul which focuses on the production, discourse and presentation of contemporary art and culture since 2011. It initiates, curates and develops art projects at home and abroad. Halka art project runs curated individual or group exhibitions, artist talks, screenings and workshops on art, ecology, culinary arts and self-sustaining community issues, as well as an international residency programme. In its first 6 years the residency programme has hosted more than 60 artists from around 35 countries. Halka art project residency is located in the Asian Side of Istanbul, in Moda district of Kadıköy. The residency period depends upon request, project and possibilities from 3 weeks to 3 months.The aim of the residency programme is to provide a centre of concentration, collaboration and/or isolation for the artists and theoricians from various disciplines in order to create and develop their artistic projects. The programme supports their guest artists in finding connections from local and international circles, sharing ideas, exchanging experiences. It also aims to form a basis for local and international collaborations. Halka art/ residency is not an artist hotel. Based on application, project ideas which are open for improvement are carefully invited to join the programme. Halka art project works with the artists in the execution of their project in every step such as the curatorial support, artist assistance, presentation, and networking.
studioInfo: 3 studio spaces in a 3 floor residency building - they are open for the participation of visual artists, curators and writers.
accommodationInfo: Halka art project residency programme offers private rooms with working units within, aside from the co-shared studio spaces, a co-shared kitchen, bathrooms, a recreational garden and a gallery space for meetings, exhibitions and artist talks.
technicalInfo: Halka art/ residency has a wireless internet connection, a printer and a beamer for presentations.

name: ComPeung
description: ComPeung is not only the first independent AiR program in Thailand, but also the longest ongoing program since 2007. They have hosted over 100 artists in a wide variety of disciplines from around the world. As an evolving art project, ComPeung encourages artists to explore and discover – not only new ideas, techniques, and networks, but also themselves as human beings though the process of creative activities and everyday living. ComPeung aims to be an open space for dialogues, encouraging the exchange of ideas and experiments, and exploring the interdependence between art, artists and society. For artists who need time away from regular commitments to finish current projects, to reflect on their practice, or to explore and develop new works, ComPeung is the ideal place to do so. In an unregimented and relaxed atmosphere, artists have the freedom to focus on their work without having to worry about daily routines such as preparing meals. We hope that by living and working together in a tranquil setting with our team, the local community, and a small diverse group of artists, people will be inspired and challenged to explore possibilities and dreams. ComPeung offers genuine hospitality with fresh daily produce from the local market for delicious home-cooked meals, assistance where needed, and provides all the necessities for living in a semi-rural, tropical area.
studioInfo: Approximate area of 2.8 acres near natural fishing lakes, forest and mountains.
accommodationInfo: Approximate area of 2.8 acres (appx 2 soccer fields) Main house for staff Artist house #1 with a basic bedroom, private bathroom, indoor and outdoor studio spaces Artist house #2 with 1 maisonette bedroom, 1 small bedroom downstairs, spacious private bathroom, indoor and outdoor working spaces Kitchen & Communal Space Electric fans, mosquito nets Variety of manual and electric tools Running water. 220 volt electricity Good mobile phone reception Internet access (Fiber Optic, Wifi, download/upload: 100M/30 Mbps, LAN is avialable) No shared computers. Artists do need to bring their own laptop.
technicalInfo: Multi-function outdoor space for performing artists, 5 x 10 m with projection screens and projector. Industrial fan, a variety of manual and electric tools. Running water. 220 volt electricity. Good mobile phone reception. Internet access (Wifi, download/upload: 10M/512K).

name: Studio 88
description: Studio 88 Artist Residency provides a space to reflect and experiment for all creative thinkers and makers. They believe in the power of integrating art into everyday life to create positive change in the world. Studio 88 is particularly interested in how art can interact with nature, people and culture in daily life, challenging ways of thinking and also providing innovative alternatives. From artists’ self-exploration to artistic collaborations, from creatively engaging with the aspirations of schoolchildren to crafting with older generations, every creative project has the potential to change lives. Co-founded by cultural managers Sasiwimon Wongjarin and Claire Rosslyn Wilson, Studio 88 desires to connect creative thinkers and contribute to local communities. Studio 88 provides space to experiment with the process of creating, as well as time out from busy day-to-day life in order to relax and reflect. Studio 88 has an international outreach. It believes in the importance of connecting international creative thinkers with local communities and aims to foster this connection through meaningful and tangible projects. Keep an eye out on upcoming open calls for more information about the special projects. The 4-week programme is titled Reviving Nature: Pollution Alert Artist Residency 2024. In their residency space in Doi Saket, 30 minutes from the centre of Chiang Mai, you explore the topic of air quality. The residency, with a select group of international and Thai artists, is facilitated by locally based arts manager and Studio 88 founder Sasiwimon Wongjarin (Aom). The theme of this residency is very open and it can explore multifaceted aspects of pollution. It could encompass air, water, soil, noise, light, or any other form of pollution affecting our environment and communities. It could seek to examine the causes, consequences, and potential solutions related to pollution. It could also look at complex ways our systems are connected and how we can improve in areas such as urban planning and farming. In Chiang Mai there are particular challenges with air pollution, due to things such as vehicles, factories, construction, garden burning, and agricultural and forest fires. Therefore, as part of the residency, you will be visiting RUEE Lab (the Rajamangala University of Technology Lanna), which researches the measurement, control and prevention of pm2.5 pollution. You don’t have to be an expert in air pollution, rather they are interested in seeing how creative approaches can contribute diverse perspectives to pollution and scientific processes. This can be a new area for you. They just ask that you bring your curiosity and an active interest in the topic.
accommodationInfo: Individual bungalows with equipped kitchenettes and cleaning service Individual and/or shared studio/workspace Electricity, water, and Wi-Fi (including air-conditioning and fans) Twice a week the bungalow will be cleaned. However, it is also expected that the spaces will be kept relatively clean throughout the stay. If there is any damage to the bungalows the resident will need to cover the cost of repair. Breakfast and dinner can be provided at the residency (for an additional cost of 100 USD per week per resident), please contact us beforehand if you would like to take up this option. In this case, breakfast would be a selection of fruits and cereals, and dinner would be home-cooked local dishes. Otherwise, in town, there are several restaurant options serving local dishes, and one Italian restaurant. Meals range from 30 baht to 250 baht, depending on the restaurant. There are also cafes that serve tea and coffee, ranging from 30 baht to 90 baht. There are small market stalls in town that sell fruit and vegetables and also a small supermarket that sells a range of products.

name: Mouhit Space
description: Mouhit is an artist-residence based in Tunis. The residence supports creative practitioners at all levels of their career by offering a convivial environment for reflection, artistic experimentation, and self-development At Mouhit, they believe that feedback culture and critical thinking constitute the core of a nurturing arts practice, hence they work with mentors from different backgrounds to support artists during their residency. At the same time, Mouhit offers tools for artists to organize their residency in a self-directed way. To the organisers, openness and accessibility are important values, thus they encourage artists to engage with the public during their residency period by offering experiences, open studios, and activities of their choice. Mouhit strives to become a bridge between Tunisian and international artists by fostering dialogues and exchanges. They support artists in residence by integrating them into both the local and international art scenes, providing them with mentoring, guidance, and production and communication support tailored to their practices and needs during their residency.
studioInfo: Mouhit Space is a 3 story residence located in Menzah 1 on a plot of (1100) sq.m with a large garden space. It offers a shared sunny and bright workspace (50) sq.m. with a large work table and large multifunctional outdoor space. A sound studio is available on demand. The shared spaces facilitate cooperation and communication between guests and residents as well as the sharing of thoughts and ideas. The garden can also be used as an exhibition space. The house and the neighborhood provides the space to reflect, experiment and create, whether an artist wants to do research or production.
accommodationInfo: The residency is housed in a villa: it provides a communal living setting for residents which reinforces the socially engaged, environmentally oriented approach of the organization. Two private bedrooms with a bed, a desk and storage space are available. The common areas include an equipped kitchen, a bathroom, a restroom and a large garden.

name: Gate27
description: Gate 27 is an international residency program established in 2019 to facilitate the research and production processes of different practices and to provide a platform for interdisciplinary interaction. Treating art as a research method, Gate 27 invites artists, researchers and academics to establish a dialogue around ecology, sustainability, accessibility and local creative networks. Gate 27 encourages the formation of new collaborations with the public programs and events it organizes. Gate 27 provides a calm working environment where residents can transform their ideas into production process, and facilitates access to various resources and individuals to deepen their research. Participants become part of a wide and ever-growing network of artists and researchers who have been residents in the program. Gate 27 hosts artists and researchers in its guest houses in Istanbul and Ayvalık. Gate 27 İstanbul offers an entry into the vibrant cultural life of Istanbul especially for emerging and established artists who reside outside of Istanbul and provides a quiet production space in nature where they can observe the city from a peaceful distance. Gate 27 Ayvalık aims to create an experience that nurtures conceptual research and production for artists and researchers who focus on the process rather than results.
studioInfo: In Ayvalık, studio space is within the private room of the artists. The garden can also be used for practice and production. In Istanbul, there are two spacious studios and a small library to make research. Plus there is a separate workshop with basic tools (circular saw, table saw, sander, angle grinder, bench drill and hand tools etc.)
accommodationInfo: In Ayvalık they provide: Private room with a double bed (suitable also for artist duos) and a private bathroom Studio/working space within the private room Three meals a day Transportation support within Ayvalık Introduction to Ayvalık contemporary art scene Online studio visits with curators and art professionals Spacious communal workspaces intertwined with nature In Istanbul, they provide: Production studio with basic tools (circular saw, table saw, sander, angle grinder, bench drill and hand tools etc.) Private room with a double bed and a private bathroom (The rooms can host 2 people and are suitable for artist duos) Fully equipped shared kitchen where residents cook their own food Introduction to Istanbul’s contemporary art and culture scene via: Events targeting engagement with artists, curators, professionals from art institutions Open studio days Access to Sabancı University Faculty of Social Sciences laboratories (upon request and availability)

name: Dar Meso SARL
description: Dar Meso is an artist residency based in a picturesque corner of nature In the heart of the medina of Tunis, a calm and exotic place that will foster innovation and cultural exchange. The residency is located in Bab Souika, a popular and lively district of the Medina of Tunis. The house, built in the 1900s, was for a long time occupied by various religious associations that lived there independently thanks to its garden and its fruit trees. Dar Meso offers artists a private workspace, co-working spaces equipped with the necessary tools for their creation, housing and catering. The artist comes to work on a specific artistic project and is autonomous. The idea is that they come to Dar Meso to find peace, tranquility and a change in scenery to boost their work and foster his innovation. The organisers also offer to artists the possibility to get in touch with the artisans and craftsmiths of the neighborhood (blacksmiths, cabinetmakers, seamstress …) to promote local crafts and open up new horizons in the artists’ work and creation.
studioInfo: The residence comprises: 2 kitchens: one in the ground floor with direct access to the garden and one on the first level, closer and easier to access to residents. 2 bathrooms and 1 water closet 6 rooms with different atmospheres and decorations: Berber style, vegetal decoration, Tunisian style and also 30’s … A chapel revamped into a workshop, might be transformed in rehearsal studio, gallery… An office/workshop in the first level Three shared spaces : oriental living room in the first level, Tunisian living room in the gound level and a reading space Dar Meso offers as well many work spaces or outdoor exhibition possibilities such as the large garden, terrace and flat roof overlooking the entire medina.
accommodationInfo: Each artist has their own room with storage and a work space. The residency functions as a community and they regularly share meals together. Everything in the 2 kitchens is available for self-service for residents.

name: Elagza Dağ Evleri
description: Elagza Dağ Evleri [Elagza Chalets] is a boutique hotel at the Eastern Blacksea Coast of Turkey. Elagza Artists' Retreat [E.A.R.] is an artists' residency program that will take place at Elagza Chalets [Elagza Dağ Evleri], every year seven months between October to May. Elagza Chalets, which is built upon seven acres of land surrounded with tea fields and forest, will support E.A.R. by opening its two duplex appartments, three bungalows and one village house to the disposal of the artists. All living spaces has the area of 50 squaremeters. Five of these six residency slots are paid by artists and one slot will be provided to artists free of charge by utilizing the open call and invitation methods. Minimum duration to join the program is one mont and maximum is seven months. Each of these six accomodation options can be utilized for different working practices. Houses will be kept empty and will be furnished in accordance with the artists' need, upon the arrival of the artist. Artists from wide variety of background and disciplines will be accepted to the program. Elagza Artists' Retreat, as the name offers, will provide a silent and peacefull, yet inspirational working enviroment. E.A.R. will provide exhibiton space alternatives, either in Rize or various cities for artists willing to launch an exhibition after their work on E.A.R. Elagza Artists' Retreat will provide logistics support in finding all the materials necessary for the production of the artists, compensation of the fees of these materials belong to the artist. E.A.R. will take initiative to make possible the meetings between Turkish art scene and artists in residence, for this purpose, artists from Turkey will be invited to the program free of charge. Elagza Artists' Retreat supports collaborations between artists and researchers from Blacksea region, either on national or international level. In addition to the six houses, Elagza Chalets will open its kitchen, its salon that can be used as meeting or resting area and its depot that can be used as a sculpture studio to the disposal of artists.
studioInfo: Three bungalows, each 65 squaremeters. One wooden house, 50 squaremeters. Two duplex appartments, approx 50 squaremeters. Accomodation and studio spaces are the same.
accommodationInfo: Three bungalows, each 65 squaremeters. One wooden house, 50 squaremeters. Two duplex appartments, approx 50 squaremeters. Accomodation and studio spaces are the same.
technicalInfo: Groups, patners, family, welcome.

name: Atelier Muse
description: Atelier Muse is a creative initiative as an arts and culture consultancy office that implements new approaches to arts and culture field by carrying out interdisciplinary cross-sectoral projects. Atelier Muse adopts a global and collaborative point of view with partners sharing the same vision as being present and actively productive in life. Atelier Muse Residency Program, among other projects, initiated in 2017, is the realisation of a lifelong dream of its founder Müge Olacak to add value to life by coming together, exchanging knowledge and creativity with curiosity. The program is established to host artists from all around the world, creating a bridge of understanding between cultures and leveraging the knowhow and qualifications of arts and culture field. Istanbul, a city that is both Asian and European, is without a doubt the best place to get stimulated and inspired. The organisation shares its founder’s believe, that art is a remedy for growing divisions and conflicts in today’s societies and we are able find a common ground by working together in creating it. While program focuses on contemporary dance, performance, writing and new media arts, it is also open for artists who works on social causes independently of disciplines.

name: Arthere Istanbul
description: arthereistanbul, a multicultural space located at the crossing-bridge between Europe and Asia Istanbul is often considered as one of the Art Cities of the Future: a city rich a vibrant and vital art scene, connected both to Europe and Asia, while also relating to the Middle-East. The city is often seen as a bridge between the East and the West, a cosmopolitan space where hundreds of cultures coexist. One of Istanbul art scene's main characteristics may also be its strong intertwining with the country’s political life and its geographic situation. This contributed to shape singular and strong artistic expressions tied to local issues and individual specificities. In this context, arthereistanbul aims to: – foster research, creativity and in arts and culture by opening an space to artists from all over the world to develop their ideas and projects. – favour exchange between artists at risk / exiled artists together with artists from Turkey and International artists, curators, researchers, and arts professionals. – increase the interaction between local and international artists and/or initiatives. – encourage and support dialogue, diversity, tolerance and understanding against fear and suspicion. In arthereistanbul, the residents will benefit from a multicultural environment and will have opportunities to broaden their vision and understanding of the region particularly in terms of culture and the arts while working in a cosmopolitan, international atmosphere. In arthereistanbul, the resident will find full understanding, the needed support and constructive guidance to develop his/her own artwork and progress in his/her knowledge out of his/her experience from the residency. THE CUSTOM MADE RESIDENCY PROGRAM arthereistanbul is launching its Custom-Made Residency Program and will welcome the first residents in 2017. These residencies of one to three months (or more) can be for research, reflection, project's writing or development, without the pressure of production. The Custom-Made Residency Program is opened to artists, researchers, curators, writers, from all backgrounds and all kind of experience in various disciplines of arts and culture. The project and its adequacy with arthereistanbul’s vision and territory will determine the participation in our residency program. The purpose of this Custom-Made Residency Program is to allow the artist / researcher / curator / art professional to work on the first steps of his/her project. This can consist of writing a first draft, leading a research, looking for archives, gathering elements for an art project, or work on a small production. A custom made package is put together for each artist or group of artists. There can be an individual accompaniment by artehereistanbul team and other external specialists, if required for the artistic work process. arthereistanbul team can also offer her support and advice on administrative matters and help in finding partners
studioInfo: 2 working studio spaces 2 archive rooms Music room for rehersal and recording New art media Lab ( 3d Printers, resin printers, electronics workshop) Darkroom facilities Gallery/exhibition space Courtyard/garden Wood working shop Small kitchen for tea or coffee   Materials: 3D Printers, resin printer Wood and carpenter tools Basic office materials Technical material (cables, speakers, projectors etc) Non-professional printer Internet
accommodationInfo: Accommodation type: shared apartment (three people max). Accommodation in Kadiköy, in the neighborhood of Rasimpasa, nearly arthereistanbul and the studio space, which consists of a two rooms of 20 – 30 sqm in a shared flat of 85 to 110 sqm of living space, well-equipped kitchen, and all neccessary services like: hot water – heating – washing machine – TV – shower – toilet – terrace overlooking istanbul sea side, internet access.
technicalInfo: Preparation, administrative advisory, networking: Pre-residency online preparation with the arthereistanbul's team to plan the the residency accordingly to the needs and requirements of the project Support, advice, for administrative, financial, partnerships issues for each resident. arthereistanbul aims to fill the gap between the participants and the different actors in the city Series of cultural visits to some local organizations, spaces, art centers of Istanbul in relation to the needs of the project. These activities can be accompanied by informal meetings with local cultural actors Organization of public events or exhibition, at the end of the residency, in line with the project and the need of the resident. arthereistanbul helps with visa application by sending the selected applicants an official invitation letter and helping with all other necessary documents required.

name: Charitable Foundation for Art Support "Artsvit Gallery"
description: Artsvit Gallery has been operating in Dnipro since 2013 and, since then, has become a cultural platform for interdisciplinary projects, discussions, and representations of contemporary Ukrainian art. Main directions of work: – Exhibitions; – Educational and research programs; – Residencies; – Collection of Ukrainian art from the II WW until today. The gallery is focused on socio-critical art and is oriented to the socio-cultural context of Dnipro and the region and its cultural, industrial, and post-Soviet heritage. Non-formal education is an essential component of the projects. The main goal is to affect the development of local creative communities and highlight important contexts and events in Ukraine, including the full-scale Russian invasion, through art and non-formal education. The gallery also implements international art projects with the aim of representing Ukraine's interests in the world. The mission of the Artsvit gallery is to support contemporary Ukrainian art and strengthen its role in Ukrainian society and among the international community. The residency program is oriented towards the socio-cultural context of the city of Dnipro and the region. It has a component of informal education, with a focus on working with young artists and supporting their professional growth. They mainly offer a group residency format with mentoring and involving experts (Ukrainian and international). Important note: Due to the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine and the proximity to the front line, they are temporarily working mainly with local artists and cultural activists. This is an attempt to support those who remained in Dnipro, as well as due to security issues. However, if any international artists are willing to come to Dnipro, independently raising funding, we can provide institutional support and host him or her as a resident.
studioInfo: Artists working in various media. Work space is selected upon request.
accommodationInfo: Apartment for rent in the central part of the city. Shared accommodation is possible - two people in one room.
technicalInfo: Office equipment, library, materials for creativity upon request, own collection of Ukrainian art, acquaintance with various cultural figures in the city and their exhibitions, archives, etc (upon request).

name: NADAS
description: NADAS is a creative house, located in Yeldeğirmeni, Kadıköy, Istanbul, founded in June 2018. The platform aims to open space for individual and community projects valuing the diversity of urban life and people’s connection to their environments. At Nadas, maximum conditions are provided for artists and their ideas to be heard, tested, and integrated; slowly, mindfully, and empathetically. ‘Nadas’a Bırak’ artists residencies programmes hosts artists from all creative mediums and stages of their carriers. Their regular week-long residency takes place in the Spring and Fall, with longer-term residencies available in-between. During the pandemic, the program has moved mostly online, while continuing to offer private studio space to individuals and small groups. Therefore, the third edition of Nadas’a Bırak Artist Residency was hybrid in form, offering residents the opportunity to work virtually and/or in-house. Group meetings, co-working hours, artists talks, and studio sharings offer opportunities for all artists to connect with one another and the wider Nadas community, whether joining online or in-person. The residency culminated in an online exhibition and open studio event, where artists had a chance to share their experiences and works from the programme with visitors from around the world. Overall, the residency is most suited for artists or creative individuals who seek to: Develop a project within a focused period of time; Work independently, within the support of a shared working environment; Present their work in an alternative community space and online exhibition; Incorporate sustainability and ecological practices into their work.
accommodationInfo: Please note that this residency does not include accommodation. Residents are responsible for finding and covering the cost of their own accommodation. The organization, however, can assist residents in finding places to stay.
technicalInfo: Nadas’a Bırak Art Residency, for online residents includes: Daily co-working hours and check-ins with NB team; Weekly group meetings; Weekly virtual studio visits with local and international artists, and past Nadas’a Bırak residents; Optional morning yoga classes; Optional online yoga classes, 2 times per week; Participation in an online exhibition and open studio event; Optional artistic and curatorial support; Opportunity to join Nadas’s creative community. Nadas’a Bırak Spring Art Residency, for in-person residents includes all of the above, as well as*: Access to a private studio space Access to a shared living room, balcony, garden, and kitchen; Vegan lunch, plus tea and coffee throughout the day. Note: In-person residents have access to a studio space at least two days per week. On all remaining days, they are invited to join virtually.

name: Open Place
description: Platform for Interdisciplinary Practice Open Place (Open Place) is an artistic initiative that aims to facilitate discussions and exchange of opinions, ideas, and experiences between artists, curators, and various social groups across Ukraine and other countries. The platform organizes meetings and conducts joint events to foster the development of art, politics, and socio-cultural transition. Open Place supports artists and their outreach to various social groups across Ukraine and abroad. Embracing the diversity of ideas, methods, and actions in visual arts, design, performance, media art, architecture, research, social action, and economics, Open Place has been developing grassroots and social engagement practices since 1999. Art residencies are an important part of Open Place’s activities. Open Place supports interdisciplinary projects aimed at the expansion of art-making concepts and the engagement of new groups of people in the creative process. They are interested in the experience of international colleagues working with socially minded practices and how they use participatory art and engage different social groups. Open Place works on researching practices of collective coexistence, building horizontal structures, and peer-to-peer learning. A significant part of Open Place’s activities is aimed at building connections between different social and professional groups, different contexts, and different types of knowledge. The goal of the residency is to exchange knowledge and practical experience, examine the specifics of various local contexts, and develop new methods in the field of socially engaged art. Open Place is attentive to the ideas and practices of its residents. For its part, the residency program helps artists to explore the context and forge links with the artistic and research milieu upon their needs. They are particularly looking for applications from artists and curators who are interested in development and transformation of contemporary interdisciplinary practices, focused on working with communities, and the topic of inclusion.
studioInfo: The studio offers a total area of 50 square meters including three working spaces, kitchen and bathroom. It is suitable for curators, researchers, visual and performing artists, photographers, video and multimedia artists.
accommodationInfo: One studio a total area of 35 square meters consists of sleeping area, kitchen and bathroom.
technicalInfo: Tools for wood (carving tools, wood chisels, power jigsaw, sander polisher, electric drill) and metal (hacksaw, metal brush, metal files); audio-visual equipment for the production of photos, videos, and audio materials (two film photo cameras (Nikon F2A and Canon EOS Elan7), one digital photo camera (Nikon D90), two video cameras (MiniDV Panasonic DVX100B, Sony FDR-AX53), microphone, recorder, tripod, projector and two LSD monitors). Library where among others there are the single and rare editions and publications of partner institutions on art, philosophy, actual art practises and methodologies. The Open Place residency program is not only a space for creation, but also an archive which contains a diverse collection of contemporary visual art resources. Open Place collects and manages art-related materials as well as facilitates the exchange of resources through networks between local and international partners. The Archive that Open Place has developed since 2004 is partly dedicated to archiving the main organizational processes of the residency, such as performances, seminars, workshops, lectures, discussions and educational programs, as well as contains a portfolio of artists selected by their curators and by partners' organizations.

name: Kulturakademie Tarabya
description: The Tarabya Cultural Academy awards annual fellowships to artists and cultural professionals from different disciplines for four to eight-month stays in Istanbul as part of an open call procedure. The fellowships contribute in a special way to the transcultural exchange between Turkey and Germany and foster intensive engagement with both societies. Exceptionally qualified artists and cultural professionals who have already gained public recognition for their works or publications and who live and work in the Federal Republic of Germany and tandems of cultural professionals residing in Germany and Turkey who qualify within the framework of the Turkish-German co-production grants . Applications from students are excluded. Examples of tandems that qualify within the framework of the Turkish-German co-production grants: A film director who lives in Turkey wants to work on a new project with a screenwriter from Germany A musician residing in Turkey would like to work for several months with a composer from Germany. A visual artist residing in Germany would like to realize a joint project with a visual artist residing in Turkey Benefits and services:  Work in an environment of excellent fellow artists. Communal use of a multi-purpose room usable as a studio, of a rehearsal room (with Steinway piano and drums), and of an event space used by several organizations. In addition, fellowship holders can apply for the defrayment of project-related material costs arising from the realization and presentation of artistic work. The German Embassy in Ankara is responsible for the supervision of the program. The Goethe-Institut bears curatorial responsibility and is also responsible for networking with Turkish cultural professionals and supporting the realisation of projects on site.
studioInfo: Please check the accommodation information.
accommodationInfo: The residency includes a furnished accommodation (apartment with cooking facilities and bathroom),communal use of a multi-purpose room usable as a studio, of a rehearsal room (with Steinway piano and drums) and of an event space used by several organizations.

name: Creative Residence MC6
description: The Creative Residency MC6 is a meaning-building space and community located in the Ukrainian Carpathians, where, in a natural environment of values, trust, and dialogue, meaningful transformations occur at both personal and societal levels. The activities of the MC6 community encompass cultural research, education, arts, architecture, and social initiatives. By uniting cultural figures, artists, civic activists, members of the local community, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and defenders around shared values, the organisers create a network of intersections, warm interactions, and horizontal trust to foster dialogue and the development of their country. The Creative residency of MC6 is about a broad perspective: rethinking traditions, local context, nature as a basis, authenticity and innovation, interdisciplinary and holistic approaches. It is also about finding bridges of intersection between different national communities of Ukraine, knowing one's own identity, exploring creative processes and methods that cause changes at the level of the individual and society. A separate topic for research is the history of the Ukrainian Avantgarde and Boykivshchyna of that time (1910-1940) - rethinking and creating something new. The residency creates a safe space and conditions for collaborations, experiments and cultural dialogue. The program includes research, creative and educational components: lectures, master classes, excursions, curatorial support and presentation of artists' works.
studioInfo: On the territory of MC6 there are two separate rooms for collaborative work: Residence and Trepeta (spaces with an area of about 90 m²), suitable for both visual arts and performative or movement practices. The time of use must be agreed with other guests of the Creative Residence MC6 through the project managers. It is possible to fully rent a separate space for a project for an additional fee. The coworking Art space with an area of 20 m² can be adapted to various creative requests. There is also a workshop with tools for working with wood. A small Music Studio of 12 m2 (will be available from March 2025). Summer covered terraces - for visual and performative arts. They accept artists from various fields: visual arts, music, architecture, design, literature, performative art practices. Their focus and themes include: artistic freedom and experimentation, rethinking Ukrainian avant-garde and the history of Boykivshchyna, reinterpreting traditions, authenticity and innovation, connection with nature, local context, interdisciplinarity, and interaction with the MC6 community and the local population (e.g., organizing lectures, workshops, or creative sessions).
accommodationInfo: For residents, they offer three spaces: Sadyba: 2 rooms for single settlement. Shared spaces include a living room with a fireplace and a kitchen. The bathrooms are shared and located in the corridor. Art Space: 1 rooms for double settlement or 1 room for single settlement, with a bathroom in each room. Shared spaces include a mini-kitchen and a coworking area equipped with a projector and screen. Camping: from May to September, they provide 2 tents for 2 residents. The tents have heated beds and basic furniture. The bathroom and shower are located within the camping area.
technicalInfo: The space is equipped with a weaving loom, an etching press, a woodworking workshop, musical instruments, a recording studio, and music equipment for performances. There is also a hall for movement and dance (use must be specified separately) and a mini-library in the art area. During warm seasons, covered terraces and open natural spaces can serve as workshops.

name: Project Diffusion
description: Project ‘Diffusion’ came to life in 2016. Its' aim is to bring together artists from different spheres (film and photography, multi-media, street arts, fine arts and crafts, contemporary art performance, dance, theatre, design, drawing etc.) to create artworks that address important social and environmental issues and preferably involve local community in development of artwork. The residency is open for artists both from Ukraine and abroad. The culminating moment of the residency is a final exhibition in the Kramatorsk Art Museum where the artworks created during the residency will be shown. Kramatorsk is a small industrial, but very green town that due to geo-political turbulence became a kind of center of Southeast Ukraine. By choosing Kramatorsk as the city for the residency, the program offers a unique experience when it comes to discovering the cultural transitions which are so characteristic to all ‘Post-Soviet’ era of the Eastern European countries. Feedback and experience of the first editions of “Diffusion” has shown that the acclimatization process which accompanies the residency in a new city full of contrasts invariably generates creative impulses that sooner or later manifest themselves in some form of artistic expression. Participants present their depiction of their sensations to local people by giving them a chance to view their city through the eyes of a stranger. The Residency is not limited to Kramatorsk only. It offers wide range of places to discover and to present their works around Kramatorsk such as Bachmut, Slovyansk, Dobropilla, Druzkivka, Pokrovsk, Avdiivka and as far as the coastal city of Mariupol. The program covers accommodation and shared open studio spaces costs for the duration of the residency and some limited material costs. Applicants are responsible for covering travel and food expenses / daily allowances, and some additional materials costs. Access to analogue photo laboratory and video editing room can be made available upon demand. Some production (materials) support can be provided upon additional request. If required, the Kramatorsk Art Museum can issue acceptance / participation confirmation letter to help the participants to obtain grants to cover their travel, insurance, food costs, materials costs etc.
studioInfo: Participants work in museum itself, outside and inside different studio places.
accommodationInfo: Participants live in hostel or in a shared apartment.

name: Sorry No Rooms Available
description: The residency Sorry No Rooms Available is aimed at: Decentralizing the development of the cultural economy and contemporary art in Ukraine. Creating the possibility of cultural exchange and research in the new context. Integrating the participants into the local art scene. Integrating the residency as a cultural international platform into European and world art processes. The residency has been based at the hotel Intourist-Zakarpattya in Uzhhorod since 2016. Sorry No Rooms Available favors artistic research and creates conditions for artists to connect with the cultural scene of Uzhhorod and the Zakarpattya (Transcarpathian) region. The resident is expected to carry out at least one site-specific project in Uzhhorod or in the region. The project may reflect on the hotel itself, its site, history, etc. From 2020, Sorry No Rooms Available is receiving participants from the regions of Ukraine where war actions are taking place. At present, the residency, which rents one room from the Intourist-Zakarpattya Hotel, has a maximum capacity of 1 to 2 residents at a time.
studioInfo: Studio room of the hotel Intourist-Zakarpattia about 20 sq.m.
accommodationInfo: There are two main options available to residents: Option 1: The resident gets to live in a hotel room in Intourist-Zakarpattya. It is a 20 sq m room with bathroom, balcony, electric kettle, multicooker, bed, sofa, two armchairs, chair, standard lamp, two desk lamps, TV set, and internet. The room is free for the resident, but they must donate a 60x80 cm painting to the hotel for each month of stay. The room can be used as both accommodation and a studio. Option 2: The room in the hotel is only used as a studio. The resident can rent another room in Intourist-Zakarpattya with a 40% discount (prices can be found here http://intur-zak.com/web/en/prices). Alternatively, the resident may rent an apartment in Uzhhorod for an approximate rate of 250 EUR per month.
technicalInfo: A Zoom H4 recorder, TV + DVD, and a projector can be provided.

name: YermilovCentre Art Kuzemyn
description: YermilovCentre is a centre of contemporary art in Kharkiv, opened in March 2012. It is named after a famous Kharkiv artist, representative of the Ukrainian avant-garde, Vasyl Yermilov. The largest exhibition space in Kharkiv, YermilovCentre represents contemporary Ukrainian art processes. Our priorities are artistic dialogue with the viewer and international cooperation. Activities of the YermilovCentre include curatorial projects, artistic residences, lectures and discussions, performances, seminars, cinema, and video shows. Multidisciplinary art residency, where the cultural and artistic components are intertwined with seeking solutions to social issues and preservation of cultural and historical heritage. Artists work outside their usual environment, explore cultural and historical contexts, reflect, experiment with materials. We create a comfortable place for creativity and give artists the opportunity to interact with the local community. The residency should revitalize the countryside, promote decentralization and give the area a new cultural significance. The project includes such activities: excursions, art workshops for children and teenagers, an exhibition in the village house of culture or in the public space of the village. Art Kuzemyn Carrying out a residency in the village of Kuzemyn in the Sumy region means for the YermilovCentre: New experience in organizing a program of residencies outside Kharkiv. Intervention of art practices into a non-artistic social environment. Research of this intervention. Expanding the audience interested in contemporary art through interaction with the local community, children, organizers of cultural events in the local house of culture. And the opportunity to show the village community how contemporary art and cultural initiatives can change you and the world around you, how they can affect your thoughts and your village. Establishing permanent professional horizontal connections in the Ukrainian art environment, promoting their development through the organization of joint events and artist talks during the residency. Exploring a new format and deepening the skills of working with multidisciplinary projects. Important note: Starting from 2020, the residency focuses exclusively on the city of Kharkiv and its art. The time and circumstances are such that they have to solve only specific and urgent tasks to preserve and strengthen the cultural field.
studioInfo: 3 rooms adapted for studios with workplaces (desks, chairs) in a separate building.
accommodationInfo: Private house with three rooms, shared kitchen and dining space. Each room has a bed, desk, and a chair. Wi-Fi is available. Shared toilet and shower inside the building. Three residents at a time. Duos are welcome, partners and childrens are negotiable.
technicalInfo: Library, projector, construction tools such as screwdriver, chainsaw, construction staplers, and glue guns.

name: The Muzychi Expanded History project
description: The Muzychi Expanded History project is a private residency program supported and organized by the artist Alevtina Kakhidze. It is taking place in the village of Muzychi, an hour away from Kyiv with public transportation. The studio and accommodation of the resident are personally lent by Alevtina Kakhidze, residency coordinator and neighbor. Due to the qualities of the residency location and context, no specific project or exhibition is expected from the resident, although the program is open to any kind of initiatives and ideas. The resident biography and work will also be included in the book to be published ‘Expanded History of Muzychi, a history of the residencies in Muzychi through the years. The whole concept of the residency program is that Alevtina lends her own studio for the period of the artist’s stay, working in this period of time from the house next door. Alevtina's personal items are hidden inside the furniture, which consists of wooden cubes and a storage-bed, for the comfort of the resident not to be surrounded with them. There are three Central Asian Shepherd dogs in the area. Residents can receive a small workshop on request about how to behave with and befriend them. In case of someone having fear of dogs, there is an additional exit to a residential house, which does not allow the residents to encounter them again. They are loud and audible, and in Ukrainian villages people have dogs outside.
studioInfo: 1 studio for the artist/curator
accommodationInfo: The studio has two rooms: one room can be for living and the second for work. There is water, a shower and a toilet, furniture, a small kitchen, internet and electricity. There is a bike donated to the program by the first resident of the program — Stefka Ammon from Germany. Only 1 resident can be hosted at once. Therefore, only individual artists are eligible to apply. However, guests can be hosted for 1-2 days.
technicalInfo: Presence of scanner, printer, and opportunity to work with the personal archive of artist Alevtina Kakhidze

name: Congress of Cultural Activists
description: The organization aims for the establishment of democratic, universal values and aesthetic tolerance, as a guarantee of the development of national and world culture. They are focused on practicing and distributing the ideas of sustainable development and development of civil society in Ukraine with the help of art and mobility. Residency programs are mainly aimed at revealing the social aspects of the local context. NVAIR aims to create projects collaboratively and cooperatively, as the accumulation of shared memory and finding ways to de-isolate the countryside. The organization prefers to collaborate with artists who work with contexts and communities, exploring history and landscape. For the fruitful work of residents, meetings are organize in order to establish contacts with the local cultural scene, creative community, organizations and institutions.
studioInfo: There are 3 studios: 80 m2 with library, easels, screen and projector, desks and chairs; 30m2 with a press for manual printing, 20 m2 with equipment for ceramics. There is also a backyard where the artist can arrange a workplace. Mostly, artists who work with the visual art of classical and experimental techniques, digital artists and photographers (there is no special equipment, but NVAIR cooperates with printing studios and media labs in Ternopil) are invited.
accommodationInfo: The second floor is a shared lounge area, kitchen and shared bathroom with shower and washing machine, as well as 4 bedrooms (bed, table, chair, clothes hanger). Please note that there is no individual space available other than the bedroom. The residency is like a dormitory, where everyone lives together. Therefore, residents are responsible for the cleanliness and order of the common living space. Maximum 4 residents can be hosted at once. Individual artists and creative duos can apply. The artist can come with a partner, after having sent a prior notice. However, no children can be hosted.
technicalInfo: There are tools for painting (easels, palettes, brushes), graphics and ceramics, a hand printing press, a kiln for firing ceramics, a potter's wheel and turnettes (banding wheels). Furniture: tables, chairs. The studios have WIFI with free access 24h. There is also a projector.

name: NGO Cultural Traffic
description: Cultural Traffic is a Kharkiv based NGO dedicated to artistic and research projects. They aim to support artists and cultural actors through residency programs, and reinforce acknowledge about local culture through research and educational projects. Their main activities since 2021: exhibitions, walks, animations, research and heritage preservation projects and residency programs. Slow River House is an art residency project in the Kharkiv region, providing a space for work and relaxation, and is located in the countryside. It is a place where you can slow down far from the city, retreat and focus on your current project, do research for a new project, work on concepts and texts, find time for production and experiments with new techniques, or take a break from work and devote time to rest and recovery. The location of the residency encourages participants to explore the local natural landscape, the system of reservoirs, and take long walks through the ravines and forests. The residence is located near Kharkiv, and aims to provide a place to work primarily for cultural actors from the eastern regions of Ukraine. At the same time, representatives of other regions of Ukraine and foreign artists can also participate in the residency if their practice is related to the local culture and they understand the risks associated with being in the border regions of eastern Ukraine.
studioInfo: The house has a place to work at a desk. There is also a small workshop house on the territory for work in the summer. The organisers are happy to welcome artists who work in multimedia, with text, graphics, video, and sound. Additionally, in the summer they are open to artists who work in various techniques with materials such as clay, plaster, wood and others that require more space.
accommodationInfo: Residents are invited to live in a traditional Ukrainian house (mazanka), adapted to the needs of a modern lifestyle. The house has a kitchen-living room, a room, a shower, and a toilet. The house is surrounded by an orchard and a field, where residents can spend time.
technicalInfo: Among the equipment available to residents are: a projector, recording microphones, a tripod, a printer, scanner, and laptop. The summer workshop has a workbench with vises, and vintage tools for working with wood.

name: Cove Park
description: Cove Park is an international residency based on an outstanding 50-acre rural site in Argyll on Scotland’s west coast. Its programme of residencies, commissions, and collaborative projects respond to and promote the diversity of contemporary artistic practice. Cove Park supports artists, creative practitioners, and researchers to develop and produce ambitious, innovative, and ground-breaking new work for audiences and participants across Scotland and beyond. Cove Park’s residencies are unique in the UK. From its launch in 2000, the programme was conceived for local, national, and international artists working individually and in collaboration in all art forms, and at every career stage. Cove Park remains the only residency in the UK to bring together at any one time, and consistently throughout the year, up to 14 individuals specialising in a wide range of disciplines. This means it can offer exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary work and cultural exchange. Cove Park's Awarded Residencies are offered to local, national, and international artists following an application and selection process involving specialist advisors. The appointed residents receive fees in addition to travel, visa, materials, and access allowances when required. Its biennial general call for applications for Awarded Residencies in 2025 and 2026 is currently live and accepting applications until Friday 11 April 2025. Individual artists, collaborators, and collectives will be welcome to apply for residencies of between two weeks to three months taking place between June 2025 and December 2026. By programming over two years, Cove Park aims to offer international artists longer residencies, and to enable UK-based artists to structure their residencies over two years, making possible longer-term support around other professional or caring commitments. Please note, for 2025 and 2026 these residencies are open to individuals, collectives, and collaborative groups based in Scotland and the UK and in Central and South America. Artists from the Central and South American diaspora based in Europe and North America are also welcome to apply. Other targeted calls for applications for special Awarded Residencies are announced regularly throughout the year on its Current page: https://covepark.org/current/ Cove Park's Open Residencies provide opportunities for those with their own funding to take part in the annual programme: they welcome individuals, collaborators, and collectives – working in every creative discipline or area of research – who are able to meet the costs of a residency through, for example, the support of academic institutions, public funders, or trusts and foundations. Open Residencies can take place at any time of the year, and can be for as short a time as three nights or as long as four months. This programme is also open to cultural organisations and companies, and the facilities they provide are ideal for collaborative projects, seminars, programme development, and strategic planning. Full site bookings are available with an onsite capacity of 14 people. Prices depend upon the length of stay, the time of year, and whether you are coming on your own or with an organisation or company.
studioInfo: Two studios at 29sqm with direct access to accommodation in the Jacobs Building. Three studios at 30sqm housed in fully insulated, converted shipping containers. Workshop tools and basic equipment, including a 60-liter kiln, residents may need to bring any specialised equipment or materials that they require. Cove Park also has an upright piano.
accommodationInfo: Residents stay in private, self-catering accommodation set across Cove Park’s 50-acre site. If required, one of Cove Park’s five studios can be reserved. All residents have 24-hour access to the Jacobs Building, its communal kitchen, dining area, library, meeting and work spaces. Cove Park can accommodate groups of up to 14 individuals. Cove Park’s fully accessible Artists Centre, the Jacobs Building, was opened in 2016. Adjoining the Artists Centre are 2 new bedrooms, each with a desk, en suite wet room and kitchenette. Each bedroom has its own studio. For more details on accommodation and facilities, https://covepark.org/residencies-overview/accommodation-facilities/
technicalInfo: Workshop tools and basic equipment, including a 60-liter kiln, residents may need to bring any specialised equipment or materials that they require.

name: The Maltings (Berwick) Trust Residencies with Newcastle University
description: The Maltings (Berwick) Trust and Newcastle University’s Centre for Rural Economy (CRE) and Institute for Creative Arts Practice have an ongoing programme of artist residencies and commissions that supports the exchange and sharing of knowledge between the artist and researchers to inform critical responses to contemporary rural issues. Importantly, the programme enables new and unexpected dialogues, flows of ideas and exchanges between creative arts practitioners, individuals, communities, and researchers and students at the university.
studioInfo: Studio space is provided at The Maltings Theatre & Cinema.
accommodationInfo: Funds are offered to support accommodation costs in Berwick-upon-Tweed or the surrounding area.

name: The Fish Factory Art Space
description: The Fish Factory is a multi-function arts space consisting of 22 artist work spaces, a gallery, cafe and a multi-use event space. It brings together people of all ages and from all walks of life in a vibrant artistic community. Studio residents are local painters, illustrators, mixed media, installation artists, graduates, printers, potters, writers and more. The Fish Factory Arts offers a rolling programme of 2-4 week residencies at it's venue in a former sail loft in Penryn, Cornwall, South West England. Opened in 2011 by local artist Rose Hatcher, the Fish Factory has provided a forum for both Cornish emerging artists and international collaborators working in challenging and diverse mediums from interactive installations, murals, photo-montage, printmaking, music and film. The 'Fish' houses studios, an event space/independent gallery, a vegan cafe and a small shop selling work from resident artists. These diverse offerings have one thing in common: they flourish in the open and welcoming atmosphere the Fish Factory offers, a definite alternative to the corporate mainstream face of modern art today. They are looking for artists that want to engage with the lively and varied programme of contemporary, alternative and innovative visual arts, performance and events.
studioInfo: You are provided with a desk space in the open plan studio area, as well access to the b/w darkroom and photography studio. In addition you can take advantage of the vegan cafe (20% discount for residents), small art shop, gallery and the acoustic recording studio (by arrangement).
accommodationInfo: They can also offer you accomodation as part of your residency.

name: Stiwdio Maelor
description: Stiwdio Maelor was setablished in 2014 and provides the opportunity for all creatives to fully immerse themselves in their work. We offer residencies of between 1 week to 2 months and welcome artists, writers and musicians of all kinds to apply as individual applicants or as part of a group. Stiwdio Maelor is situated on the Afon Dulus in an ex-mining village in the Snowdonia National Park in North Wales. Stiwdio Maelor has a gallery and Dr Veronica Calarco's print studio.
studioInfo: There are three studios with attached bedrooms: The Attic space is a very large studio with four tables and chairs, a lounge area with two armchairs and fireplace. The bedroom has a double bed, 2 bedside drawers, chair and a chest of draws. It is suitable for a single or a couple Studio Pedwar has a medium size studio space with three tables and two chairs. The bedroom has a double bed and armchair. Studio Chwech has a small/medium size studio space with two tables and two chairs. The bedroom has a double bed, bedside drawer and and armchair. This room is suitable for a writer or an artist who tends to work smaller or outdoors. A studio/bedroom: Ystafell Ychnawnegol is Welsh for spare room.
